extraction_notes.note: The prepared source keeps 13 \input{chapter/...} lines after the Jensen chapter; their content is already inlined above them in blueprint.tex, so nothing further was extracted from them. Chapters are \chapter headings, so section numbers are chapter numbers.

Origin is mixed in a blueprint: Shannon-entropy, KL-divergence, Jensen, data-processing and basic Ruzsa-distance facts are marked external 'standard (uncited)'; Chapter 9 results are marked external (Jyun-Jie Liao) because the text says 'The arguments here are due to Jyun-Jie Liao', although the blueprint proves them.

theorem (external, GGMT 2024) or remark: a 'We remark that in the paper [GGMT2024] the variant estimate ... is also proven' sentence that states a cited result in full; [GGMT2024] is plain text, not a \cite.
The parenthetical refactoring remark has no closing period in the source; the node ends at the closing parenthesis.

Roadmap and formalization asides without mathematical content (e.g. the 'stretch goal' decidability note, 'We need some preliminary lemmas', 'One can then replace ... with') get no node; the restated zero-sum-triple setup in Chapter 9 is recorded as also_stated_at of the Chapter 5 definition.

nodes.statement: If $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable, then the symmetry group $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$ is the set of all $h \in G$ such that $X +h$ has the same distribution as $X$.
nodes.name: Symmetry group
nodes.statement_short: Sym[X] is the set of shifts h leaving the distribution of X invariant.
nodes.label: sym-group-def

nodes.statement: If $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable, then $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$ is a subgroup of $G$.
nodes.name: Symmetry group is a group
assumptions: $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable
nodes.label: sym-group

nodes.statement: Direct verification of the group axioms.
nodes.name: Proof of Symmetry group is a group
nodes.statement_short: Direct verification of the group axioms.

nodes.statement: If $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable such that $d[X ;X]=0$, and $x,y \in G$ are such that $P[X=x], P[X=y]>0$, then $x-y \in \mathrm{Sym}[X]$.
nodes.name: Zero Ruzsa distance implies large symmetry group
nodes.statement_short: If d[X;X]=0, differences of points in the support of X lie in Sym[X].
assumptions: $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable such that $d[X ;X]=0$, and $x,y \in G$ are such that $P[X=x], P[X=y]>0$
nodes.label: zero-large

nodes.statement: Let $X_1,X_2$ be independent copies of $X$ (from \Cref{independent-exist}). Let $A$ denote the range of $X$. From \Cref{ruz-indep} and \Cref{ruz-copy} we have $$ \bbH[X_1-X_2] = \bbH[X_1].$$ Observe from \Cref{relabeled-entropy-cond} that $$ \bbH[X_1-X_2|X_2] = \bbH[X_1|X_2] = \bbH[X_1]$$ and hence by \Cref{alternative-mutual} $$ \bbI[X_1-X_2 : X_1] = 0.$$ By \Cref{vanish-entropy}, $X_1-X_2$ and $X_1$ are therefore independent, thus the law of $(X_1-X_2|X_1=x)$ does not depend on $x \in A$. The claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Zero Ruzsa distance implies large symmetry group
nodes.statement_short: Independent copies: zero distance forces X_1-X_2 independent of X_1, so differences are symmetries.

nodes.statement: If $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable with $d[X ;X]=0$, and $x_0$ is a point with $P[X=x_0] > 0$, then $X-x_0$ is uniformly distributed on $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$.
nodes.name: Translate is uniform on symmetry group
nodes.statement_short: If d[X;X]=0, X shifted by a support point is uniform on Sym[X].
assumptions: $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable with $d[X ;X]=0$, and $x_0$ is a point with $P[X=x_0] > 0$
nodes.label: sym-zero

nodes.statement: The law of $X-x_0$ is invariant under $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$, non-zero at the origin, and supported on $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$, giving the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Translate is uniform on symmetry group
nodes.statement_short: The law of X-x_0 is Sym[X]-invariant, supported on Sym[X] and nonzero at 0, hence uniform.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable such that $d[X ;X]=0$. Then there exists a subgroup $H \leq G$ such that $d[X ;U_H] = 0$.
nodes.name: Symmetric 100\% inverse theorem
nodes.statement_short: Zero self-distance forces X to be at distance zero from a uniform subgroup variable.
assumptions: $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable such that $d[X ;X]=0$
conclusions: there exists a subgroup $H \leq G$ such that $d[X ;U_H] = 0$
nodes.label: lem:100pc-self

nodes.statement: Take $H$ to be the symmetry group of $X$, which is a group by \Cref{sym-group}. From \Cref{sym-zero}, $X-x_0$ is uniform on $H$, and $d[X ;X-x_0] = d[X ;X] \leq 0$, and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Symmetric 100\% inverse theorem
nodes.statement_short: Take H = Sym[X], uniform by the translate lemma.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $X_1,X_2$ are $G$-valued random variables such that $d[X_1;X_2]=0$. Then there exists a subgroup $H \leq G$ such that $d[X_1;U_H] = d[X_2;U_H] = 0$.
nodes.name: General 100\% inverse theorem
nodes.statement_short: Zero Ruzsa distance between X_1,X_2 forces both to be at distance zero from some U_H.
assumptions: $X_1,X_2$ are $G$-valued random variables such that $d[X_1;X_2]=0$
conclusions: there exists a subgroup $H \leq G$ such that $d[X_1;U_H] = d[X_2;U_H] = 0$
nodes.label: lem:100pc

nodes.statement: Using \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} and \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg} we have $d[X_1;X_1]=0$, hence by \Cref{lem:100pc-self} $d[X_1;U_H]=0$ for some subgroup $H$. By \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} and \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg} again we also have $d[X_2;U_H]$ as required.
nodes.name: Proof of General 100\% inverse theorem
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality and nonnegativity reduce to the symmetric case.

nodes.statement: If $G$ is a finite additive group and $A$ is a subset of $G$, the \emph{additive energy} $E(A)$ of $A$ is the normalized count $$ E(A) := \frac{|\{(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4) \in A^4 : a_1+a_2 = a_3+a_4\}|}{|G|^3}. $$ The normalization by $|G|^3$ is the convention of \texttt{Finset.addEnergy'}, and every statement in this chapter that mentions $E(A)$ uses it.
nodes.name: Additive energy
nodes.statement_short: Additive energy E(A): normalized count of additive quadruples in A.
nodes.label: energy-def

nodes.statement: If $G$ is a finite additive group and $A,B$ are subsets of $G$, then $$ \left( \frac{|\{ (a,a') \in A \times A: a+a' \in B \}|}{|G|^2} \right)^2 \leq \frac{|B|}{|G|}\, E(A). $$ The left-hand side is the square of the density of a subset of $G \times G$, and the right-hand side involves the density of a subset of $G$.
nodes.name: Cauchy--Schwarz bound
nodes.statement_short: Squared density of pairs summing into B is at most density of B times E(A).
assumptions: $G$ is a finite additive group and $A,B$ are subsets of $G$
conclusions: $$ \left( \frac{|\{ (a,a') \in A \times A: a+a' \in B \}|}{|G|^2} \right)^2 \leq \frac{|B|}{|G|}\, E(A). $$ The left-hand side is the square of the density of a subset of $G \times G$, and the right-hand side involves the density of a subset of $G$
nodes.label: cs-bound

nodes.statement: If $B$ is empty then the claim is trivial (with the Lean convention $0/0$), so without loss of generality $B$ is non-empty. We can rewrite $$ |\{ (a,a') \in A \times A: a+a' \in B \}| = \sum_{b \in B} r(b)$$ where $r: G \to \N$ is the counting function $$ r(b) := |\{ (a,a') \in A \times A: a+a' = b \}|.$$ From double counting we have $$ \sum_{b \in G} r(b)^2 = |G|^3 E(A).$$ The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality then gives $$ \Bigl( \sum_{b \in B} r(b) \Bigr)^2 \leq |B| \sum_{b \in B} r(b)^2 \leq |B| \sum_{b \in G} r(b)^2 = |B|\, |G|^3 E(A),$$ and the claim follows on dividing both sides by $|G|^4$.
nodes.name: Proof of Cauchy--Schwarz bound
nodes.statement_short: Write the pair count as a sum of representation counts and apply Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $A$ be a non-empty subset of $G$ with $E(A) \geq \frac{1}{K} \left( \frac{|A|}{|G|} \right)^3$ for some $K \geq 1$. Then there is a subset $A'$ of $A$ with $|A'| \geq |A| / (C_1 K^{C_2})$ and $|A'-A'| \leq C_3 K^{C_4} |A|$, where $$C_1 = 2^4, C_2 = 1, C_3 = 2^{10}, C_4 = 5.$$ The Lean statement gives the two conclusions as inequalities between densities; these are equivalent to the ones above, the common factor $|G|$ cancelling.
nodes.name: Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers lemma
nodes.statement_short: Large additive energy gives a large subset A' with small difference set.
assumptions: $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $A$ be a non-empty subset of $G$ with $E(A) \geq \frac{1}{K} \left( \frac{|A|}{|G|} \right)^3$ for some $K \geq 1$
conclusions: there is a subset $A'$ of $A$ with $|A'| \geq |A| / (C_1 K^{C_2})$ and $|A'-A'| \leq C_3 K^{C_4} |A|$, where $$C_1 = 2^4, C_2 = 1, C_3 = 2^{10}, C_4 = 5.$$ The Lean statement gives the two conclusions as inequalities between densities; these are equivalent to the ones above, the common factor $|G|$ cancelling
nodes.label: bsg

nodes.statement: See \url{https://terrytao.files.wordpress.com/2024/01/simplebsg.pdf}.
nodes.name: Proof of Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers lemma
nodes.statement_short: Reference to Tao's note on a simple BSG proof.

nodes.statement: Let $G,G'$ be finite abelian $2$-groups. Let $f: G \to G'$ be a function, and suppose that there are at least $|G|^2 / K$ pairs $(x,y) \in G^2$ such that $$ f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y).$$ Then there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ and a constant $c \in G'$ such that $f(x) = \phi(x)+c$ for at least $|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122})$ values of $x \in G$.
nodes.name: Approximate homomorphism form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: A function on finite 2-groups that is often additive agrees with an affine map on a polynomial fraction of G.
conclusions: Let $G,G'$ be finite abelian $2$-groups. Let $f: G \to G'$ be a function, and suppose that there are at least $|G|^2 / K$ pairs $(x,y) \in G^2$ such that $$ f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y).$$ Then there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ and a constant $c \in G'$ such that $f(x) = \phi(x)+c$ for at least $|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122})$ values of $x \in G$
nodes.label: approx-hom-pfr

nodes.statement: Consider the graph $A \subset G \times G'$ defined by $$ A := \{ (x,f(x)): x \in G \}.$$ Clearly, $|A| = |G|$. By hypothesis, we have $a+a' \in A$ for at least $|A|^2/K$ pairs $(a,a') \in A^2$. By \Cref{cs-bound}, this implies that $E(A) \geq \frac{1}{K^2} \left( \frac{|A|}{|G \times G'|} \right)^3$. Applying \Cref{bsg}, we conclude that there exists a subset $A' \subset A$ with $|A'| \geq |A|/C_1 K^{2C_2}$ and $|A'+A'| \leq C_1C_3 K^{2(C_2+C_4)} |A'|$. Applying \Cref{pfr-9-aux'}, we may find a subspace $H \subset G \times G'$ such that $|H| / |A'| \in [L^{-8}, L^{8}]$ and a subset $c$ of cardinality at most $L^5 |A'|^{1/2} / |H|^{1/2}$ such that $A' \subseteq c + H$, where $L = C_1C_3 K^{2(C_2+C_4)}$. If we let $H_0,H_1$ be as in \Cref{goursat}, this implies on taking projections the projection of $A'$ to $G$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H_0$. This implies that $$ |c| |H_0| \geq |A'|;$$ since $|H_0| |H_1| = |H|$, we conclude that $$ |H_1| \leq |c| |H|/|A'|.$$ By hypothesis, $A'$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H$, and hence by at most $|c| |H_1|$ translates of $\{ (x,\phi(x)): x \in G \}$. As $\phi$ is a homomorphism, each such translate can be written in the form $\{ (x,\phi(x)+c): x \in G \}$ for some $c \in G'$. The number of translates is bounded by $$ |c|^2 \frac{|H|}{|A'|} \leq \left(L^5 \frac{|A'|^{1/2}}{|H|^{1/2}}\right)^2 \frac{|H|}{|A'|} = L^{10}. $$ By the pigeonhole principle, one of these translates must then contain at least $|A'|/L^{10} \geq |G| / (C_1C_3 K^{2(C_2+C_4)})^{10} (C_1 K^{2C_2})$ elements of $A'$ (and hence of $A$), and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Approximate homomorphism form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Apply BSG and PFR to the graph of f, then Goursat and pigeonhole to find an affine map. The key step projects the PFR covering via Goursat's decomposition.

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian $2$-group. Then the finite abelian $2$-group $\mathrm{Hom}(G,\Z/2\Z)$ of homomorphisms from $G$ to $\Z/2\Z$ has the same order as $G$.
nodes.name: Duality
assumptions: $G$ be a finite abelian $2$-group
conclusions: the finite abelian $2$-group $\mathrm{Hom}(G,\Z/2\Z)$ of homomorphisms from $G$ to $\Z/2\Z$ has the same order as $G$
nodes.label: gdual

nodes.statement: By the classification of finite abelian groups, $G$ is isomorphic to $(\Z/2\Z)^n$. Then $\mathrm{Hom}(G,\Z/2\Z)$ is isomorphic to $(\Z/2\Z)^n$ as well, and hence has the same order.
nodes.name: Proof of Duality
nodes.statement_short: Classification: G is (Z/2Z)^n, so is its dual.

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian $2$-group, and let $x \in G$ be non-zero. Then there are $|G|/2$ homomorphisms $\phi: G \to \Z/2\Z$ such that $\phi(x) = 1$.
nodes.name: Counting
assumptions: $G$ be a finite abelian $2$-group, and let $x \in G$ be non-zero
conclusions: there are $|G|/2$ homomorphisms $\phi: G \to \Z/2\Z$ such that $\phi(x) = 1$
nodes.label: gcount

nodes.statement: The map $\phi \mapsto \phi(x)$ is a homomorphism from $\mathrm{Hom}(G,\Z/2\Z)$ to $\Z/2\Z$, and by Lemma \ref{gdual} the kernel has order equal to the order of $G / \{0,x\}$, which is $|G|/2$. Then the preimage of $1$ must also be of order $|G|/2$.
nodes.name: Proof of Counting
nodes.statement_short: Evaluation at x is a homomorphism whose kernel has order |G|/2.

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian $2$-group, and let $A$ be a subset of $G$. Then there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to \Z/2\Z$ such that $|A \cap \phi^{-1}(1)| \geq (|A|-1)/2$.
nodes.name: Slicing
assumptions: $G$ be a finite abelian $2$-group, and let $A$ be a subset of $G$
conclusions: there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to \Z/2\Z$ such that $|A \cap \phi^{-1}(1)| \geq (|A|-1)/2$
nodes.label: gslice

nodes.statement: We have $$ \sum_{\phi \in \mathrm{Hom}(G,\Z/2\Z)} |A \cap \phi^{-1}(1)| = \sum_{x \in A} |\{ \phi \in \mathrm{Hom}(G,\Z/2\Z): \phi(x) = 1 \}|$$ $$ \geq (|A|-1) |G|/2$$ thanks to Lemma \ref{gcount}. The claim now follows from Lemma \ref{gdual} and the pigeonhole principle.
nodes.name: Proof of Slicing
nodes.statement_short: Double counting over homomorphisms plus pigeonhole.

nodes.statement: Let $G,G'$ be finite abelian $2$-groups. Let $f: G \to G'$ be a function, and suppose that there are at least $|G|^2 / K$ pairs $(x,y) \in G^2$ such that $$ f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y).$$ Then there exists a homomorphism $\phi'': G \to G'$ such that $f(x) = \phi''(x)$ for at least $(|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122}) - 1)/2$ values of $x \in G$.
nodes.name: Approximate homomorphism form of PFR, no constant term
nodes.statement_short: Same as approximate-homomorphism PFR but with a genuine homomorphism, losing a factor 2.
conclusions: Let $G,G'$ be finite abelian $2$-groups. Let $f: G \to G'$ be a function, and suppose that there are at least $|G|^2 / K$ pairs $(x,y) \in G^2$ such that $$ f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y).$$ Then there exists a homomorphism $\phi'': G \to G'$ such that $f(x) = \phi''(x)$ for at least $(|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122}) - 1)/2$ values of $x \in G$
nodes.label: approx-hom-pfr-no-const

nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{approx-hom-pfr}, there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ and a constant $c \in G'$ such that the set $A := \{ x \in G: f(x) = \phi(x) + c\}$ has cardinality at least $|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122})$. By Lemma \ref{gslice}, there exists a homomorphism $\phi': G \to \Z/2\Z$ such that $$ |A \cap \phi'^{-1}(1)| \geq (|A|-1)/2 \geq (|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122}) - 1)/2.$$ Then the claim follows by taking $\phi'' = \phi + \phi' \bullet c$ (where we view $G'$ as a $\Z/2\Z$-module).
nodes.name: Proof of Approximate homomorphism form of PFR, no constant term
nodes.statement_short: Apply the approximate homomorphism theorem, then slice to absorb the constant.

nodes.statement: In this section $G$ will be a finite additive group.
nodes.name: Finite additive group $G$

nodes.statement: If $X$ is $G$-valued, then $\bbH[-X]=\bbH[X]$.
nodes.name: Negation preserves entropy
assumptions: $X$ is $G$-valued
nodes.label: neg-ent

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{relabeled-entropy}.
nodes.name: Proof of Negation preserves entropy
nodes.statement_short: Relabeling by negation.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are $G$-valued, then $\bbH[X \pm Y | Y]=\bbH[X|Y]$ and $\bbH[X \pm Y, Y] = \bbH[X, Y]$.
nodes.name: Shearing preserves entropy
assumptions: $X,Y$ are $G$-valued
conclusions: $\bbH[X \pm Y | Y]=\bbH[X|Y]$ and $\bbH[X \pm Y, Y] = \bbH[X, Y]$
nodes.label: shear-ent

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{relabeled-entropy-cond} and \Cref{chain-rule}.
nodes.name: Proof of Shearing preserves entropy
nodes.statement_short: Relabeling under conditioning plus chain rule.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$, we have $$ \max(\bbH[X], \bbH[Y]) - \bbI[X:Y] \leq \bbH[X \pm Y].$$
nodes.name: Lower bound of sumset
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of X±Y is at least max(H[X],H[Y]) minus their mutual information.
assumptions: $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$
nodes.label: sumset-lower-gen

nodes.statement: By \Cref{cond-reduce}, \ref{shear-ent}, \ref{alternative-mutual}, \ref{neg-ent} we have $$ \bbH[X\pm Y] \geq \bbH[X\pm Y|Y] = \bbH[X|Y]= \bbH[X] - \bbI[X:Y] $$ and similarly with the roles of $X,Y$ reversed, giving the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Lower bound of sumset
nodes.statement_short: Conditioning reduces entropy, shearing, and the mutual information formula.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$ and $Z$ is another random variable on $\Omega$ then \[ \max(\bbH[X|Z], \bbH[Y|Z]) - \bbI[X:Y|Z] \leq \bbH[X\pm Y|Z], \]
nodes.name: Conditional lower bound on sumset
assumptions: $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$ and $Z$ is another random variable on $\Omega$
nodes.label: sumset-lower-gen-cond

nodes.statement: This follows from \Cref{sumset-lower-gen} by conditioning to $Z = z$ and summing over $z$ (weighted by $\bbP[Z=z]$).
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional lower bound on sumset
nodes.statement_short: Average the unconditional bound over values of Z.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are independent $G$-valued random variables, then $$\max(\bbH[X], \bbH[Y]) \leq \bbH[X\pm Y]. $$
nodes.name: Independent lower bound on sumset
assumptions: $X,Y$ are independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: sumset-lower

nodes.statement: Combine \Cref{sumset-lower-gen} with \Cref{vanish-entropy}.
nodes.name: Proof of Independent lower bound on sumset
nodes.statement_short: Combine the general lower bound with vanishing mutual information.

nodes.statement: One random variable is said to be a copy of another if they have the same distribution.
nodes.name: Copy of a random variable

nodes.statement: If $X'$ is a copy of $X$ then $\bbH[X'] = \bbH[X]$.
nodes.name: Copy preserves entropy
assumptions: $X'$ is a copy of $X$
nodes.label: copy-ent

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{entropy-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Copy preserves entropy
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definition of entropy.

nodes.statement: Let $X_i : \Omega_i \to S_i$ be random variables for $i=1,\dots,k$. Then if one gives $\prod_{i=1}^k S_i$ the product measure of the laws of $X_i$, the coordinate functions $(x_j)_{j=1}^k \mapsto x_i$ are jointly independent random variables which are copies of the $X_1,\dots,X_k$.
nodes.name: Existence of independent copies
assumptions: $X_i : \Omega_i \to S_i$ be random variables for $i=1,\dots,k$
conclusions: if one gives $\prod_{i=1}^k S_i$ the product measure of the laws of $X_i$, the coordinate functions $(x_j)_{j=1}^k \mapsto x_i$ are jointly independent random variables which are copies of the $X_1,\dots,X_k$
nodes.label: independent-exist

nodes.statement: Explicit computation.
nodes.name: Proof of Existence of independent copies
nodes.statement_short: Product measure construction.

nodes.statement: Let $X,Y$ be $G$-valued random variables (not necessarily on the same sample space). The \emph{Ruzsa distance} $d[X ;Y]$ between $X$ and $Y$ is defined to be $$ d[X ;Y] := \bbH[X' - Y'] - \bbH[X']/2 - \bbH[Y']/2$$ where $X',Y'$ are (the canonical) independent copies of $X,Y$ from \Cref{independent-exist}.
nodes.name: Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement_short: Entropic Ruzsa distance d[X;Y] = H[X'-Y'] - H[X']/2 - H[Y']/2 for independent copies.
nodes.label: ruz-dist-def

nodes.statement: If $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable and $0$ is the random variable taking the value $0$ everywhere then \[d[X;0]=\mathbb{H}(X)/2.\]
nodes.name: Distance from zero
assumptions: $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable and $0$ is the random variable taking the value $0$ everywhere
nodes.label: dist-zero

nodes.statement: This is an immediate consequence of the definitions and $X-0\equiv X$ and $\mathbb{H}(0)=0$.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance from zero
nodes.statement_short: Unfold definitions with X-0=X and H(0)=0.

nodes.statement: If $X',Y'$ are copies of $X,Y$ respectively then $d[X';Y']=d[X ;Y]$.
nodes.name: Copy preserves Ruzsa distance
assumptions: $X',Y'$ are copies of $X,Y$ respectively
nodes.label: ruz-copy

nodes.statement: Immediate from Definitions \ref{ruz-dist-def} and \Cref{copy-ent}.
nodes.name: Proof of Copy preserves Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement_short: Definition of Ruzsa distance and copy invariance of entropy.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are independent $G$-random variables then $$ d[X ;Y] := \bbH[X - Y] - \bbH[X]/2 - \bbH[Y]/2.$$
nodes.name: Ruzsa distance in independent case
assumptions: $X,Y$ are independent $G$-random variables
nodes.label: ruz-indep

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{ruz-dist-def} and Lemmas \ref{relabeled-entropy}, \ref{copy-ent}.
nodes.name: Proof of Ruzsa distance in independent case
nodes.statement_short: Definition of Ruzsa distance plus relabeling and copies.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables, then $$ d[X ;Y] = d[Y;X].$$
nodes.name: Distance symmetric
assumptions: $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: ruzsa-symm

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{neg-ent} and \Cref{ruz-dist-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance symmetric
nodes.statement_short: Negation preserves entropy.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables, then $$|\bbH[X]-H[Y]| \leq 2 d[X ;Y].$$
nodes.name: Distance controls entropy difference
assumptions: $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: ruzsa-diff

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{sumset-lower} and \Cref{ruz-dist-def}, and also \Cref{neg-ent}.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance controls entropy difference
nodes.statement_short: Independent sumset lower bound applied to the definition.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are independent $G$-valued random variables, then $$ \bbH[X-Y] - \bbH[X], \bbH[X-Y] - \bbH[Y] \leq 2d[X ;Y].$$
nodes.name: Distance controls entropy growth
assumptions: $X,Y$ are independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: ruzsa-growth

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{sumset-lower} and \Cref{ruz-dist-def}, and also \Cref{neg-ent}.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance controls entropy growth
nodes.statement_short: Independent sumset lower bound applied to the definition.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables, then $$ d[X ;Y] \geq 0.$$
nodes.name: Distance nonnegative
assumptions: $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: ruzsa-nonneg

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{ruzsa-diff}.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance nonnegative
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the entropy difference bound.

nodes.statement: If $G$ is an additive group and $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable and $H\leq G$ is a finite subgroup then, with $\pi:G\to G/H$ the natural homomorphism we have (where $U_H$ is uniform on $H$) \[\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))\leq 2d[X;U_H].\]
nodes.name: Projection entropy and distance
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of the projection of X to G/H is at most twice d[X;U_H].
conclusions: If $G$ is an additive group and $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable and $H\leq G$ is a finite subgroup then, with $\pi:G\to G/H$ the natural homomorphism we have (where $U_H$ is uniform on $H$) \[\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))\leq 2d[X;U_H].\]
nodes.label: dist-projection

nodes.statement: WLOG, we make $X$, $U_H$ independent (\Cref{independent-exist}). Now by Lemmas \ref{submodularity}, \ref{shear-ent}, \ref{jensen-bound} \begin{align*} &\mathbb{H}(X-U_H|\pi(X)) \geq \mathbb{H}(X-U_H|X) &= \mathbb{H}(U_H) \\ &\mathbb{H}(X-U_H|\pi(X)) \leq \log |H| &= \mathbb{H}(U_H) \end{align*} By \Cref{chain-rule} \[\mathbb{H}(X-U_H)=\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))+\mathbb{H}(X-U_H|\pi(X))=\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))+\mathbb{H}(U_H)\] and therefore \[d[X;U_H]=\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))+\frac{\mathbb{H}(U_H)-\mathbb{H}(X)}{2}.\] Furthermore by \Cref{ruzsa-diff} \[d[X;U_H]\geq \frac{\lvert \mathbb{H}(X)-\mathbb{H}(U_H)\rvert}{2}.\] Adding these inequalities gives the result.
nodes.name: Proof of Projection entropy and distance
nodes.statement_short: Bound H(X-U_H|pi(X)) from both sides, use the chain rule, then add the entropy difference bound.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y,Z$ are $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$ with $(X,Y)$ independent of $Z$, then \begin{equation} \bbH[X - Y] \leq \bbH[X-Z] + \bbH[Z-Y] - \bbH[Z]\end{equation}
nodes.name: Improved Ruzsa triangle inequality
nodes.statement_short: Entropic submodular triangle bound H[X-Y] <= H[X-Z]+H[Z-Y]-H[Z] when Z is independent of (X,Y).
assumptions: $X,Y,Z$ are $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$ with $(X,Y)$ independent of $Z$
nodes.label: ruzsa-triangle-improved

nodes.statement: \bbH[X - Y] \leq \bbH[X-Z] + \bbH[Z-Y] - \bbH[Z]
nodes.name: Equation (3.1)
nodes.label: submod-explicit

nodes.statement: This is an improvement over the usual Ruzsa triangle inequality because $X,Y$ are not assumed to be independent. However we will not utilize this improvement here.
nodes.name: Remark on the improved Ruzsa triangle inequality

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{alt-submodularity} to obtain \[\bbH[X - Z, X - Y] + \bbH[Y, X - Y] \geq \bbH[X - Z, Y, X - Y] + \bbH[X - Y].\] Using \[\bbH[X - Z, X - Y] \leq \bbH[X - Z] + \bbH[Y - Z]\] (from \Cref{relabeled-entropy}, \Cref{subadditive}), \[\bbH[Y, X - Y] = \bbH[X, Y] \] (from \Cref{relabeled-entropy}), and \[\bbH[X - Z, Y, X - Y] = \bbH[X, Y, Z] = \bbH[X, Y] + \bbH[Z]\] (from \Cref{relabeled-entropy} and \Cref{add-entropy}) and rearranging, we indeed obtain~\eqref{submod-explicit}.
nodes.name: Proof of Improved Ruzsa triangle inequality
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity applied to (X-Z, Y, X-Y), then relabeling and independence.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y,Z$ are $G$-valued random variables, then $$ d[X ;Y] \leq d[X ;Z] + d[Z;Y].$$
nodes.name: Ruzsa triangle inequality
assumptions: $X,Y,Z$ are $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: ruzsa-triangle

nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruz-copy} and Lemmas \ref{independent-exist}, \ref{ruz-indep}, it suffices to prove this inequality assuming that $X,Y,Z$ are defined on the same space and are independent. But then the claim follows from \Cref{ruzsa-triangle-improved} and \Cref{ruz-dist-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Ruzsa triangle inequality
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to independent variables and apply the improved triangle inequality.

nodes.statement: If $(X, Z)$ and $(Y, W)$ are random variables (where $X$ and $Y$ are $G$-valued) we define $$ d[X | Z; Y | W] := \sum_{z,w} \bbP[Z=z] \bbP[W=w] d[(X|Z=z); (Y|(W=w))].$$ similarly $$ d[X ; Y | W] := \sum_{w} \bbP[W=w] d[X ; (Y|(W=w))].$$
nodes.name: Conditioned Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement_short: Conditioned Ruzsa distance as the average of distances of conditioned variables.
nodes.label: cond-dist-def

nodes.statement: The expression $d[X | Z;Y | W]$ is unchanged if $(X,Z)$ or $(Y,W)$ is replaced by a copy. Furthermore, if $(X,Z)$ and $(Y,W)$ are independent, then $$ d[X | Z;Y | W] = \bbH[X-Y|Z,W] - \bbH[X|Z]/2 - \bbH[Y|W]/2$$ and similarly $$ d[X ;Y | W] = \bbH[X-Y|W] - \bbH[X]/2 - \bbH[Y|W]/2.$$
nodes.name: Alternate form of distance
nodes.statement_short: Conditioned Ruzsa distance is copy-invariant and equals an entropy expression for independent pairs.
conclusions: The expression $d[X | Z;Y | W]$ is unchanged if $(X,Z)$ or $(Y,W)$ is replaced by a copy. Furthermore, if $(X,Z)$ and $(Y,W)$ are independent, then $$ d[X | Z;Y | W] = \bbH[X-Y|Z,W] - \bbH[X|Z]/2 - \bbH[Y|W]/2$$ and similarly $$ d[X ;Y | W] = \bbH[X-Y|W] - \bbH[X]/2 - \bbH[Y|W]/2.$$
nodes.label: cond-dist-alt

nodes.statement: Straightforward thanks to \Cref{copy-ent}, \Cref{ruz-copy}, \Cref{ruz-indep}, \Cref{cond-dist-def}, \Cref{conditional-entropy-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Alternate form of distance
nodes.statement_short: Straightforward from the definitions and copy invariance.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $X, Y, Z$ are independent $G$-valued random variables. Then \[ \bbH[X + Y + Z] - \bbH[X + Y] \leq \bbH[Y+ Z] - \bbH[Y]. \]
nodes.name: Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman inequality
nodes.statement_short: H[X+Y+Z]-H[X+Y] <= H[Y+Z]-H[Y] for independent X,Y,Z.
assumptions: $X, Y, Z$ are independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: kv

nodes.statement: From \Cref{submodularity} we have $$ \bbH[X, X + Y+ Z] + \bbH[Z, X + Y+ Z] \geq \bbH[X, Z, X + Y+ Z] + \bbH[X + Y+ Z].$$ However, using Lemmas \ref{add-entropy}, \ref{relabeled-entropy} repeatedly we have $\bbH[X, X + Y+ Z] = \bbH[X, Y+ Z] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y+ Z]$, $\bbH[Z, X + Y + Z] = \bbH[Z, X + Y] = \bbH[Z] + \bbH[X + Y]$ and $\bbH[X, Z, X + Y+ Z] = \bbH[X, Y, Z] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y] + \bbH[Z]$. The claim then follows from a calculation.
nodes.name: Proof of Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman inequality
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity for (X, Z, X+Y+Z), then independence and relabeling.

nodes.statement: For $X,Y$ random variables, there exist random variables $X_1,X_2,Y'$ on a common probability space with $(X_1, Y'), (X_2, Y')$ both having the distribution of $(X,Y)$, and $X_1, X_2$ conditionally independent over $Y'$ in the sense of \Cref{conditional-independent-def}.
nodes.name: Existence of conditional independent trials
conclusions: For $X,Y$ random variables, there exist random variables $X_1,X_2,Y'$ on a common probability space with $(X_1, Y'), (X_2, Y')$ both having the distribution of $(X,Y)$, and $X_1, X_2$ conditionally independent over $Y'$ in the sense of \Cref{conditional-independent-def}
nodes.label: cond-indep-exist

nodes.statement: Explicit construction.
nodes.name: Proof of Existence of conditional independent trials
nodes.statement_short: Explicit construction.

nodes.statement: Let $A,B$ be $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$, and set $Z := A+B$. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{z} \bbP[Z=z] d[(A | Z = z); (B | Z = z)] \leq 3 \bbI[A:B] + 2 \bbH[Z] - \bbH[A] - \bbH[B]. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Balog-Szemer\'edi-Gowers
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG: average distance of A,B conditioned on A+B is bounded by mutual information and entropies.
assumptions: $A,B$ be $G$-valued random variables on $\Omega$, and set $Z := A+B$
nodes.label: entropic-bsg

nodes.statement: \sum_{z} \bbP[Z=z] d[(A | Z = z); (B | Z = z)] \leq 3 \bbI[A:B] + 2 \bbH[Z] - \bbH[A] - \bbH[B].
nodes.name: Equation (3.2)
nodes.label: 2-bsg-takeaway

nodes.statement: Let $(A_1, B_1)$ and $(A_2, B_2)$ (and $Z'$, which by abuse of notation we call $Z$) be conditionally independent trials of $(A,B)$ relative to $Z$ as produced by \Cref{cond-indep-exist}, thus $(A_1,B_1)$ and $(A_2,B_2)$ are coupled through the random variable $A_1 + B_1 = A_2 + B_2$, which by abuse of notation we shall also call $Z$. Observe from \Cref{ruz-indep} that the left-hand side of~\eqref{2-bsg-takeaway} is \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2| Z] - \bbH[A_1 | Z]/2 - \bbH[B_2 | Z]/2. \end{equation} since, crucially, $(A_1 | Z=z)$ and $(B_2 | Z=z)$ are independent for all $z$. Applying submodularity (\Cref{alt-submodularity}) gives \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\bbH[A_1 - B_2] + \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1] \\ &\qquad \leq \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1] + \bbH[A_1 - B_2,B_1]. \end{split}\end{equation} We estimate the second, third and fourth terms appearing here. First note that, by \Cref{cond-trial-ent} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy} (noting that the tuple $(A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1)$ determines the tuple $(A_1, A_2, B_1, B_2)$ since $A_1+B_1=A_2+B_2$) \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1] = \bbH[A_1, B_1, A_2, B_2,Z] = 2\bbH[A,B] - \bbH[Z].\end{equation} Next observe that \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1] = \bbH[A_1, B_2] \leq \bbH[A] + \bbH[B]. \end{equation} Finally, we have \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2, B_1] = \bbH[A_2 - B_1, B_1] = \bbH[A_2, B_1] \leq \bbH[A] + \bbH[B].\end{equation} Substituting~\eqref{bsg-24},~\eqref{bsg-23} and~\eqref{bsg-25} into~\eqref{bsg-31} yields \[\bbH[A_1 - B_2] \leq 2 \bbI[A:B] + \bbH[Z]\] and so by \Cref{cond-reduce} \[\bbH[A_1 - B_2 | Z] \leq 2 \bbI[A:B] + \bbH[Z].\] Since \begin{align*} \bbH[A_1 | Z] & = \bbH[A_1, A_1 + B_1] - \bbH[Z] \\ & = \bbH[A,B] - \bbH[Z] \\ & = \bbH[Z] - \bbI[A:B] - 2 \bbH[Z]- \bbH[A]-\bbH[B]\end{align*} and similarly for $\bbH[B_2 | Z]$, we see that~\eqref{lhs-to-bound} is bounded by $3 \bbI[A:B] + 2\bbH[Z]-\bbH[A]-\bbH[B]$ as claimed.
nodes.name: Proof of Balog-Szemer\'edi-Gowers
nodes.statement_short: Conditionally independent trials over Z, submodularity, and estimating three entropy terms. The key step bounds H[A_1-B_2|Z] by 2I[A:B]+H[Z].

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\bbH[A_1 - B_2] + \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1] \\ &\qquad \leq \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1] + \bbH[A_1 - B_2,B_1]. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (3.4)
nodes.label: bsg-31

nodes.statement: \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1] = \bbH[A_1, B_2] \leq \bbH[A] + \bbH[B].
nodes.name: Equation (3.6)
nodes.label: bsg-23

nodes.statement: \bbH[A_1 - B_2, B_1] = \bbH[A_2 - B_1, B_1] = \bbH[A_2, B_1] \leq \bbH[A] + \bbH[B].
nodes.name: Equation (3.7)
nodes.label: bsg-25

nodes.statement: Suppose that $(X, Z)$ and $(Y, W)$ are random variables, where $X, Y$ take values in an abelian group. Then \[ d[X | Z;Y | W] \leq d[X ; Y] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[X : Z] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[Y : W].\] In particular, \[ d[X ;Y | W] \leq d[X ; Y] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[Y : W].\]
nodes.name: Upper bound on conditioned Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement_short: Conditioning raises Ruzsa distance by at most half the mutual informations.
assumptions: $(X, Z)$ and $(Y, W)$ are random variables, where $X, Y$ take values in an abelian group
conclusions: \[ d[X | Z;Y | W] \leq d[X ; Y] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[X : Z] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[Y : W].\] In particular, \[ d[X ;Y | W] \leq d[X ; Y] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[Y : W].\]
nodes.label: cond-dist-fact

nodes.statement: Using \Cref{cond-dist-alt} and \Cref{independent-exist}, if $(X',Z'), (Y',W')$ are independent copies of the variables $(X,Z)$, $(Y,W)$, we have \begin{align*} d[X | Z; Y | W]&= \bbH[X'-Y'|Z',W'] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X'|Z'] - \tfrac{1}{2}H[Y'|W'] \\ &\le \bbH[X'-Y']- \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X'|Z'] - \tfrac{1}{2}H[Y'|W'] \\ &= d[X';Y'] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[X' : Z'] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[Y' : W']. \end{align*} Here, in the middle step we used \Cref{cond-reduce}, and in the last step we used \Cref{ruz-dist-def} and \Cref{information-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Upper bound on conditioned Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement_short: Independent copies, then conditioning reduces entropy.

nodes.statement: Let $X, Y, Z$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group of characteristic $2$, and with $Y, Z$ independent. Then we have \begin{align}\nonumber d[X ; Y + Z] -d[X ; Y] & \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[Y+ Z] - \bbH[Y]) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} d[Y; Z] + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Z] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Y]. \end{align} and \begin{align}\nonumber d[X ;Y|Y+ Z] - d[X ;Y] & \leq \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\bbH[Y+ Z] - \bbH[Z]\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} d[Y;Z] + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Y] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Z]. \end{align}
nodes.name: Comparison of Ruzsa distances, I
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on how much d[X;Y+Z] and d[X;Y|Y+Z] exceed d[X;Y], in characteristic 2.
assumptions: $X, Y, Z$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group of characteristic $2$, and with $Y, Z$ independent
conclusions: \begin{align}\nonumber d[X ; Y + Z] -d[X ; Y] & \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[Y+ Z] - \bbH[Y]) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} d[Y; Z] + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Z] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Y]. \end{align} and \begin{align}\nonumber d[X ;Y|Y+ Z] - d[X ;Y] & \leq \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\bbH[Y+ Z] - \bbH[Z]\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} d[Y;Z] + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Y] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Z]. \end{align}
nodes.label: first-useful

nodes.statement: \nonumber d[X ; Y + Z] -d[X ; Y] & \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[Y+ Z] - \bbH[Y]) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} d[Y; Z] + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Z] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Y].
nodes.name: Equation (3.8)
nodes.label: lem51-a

nodes.statement: \nonumber d[X ;Y|Y+ Z] - d[X ;Y] & \leq \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\bbH[Y+ Z] - \bbH[Z]\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} d[Y;Z] + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Y] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[Z].
nodes.name: Equation (3.9)
nodes.label: ruzsa-3

nodes.statement: We first prove~\eqref{lem51-a}. We may assume (taking an independent copy, using \Cref{independent-exist} and \Cref{ruz-copy}, \ref{ruz-indep}) that $X$ is independent of $Y, Z$. Then we have \begin{align*} d[X ;Y+ Z] & - d[X ;Y] \\ & = \bbH[X + Y + Z] - \bbH[X + Y] - \tfrac{1}{2}\bbH[Y + Z] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Y].\end{align*} Combining this with \Cref{kv} gives the required bound. The second form of the result is immediate \Cref{ruz-indep}. Turning to~\eqref{ruzsa-3}, we have from \Cref{information-def} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy} \begin{align*} \bbI[Y : Y+ Z] & = \bbH[Y] + \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Y, Y + Z] \\ & = \bbH[Y] + \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Y, Z] = \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Z],\end{align*} and so~\eqref{ruzsa-3} is a consequence of \Cref{cond-dist-fact}. Once again the second form of the result is immediate from \Cref{ruz-indep}.
nodes.name: Proof of Comparison of Ruzsa distances, I
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to independence, apply Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman; second part via the conditional distance bound.

nodes.statement: Let $X, Y, Z, Z'$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z, Z'$ independent. Then we have \begin{align}\nonumber & d[X ;Y + Z | Y + Z + Z'] - d[X ;Y] \\ & \qquad \leq \tfrac{1}{2} ( \bbH[Y + Z + Z'] + \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Y] - \bbH[Z']). \end{align}
nodes.name: Comparison of Ruzsa distances, II
nodes.statement_short: Bound on d[X;Y+Z|Y+Z+Z'] - d[X;Y] by entropies.
assumptions: $X, Y, Z, Z'$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z, Z'$ independent
conclusions: \begin{align}\nonumber & d[X ;Y + Z | Y + Z + Z'] - d[X ;Y] \\ & \qquad \leq \tfrac{1}{2} ( \bbH[Y + Z + Z'] + \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Y] - \bbH[Z']). \end{align}
nodes.label: second-useful

nodes.statement: \nonumber & d[X ;Y + Z | Y + Z + Z'] - d[X ;Y] \\ & \qquad \leq \tfrac{1}{2} ( \bbH[Y + Z + Z'] + \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Y] - \bbH[Z']).
nodes.name: Equation (3.10)

nodes.statement: By \Cref{first-useful} (with a change of variables) we have \[d[X ; Y + Z | Y + Z + Z'] - d[X ; Y + Z] \leq \tfrac{1}{2}( \bbH[Y + Z + Z'] - \bbH[Z']).\] Adding this to~\eqref{lem51-a} gives the result.
nodes.name: Proof of Comparison of Ruzsa distances, II
nodes.statement_short: Apply the first comparison twice and add.

nodes.statement: Random variables in this paper are measurable maps $X : \Omega \to S$ from a probability space $\Omega$ to a measurable space $S$, and called $S$-valued random variables.
nodes.name: $S$-valued random variable

nodes.statement: If $X$ is an $S$-valued random variable, the entropy $\bbH[X]$ of $X$ is defined $$ \bbH[X] := \sum_{s \in S} \bbP[X=x] \log \frac{1}{\bbP[X=x]}$$ with the convention that $0 \log \frac{1}{0} = 0$.
nodes.name: Entropy
nodes.statement_short: Shannon entropy of a random variable.
nodes.label: entropy-def

nodes.statement: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] If $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables, and $Y = f(X)$ for some injection $f: S \to T$, then $\bbH[X] = \bbH[Y]$. \item[(ii)] If $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables, and $Y = f(X)$ and $X = g(Y)$ for some functions $f: S \to T$, $g: T \to S$, then $\bbH[X] = \bbH[Y]$. \end{itemize}
nodes.name: Entropy and relabeling
nodes.statement_short: Entropy is invariant under injective or invertible relabelings.
conclusions: \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] If $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables, and $Y = f(X)$ for some injection $f: S \to T$, then $\bbH[X] = \bbH[Y]$. \item[(ii)] If $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables, and $Y = f(X)$ and $X = g(Y)$ for some functions $f: S \to T$, $g: T \to S$, then $\bbH[X] = \bbH[Y]$. \end{itemize}
nodes.label: relabeled-entropy

nodes.statement: Expand out both entropies and rearrange.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy and relabeling
nodes.statement_short: Expand both entropies and rearrange.

nodes.statement: If $X$ is an $S$-valued random variable, then $\bbH[X] \leq \log |S|$.
nodes.name: Jensen bound
assumptions: $X$ is an $S$-valued random variable
nodes.label: jensen-bound

nodes.statement: This is a direct consequence of \Cref{concave} and Jensen's inequality.
nodes.name: Proof of Jensen bound
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality with concavity of h.

nodes.statement: If $H$ is a subset of $S$, an $S$-random variable $X$ is said to be uniformly distributed on $H$ if $\bbP[X = s] = 1/|H|$ for $s \in X$ and $\bbP[X=s] = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.name: Uniform distribution
nodes.label: uniform-def

nodes.statement: Given a finite non-empty subset $H$ of a set $S$, there exists a random variable $X$ (on some probability space) that is uniformly distributed on $H$.
nodes.name: Uniform distributions exist
conclusions: Given a finite non-empty subset $H$ of a set $S$, there exists a random variable $X$ (on some probability space) that is uniformly distributed on $H$
nodes.label: unif-exist

nodes.statement: Direct construction.
nodes.name: Proof of Uniform distributions exist
nodes.statement_short: Direct construction.

nodes.statement: If $X$ is $S$-valued random variable, then $\bbH[X] = \log |S|$ if and only if $X$ is uniformly distributed on $S$.
nodes.name: Entropy of uniform random variable
assumptions: $X$ is $S$-valued random variable
conclusions: $\bbH[X] = \log |S|$ if and only if $X$ is uniformly distributed on $S$
nodes.label: uniform-entropy

nodes.statement: Direct computation in one direction. Converse direction needs the strict Jensen inequality and \Cref{concave}.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy of uniform random variable
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation; converse via strict Jensen.

nodes.statement: If $X$ is uniformly distributed on $H$, then, then $\bbH[X] = \log |H|$.
nodes.name: Entropy of uniform random variable, II
assumptions: $X$ is uniformly distributed on $H$, then
nodes.label: uniform-entropy-II

nodes.statement: Direct computation.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy of uniform random variable, II
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation.

nodes.statement: If $X$ is an $S$-valued random variable, then there exists $s \in S$ such that $\bbP[X=s] \geq \exp(-\bbH[X])$.
nodes.name: Bounded entropy implies concentration
assumptions: $X$ is an $S$-valued random variable
nodes.label: bound-conc

nodes.statement: We have $$ \bbH[X] = \sum_{s \in S} \bbP[X=s] \log \frac{1}{\bbP[X=s]} \geq \min_{s \in S} \log \frac{1}{\bbP[X=s]}$$ and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Bounded entropy implies concentration
nodes.statement_short: Entropy is at least the minimal log-reciprocal probability.

nodes.statement: We use $X,Y$ to denote the pair $\omega \mapsto (X(\omega),Y(\omega)$).
nodes.name: Pair notation $X,Y$

nodes.statement: If $X: \Omega \to S$, $Y: \Omega \to T$, and $Z: \Omega \to U$ are random variables, then $\bbH[X, Y] = \bbH[Y, X]$ and $\bbH[X, (Y,Z)] = \bbH[(X,Y), Z]$.
nodes.name: Commutativity and associativity of joint entropy
assumptions: $X: \Omega \to S$, $Y: \Omega \to T$, and $Z: \Omega \to U$ are random variables
nodes.label: entropy-comm

nodes.statement: Set up an injection from $(X,Y)$ to $(Y,X)$ and use \Cref{relabeled-entropy} for the first claim. Similarly for the second claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Commutativity and associativity of joint entropy
nodes.statement_short: Injection between (X,Y) and (Y,X) plus relabeling.

nodes.statement: If $X: \Omega \to S$ is an $S$-valued random variable and $E$ is an event in $\Omega$, then the conditioned event $(X|E)$ is defined to be the same random variable as $X$, but now the ambient probability measure has been conditioned to $E$.
nodes.name: Conditioned event
nodes.label: condition-event-def

nodes.statement: Note: it may happen that $E$ has zero measure. In which case, the ambient probability measure should be replaced with a zero measure. (In our formalization we achieve this by working with arbitrary measures, and normalizing them to be probability measures if possible, else using the zero measure. Conditioning is also formalized using existing Mathlib definitions.)
nodes.name: Conditioning on a null event

nodes.statement: If $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables, the conditional entropy $\bbH[X|Y]$ is defined as $$ \bbH[X|Y] := \sum_{y \in Y} \bbP[Y = y] \bbH[(X | Y=y)].$$
nodes.name: Conditional entropy
nodes.statement_short: Conditional entropy as the average entropy of conditioned variables.
nodes.label: conditional-entropy-def

nodes.statement: If $X: \Omega \to S$, $Y: \Omega \to T$, and $Z: \Omega \to U$ are random variables, and $Y = f(X,Z)$ almost surely for some map $f: S \times U \to T$ that is injective for each fixed $U$, then $\bbH[X|Z] = \bbH[Y|Z]$. Similarly, if $g: T \to U$ is injective, then $\bbH[X|g(Y)] = \bbH[X|Y]$.
nodes.name: Conditional entropy and relabeling
assumptions: $X: \Omega \to S$, $Y: \Omega \to T$, and $Z: \Omega \to U$ are random variables, and $Y = f(X,Z)$ almost surely for some map $f: S \times U \to T$ that is injective for each fixed $U$
conclusions: $\bbH[X|Z] = \bbH[Y|Z]$. Similarly, if $g: T \to U$ is injective, then $\bbH[X|g(Y)] = \bbH[X|Y]$
nodes.label: relabeled-entropy-cond

nodes.statement: For the first part, use \Cref{conditional-entropy-def} and then \Cref{relabeled-entropy}. The second part is a direct computation.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional entropy and relabeling
nodes.statement_short: Conditional entropy definition plus relabeling; second part by computation.

nodes.statement: If $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables, then $$ \bbH[X, Y] = \bbH[Y] + \bbH[X|Y].$$
nodes.name: Chain rule
assumptions: $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables
nodes.label: chain-rule

nodes.statement: Direct computation.
nodes.name: Proof of Chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation.

nodes.statement: If $X: \Omega \to S$, $Y: \Omega \to T$, $Z: \Omega \to U$ are random variables, then $$ \bbH[X, Y | Z] = \bbH[Y | Z] + \bbH[X|Y, Z].$$
nodes.name: Conditional chain rule
assumptions: $X: \Omega \to S$, $Y: \Omega \to T$, $Z: \Omega \to U$ are random variables
nodes.label: conditional-chain-rule

nodes.statement: For each $z \in U$, we can apply \Cref{chain-rule} to the random variables $(X|Z=z)$ and $(Y|Z=z)$ to obtain $$ \bbH[(X|Z=z),(Y|Z=z)] = \bbH[Y|Z=z] + \bbH[(X|Z=z)|(Y|Z=z)].$$ Now multiply by $\bbP[Z=z]$ and sum. Some helper lemmas may be needed to get to the form above. This sort of ``average over conditioning'' argument to get conditional entropy inequalities from unconditional ones is commonly used in this paper.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Apply the chain rule to conditioned variables and average over Z.

nodes.statement: If $X: \Omega \to S$, $Y: \Omega \to T$ are random variables, then $$\bbI[X : Y] := \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y] - \bbH[X,Y].$$
nodes.name: Mutual information
nodes.label: information-def

nodes.statement: With notation as above, we have $$ \bbI[X : Y] = \bbI[Y:X]$$ $$ \bbI[X : Y] = \bbH[X] - \bbH[X|Y]$$ $$ \bbI[X : Y] = \bbH[Y] - \bbH[Y|X]$$
nodes.name: Alternative formulae for mutual information
nodes.label: alternative-mutual

nodes.statement: Immediate from Lemmas \ref{entropy-comm}, \ref{chain-rule}.
nodes.name: Proof of Alternative formulae for mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Commutativity and the chain rule.

nodes.statement: We have $\bbI[X:Y] \geq 0$.
nodes.name: Nonnegativity of mutual information
nodes.label: mutual-nonneg

nodes.statement: An application of jensen's inequality and \Cref{concave,alternative-mutual}.
nodes.name: Proof of Nonnegativity of mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality and concavity.

nodes.statement: With notation as above, we have $\bbH[X,Y] \leq \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y]$.
nodes.name: Subadditivity
nodes.label: subadditive

nodes.statement: Use \Cref{mutual-nonneg}.
nodes.name: Proof of Subadditivity
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegativity of mutual information.

nodes.statement: With notation as above, we have $\bbH[X|Y] \leq \bbH[X]$.
nodes.name: Conditioning reduces entropy
nodes.label: cond-reduce

nodes.statement: Combine \Cref{mutual-nonneg} with \Cref{alternative-mutual}.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditioning reduces entropy
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegativity of mutual information with its alternative formula.

nodes.statement: With three random variables $X,Y,Z$, one has $\bbH[X|Y,Z] \leq \bbH[X|Z]$.
nodes.name: Submodularity
conclusions: With three random variables $X,Y,Z$, one has $\bbH[X|Y,Z] \leq \bbH[X|Z]$
nodes.label: submodularity

nodes.statement: Apply the ``averaging over conditioning'' argument to \Cref{cond-reduce}.
nodes.name: Proof of Submodularity
nodes.statement_short: Average the conditioning-reduces-entropy bound over conditioning.

nodes.statement: With three random variables $X,Y,Z$, one has $$ \bbH[X,Y,Z] + \bbH[Z] \leq \bbH[X,Z] + \bbH[Y,Z].$$
nodes.name: Alternate form of submodularity
conclusions: With three random variables $X,Y,Z$, one has $$ \bbH[X,Y,Z] + \bbH[Z] \leq \bbH[X,Z] + \bbH[Y,Z].$$
nodes.label: alt-submodularity

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{submodularity} and \Cref{chain-rule}.
nodes.name: Proof of Alternate form of submodularity
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity plus chain rule.

nodes.statement: Two random variables $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are independent if the law of $(X,Y)$ is the product of the law of $X$ and the law of $Y$. Similarly for more than two variables.
nodes.name: Independent random variables
differentia: the law of $(X,Y)$ is the product of the law of $X$ and the law of $Y$
nodes.label: independent-def

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are random variables, then $\bbI[X:Y] = 0$ if and only if $X,Y$ are independent.
nodes.name: Vanishing of mutual information
assumptions: $X,Y$ are random variables
conclusions: $\bbI[X:Y] = 0$ if and only if $X,Y$ are independent
nodes.label: vanish-entropy

nodes.statement: An application of the equality case of Jensen's inequality and \Cref{concave}.
nodes.name: Proof of Vanishing of mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Equality case of Jensen's inequality.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are random variables, then $\bbH[X,Y] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y]$ if and only if $X,Y$ are independent.
nodes.name: Additivity of entropy
assumptions: $X,Y$ are random variables
conclusions: $\bbH[X,Y] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y]$ if and only if $X,Y$ are independent
nodes.label: add-entropy

nodes.statement: Direct from \Cref{vanish-entropy}.
nodes.name: Proof of Additivity of entropy
nodes.statement_short: Direct from vanishing mutual information.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y,Z$ are random variables, with $Z$ $U$-valued, then $$ \bbI[X:Y|Z] := \sum_{z \in U} P[Z=z] \bbI[(X|Z=z): (Y|Z=z)].$$
nodes.name: Conditional mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Conditional mutual information as the average of conditioned mutual informations.
nodes.label: conditional-mutual-def

nodes.statement: We have $$ \bbI[X:Y|Z] := \bbH[X|Z] + \bbH[Y|Z] - \bbH[X,Y|Z]$$ and $$ \bbI[X:Y|Z] := \bbH[X|Z] - \bbH[X|Y,Z].$$
nodes.name: Alternate formula for conditional mutual information
nodes.label: conditional-mutual-alt

nodes.statement: Routine computation.
nodes.name: Proof of Alternate formula for conditional mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Routine computation.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y,Z$ are random variables, then $\bbI[X:Y|Z] \ge 0$.
nodes.name: Nonnegativity of conditional mutual information
assumptions: $X,Y,Z$ are random variables
nodes.label: conditional-nonneg

nodes.statement: Use \Cref{conditional-mutual-def} and \Cref{submodularity}.
nodes.name: Proof of Nonnegativity of conditional mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Definition plus submodularity.

nodes.statement: Two random variables $X: \Omega \to S$ and $Y: \Omega \to T$ are conditionally independent relative to another random variable $Z: \Omega \to U$ if $P[X = s \wedge Y = t| Z=u] = P[X=s|Z=u] P[Y=t|Z=u]$ for all $s \in S, t \in T, u \in U$. (We won't need conditional independence for more variables than this.)
nodes.name: Conditionally independent random variables
nodes.label: conditional-independent-def

nodes.statement: If $X,Y,Z$ are random variables, then $\bbI[X:Y|Z] = 0$ iff $X,Y$ are conditionally independent over $Z$.
nodes.name: Vanishing conditional mutual information
assumptions: $X,Y,Z$ are random variables
nodes.label: conditional-vanish

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{vanish-entropy} and \Cref{conditional-independent-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Vanishing conditional mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing mutual information applied fibrewise.

nodes.statement: If $X, Y$ are conditionally independent over $Z$, then $$ \bbH[X,Y,Z] =\bbH[X,Z] + \bbH[Y,Z] - \bbH[Z].$$
nodes.name: Entropy of conditionally independent variables
assumptions: $X, Y$ are conditionally independent over $Z$
nodes.label: cond-trial-ent

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{conditional-vanish} and \Cref{conditional-mutual-alt}.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy of conditionally independent variables
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing conditional mutual information plus its alternative formula.

nodes.statement: Throughout this chapter, $G = \F_2^n$, and $X^0_1, X^0_2$ are $G$-valued random variables.
nodes.name: Reference variables $X^0_1, X^0_2$

nodes.statement: If $X_1,X_2$ are two $G$-valued random variables, then $$ \tau[X_1; X_2] := d[X_1; X_2] + \eta d[X^0_1; X_1] + \eta d[X^0_2; X_2].$$
nodes.name: $\tau$ functional
nodes.statement_short: tau functional: Ruzsa distance plus eta times distances to the reference variables.
nodes.label: tau-def

nodes.statement: If $X'_1, X'_2$ are copies of $X_1,X_2$, then $\tau[X'_1;X'_2] = \tau[X_1;X_2]$.
nodes.name: $\tau$ depends only on distribution
assumptions: $X'_1, X'_2$ are copies of $X_1,X_2$
nodes.label: tau-copy

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{copy-ent}.
nodes.name: Proof of $\tau$ depends only on distribution
nodes.statement_short: Copies have the same entropy.

nodes.statement: A pair of $G$-valued random variables $X_1, X_2$ are said to be a $\tau$-minimizer if one has $$\tau[X_1;X_2] \leq \tau[X'_1;X'_2] $$ for all $G$-valued random variables $X'_1, X'_2$.
nodes.name: $\tau$-minimizer
nodes.label: tau-min-def

nodes.statement: A pair $X_1, X_2$ of $\tau$-minimizers exist.
nodes.name: $\tau$ has minimum
nodes.label: tau-min

nodes.statement: By \Cref{tau-copy}, $\tau$ only depends on the probability distributions of $X_1, X_2$. This ranges over a compact space, and $\tau$ is continuous. So $\tau$ has a minimum.
nodes.name: Proof of $\tau$ has minimum
nodes.statement_short: tau depends only on distributions, a compact space, and is continuous.

nodes.statement: In this section we assume that $X_1,X_2$ are $\tau$-minimizers.
nodes.name: $X_1,X_2$ are $\tau$-minimizers

nodes.statement: We also write $k := d[X_1;X_2]$.
nodes.name: $k$
nodes.statement_short: k denotes the Ruzsa distance between the tau-minimizers.

nodes.statement: For any $G$-valued random variables $X'_1,X'_2$, one has $$ d[X'_1;X'_2] \geq k - \eta (d[X^0_1;X'_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1] ) - \eta (d[X^0_2;X'_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2] ).$$
nodes.name: Distance lower bound
nodes.statement_short: For a tau-minimizer, any pair has distance at least k minus eta times the reference-distance increments.
assumptions: $G$-valued random variables $X'_1,X'_2$
nodes.label: distance-lower

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{tau-def} and \Cref{tau-min}.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from minimality of tau.

nodes.statement: For any $G$-valued random variables $X'_1,X'_2$ and random variables $Z,W$, one has $$ d[X'_1|Z;X'_2|W] \geq k - \eta (d[X^0_1;X'_1|Z] - d[X^0_1;X_1] ) - \eta (d[X^0_2;X'_2|W] - d[X^0_2;X_2] ).$$
nodes.name: Conditional distance lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Conditional version of the distance lower bound for tau-minimizers.
assumptions: $G$-valued random variables $X'_1,X'_2$ and random variables $Z,W$
nodes.label: cond-distance-lower

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{distance-lower} to conditioned random variables and then average.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional distance lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Apply the unconditional bound to conditioned variables and average.

nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2, \tilde X_1, \tilde X_2$ be independent random variables, with $X_1,\tilde X_1$ copies of $X_1$ and $X_2,\tilde X_2$ copies of $X_2$. (This is possible thanks to \Cref{independent-exist}.)
nodes.name: Independent copies $\tilde X_1, \tilde X_2$

nodes.statement: We also define the quantity $$ I_1 := I [X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2].$$
nodes.name: $I_1$
nodes.statement_short: I_1 is the conditional mutual information of X_1+X_2 and X~_1+X_2 given the four-fold sum.

nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} & d[X_1+\tilde X_2;X_2+\tilde X_1] + d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1] \\ &\quad + \bbI[X_1+ X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 \,|\, X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2] = 2k. \end{align*}
nodes.name: Fibring identity for first estimate
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity expressing 2k as two distances plus I_1.
conclusions: \begin{align*} & d[X_1+\tilde X_2;X_2+\tilde X_1] + d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1] \\ &\quad + \bbI[X_1+ X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 \,|\, X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2] = 2k. \end{align*}
nodes.label: first-fibre

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{cor-fibre}.
nodes.name: Proof of Fibring identity for first estimate
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the specific fibring identity.

nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} d[X_1+\tilde X_2; X_2+\tilde X_1] \geq k &- \eta (d[X^0_1; X_1+\tilde X_2] - d[X^0_1; X_1]) \\& \qquad- \eta (d[X^0_2; X_2+\tilde X_1] - d[X^0_2; X_2]) \end{align*}
nodes.name: Lower bound on distances
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound on d[X_1+X~_2; X_2+X~_1] from minimality.
conclusions: \begin{align*} d[X_1+\tilde X_2; X_2+\tilde X_1] \geq k &- \eta (d[X^0_1; X_1+\tilde X_2] - d[X^0_1; X_1]) \\& \qquad- \eta (d[X^0_2; X_2+\tilde X_1] - d[X^0_2; X_2]) \end{align*}
nodes.label: first-dist-sum

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{distance-lower}.
nodes.name: Proof of Lower bound on distances
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the distance lower bound.

nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} & d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1] \\ & \qquad\quad \geq k - \eta (d[X^0_1; X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2] - d[X^0_1; X_1]) \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad - \eta(d[X^0_2; X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1] - d[X^0_2; X_2]). \end{align*}
nodes.name: Lower bound on conditional distances
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound on the conditional distance from minimality.
conclusions: \begin{align*} & d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1] \\ & \qquad\quad \geq k - \eta (d[X^0_1; X_1 | X_1 + \tilde X_2] - d[X^0_1; X_1]) \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad - \eta(d[X^0_2; X_2 | X_2 + \tilde X_1] - d[X^0_2; X_2]). \end{align*}
nodes.label: first-cond

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{cond-distance-lower}.
nodes.name: Proof of Lower bound on conditional distances
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the conditional distance lower bound.

nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} d[X^0_1; X_1+\tilde X_2] - d[X^0_1; X_1] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1]\\ d[X^0_2;X_2+\tilde X_1] - d[X^0_2; X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2], \\ d[X_1^0;X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2] - d[X_1^0;X_1] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2] \\ d[X_2^0; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1] - d[X_2^0; X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2}k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1]. \end{align*}
nodes.name: Upper bound on distance differences
nodes.statement_short: Four upper bounds on distance increments relative to reference variables.
conclusions: \begin{align*} d[X^0_1; X_1+\tilde X_2] - d[X^0_1; X_1] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1]\\ d[X^0_2;X_2+\tilde X_1] - d[X^0_2; X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2], \\ d[X_1^0;X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2] - d[X_1^0;X_1] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2] \\ d[X_2^0; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1] - d[X_2^0; X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2}k + \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_2] - \tfrac{1}{4} \bbH[X_1]. \end{align*}
nodes.label: first-upper

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{first-useful} (and recalling that $k$ is defined to be $d[X_1;X_2]$).
nodes.name: Proof of Upper bound on distance differences
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the first comparison of Ruzsa distances.

nodes.statement: We have $I_1 \leq 2 \eta k$.
nodes.name: First estimate
nodes.label: first-estimate

nodes.statement: Take a suitable linear combination of \Cref{first-fibre}, \Cref{first-dist-sum}, \Cref{first-cond}, and \Cref{first-upper}.
nodes.name: Proof of First estimate
nodes.statement_short: Linear combination of the fibring identity and the three bounds.

nodes.statement: With the same notation, we have \begin{equation} \bbH[X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] \le \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_1]+\tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_2] + (2 + \eta) k - I_1. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Entropy bound on quadruple sum
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of the four-fold sum bounded in terms of entropies, k and I_1.
nodes.label: foursum-bound

nodes.statement: \bbH[X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] \le \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_1]+\tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_2] + (2 + \eta) k - I_1.
nodes.name: Equation (5.1)
nodes.label: HS-bound

nodes.statement: Subtracting \Cref{first-cond} from \Cref{first-fibre}, and combining the resulting inequality with \Cref{first-upper} gives the bound \[ d[X_1+\tilde X_2;X_2+\tilde X_1] \le (1 + \eta) k - I_1, \] and the claim follows from \Cref{ruz-indep} and the definition of $k$.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy bound on quadruple sum
nodes.statement_short: Subtract the conditional bound from the fibring identity and combine with the upper bounds.

nodes.statement: We introduce the quantity $$ I_2 := \bbI[X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2].$$
nodes.name: $I_2$
nodes.statement_short: I_2 is the conditional mutual information of X_1+X_2 and X_1+X~_1 given the four-fold sum.

nodes.statement: We have $$ d[X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2+\tilde X_2] \geq k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( d[X_1; X_1] + d[X_2;X_2] ).$$
nodes.name: Distance between sums
conclusions: $$ d[X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2+\tilde X_2] \geq k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( d[X_1; X_1] + d[X_2;X_2] ).$$
nodes.label: dist-sums

nodes.statement: From \Cref{distance-lower} one has \begin{align*} d[X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2+\tilde X_2] \geq k &- \eta(d[X^0_1;X_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1+\tilde X_1]) \\ &- \eta(d[X^0_2;X_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2+\tilde X_2]). \end{align*} Now \Cref{first-useful} gives $$ d[X^0_1;X_1+\tilde X_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_1;X_1]$$ and $$ d[X^0_2;X_2+\tilde X_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_2;X_2], $$ and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance between sums
nodes.statement_short: Distance lower bound plus the first comparison lemma.

nodes.statement: We have \[d[X_1;X_1] + d[X_2;X_2] \leq 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \]
nodes.name: Bound on $d[X_1;X_1]+d[X_2;X_2]$
nodes.statement_short: Sum of self-distances bounded by 2k plus a multiple of 2 eta k - I_1.
nodes.label: second-estimate-aux

nodes.statement: We may use \Cref{ruz-indep} to expand \begin{align*} & d[X_1+\tilde X_1;X_2+\tilde X_2] \\ &= \bbH[X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_1+\tilde X_1] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_2+\tilde X_2] \\ &= \bbH[X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_1] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[X_2] \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( d[X_1;X_1] + d[X_2; X_2] \right), \end{align*} and hence by \Cref{foursum-bound} \[ d[X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2+\tilde X_2] \leq (2+\eta) k - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( d[X_1;X_1] + d[X_2;X_2] \right) - I_1. \] Combining this bound with \Cref{dist-sums} we obtain the result.
nodes.name: Proof of Bound on $d[X_1;X_1]+d[X_2;X_2]$
nodes.statement_short: Expand d[X_1+X~_1;X_2+X~_2] and combine with the four-sum bound and distance between sums.

nodes.statement: We have $$ I_2 \leq 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}.$$
nodes.name: Second estimate
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound on I_2 in terms of eta, k and I_1.
nodes.label: second-estimate

nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{cor-fibre}, but now with the choice \[ (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4) := (X_2, X_1, \tilde X_2, \tilde X_1). \] Now \Cref{cor-fibre} can be rewritten as \begin{align*} &d[X_1+\tilde X_1;X_2+\tilde X_2] + d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] \\ &\quad + \bbI[X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 \,|\, X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] = 2k, \end{align*} recalling once again that $k := d[X_1;X_2]$. From \Cref{cond-distance-lower} one has \begin{align*} d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] \geq k &- \eta (d[X^0_1;X_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1]) \\& - \eta (d[X^0_2;X_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2]) . \end{align*} while from \Cref{first-useful} we have \[ d[X^0_1;X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_1;X_1], \] and \[ d[X^0_2;X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_1;X_2]. \] Combining all these inequalities with \Cref{dist-sums}, we have \begin{equation} \bbI[X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] \leq \eta ( d[X_1; X_1] + d[X_2; X_2] ). \end{equation} Together with \Cref{second-estimate-aux}, this gives the conclusion.
nodes.name: Proof of Second estimate
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity with permuted variables, minimality lower bounds, and the auxiliary estimate.

nodes.statement: \bbI[X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] \leq \eta ( d[X_1; X_1] + d[X_2; X_2] ).
nodes.name: Equation (5.2)
nodes.label: combined

nodes.statement: Let $X_1,X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2$ be as before, and introduce the random variables \[U := X_1 + X_2, \qquad V := \tilde X_1 + X_2, \qquad W := X_1 + \tilde X_1\] and \[ S := X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2.\]
nodes.name: $U, V, W, S$

nodes.statement: We have $$ I(U:W | S) = I(V:W | S).$$
nodes.name: Symmetry identity
nodes.label: symm-lemma

nodes.statement: This should follow from \Cref{copy-ent}, \Cref{conditional-mutual-alt}, and \Cref{chain-rule}.
nodes.name: Proof of Symmetry identity
nodes.statement_short: Should follow from copy invariance and conditional mutual information formulas.

nodes.statement: We have $$ I(U : V \, | \, S) + I(V : W \, | \,S) + I(W : U \, | \, S) \leq 6 \eta k - \frac{1 - 5 \eta}{1-\eta} (2 \eta k - I_1). $$
nodes.name: Bound on conditional mutual informations
nodes.statement_short: Sum of the three conditional mutual informations of U,V,W given S is bounded.
nodes.label: uvw-s

nodes.statement: From the definitions of $I_1,I_2$ and \Cref{symm-lemma}, we see that \[ I_1 = I(U : V \, | \, S), \qquad I_2 = I(W : U \, | \, S), \qquad I_2 = I(V : W \, | \,S). \] Applying \Cref{first-estimate} and \Cref{second-estimate} we have the inequalities \[ I_2 \leq 2 \eta k + \frac{2\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta} . \] We conclude that $$ I_1 + I_2 + I_2 \leq I_1+4\eta k+ \frac{4\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta} $$ and the claim follows from some calculation.
nodes.name: Proof of Bound on conditional mutual informations
nodes.statement_short: Identify the three informations with I_1, I_2 and apply the first and second estimates.

nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \big(d[X^0_i;A|S] & - d[X^0_i;X_i]\big) \\ &\leq (6 - 3\eta) k + 3(2 \eta k - I_1). \end{align*}
nodes.name: Bound on distance increments
nodes.statement_short: Bound on summed reference-distance increments for A in {U,V,W} conditioned on S.
nodes.label: total-dist

nodes.statement: By \Cref{second-useful} (taking $X = X_1^0$, $Y = X_1$, $Z = X_2$ and $Z' = \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2$, so that $Y + Z = U$ and $Y + Z + Z' = S$) we have, noting that $\bbH[Y+ Z] = \bbH[Z']$, \[ d[X^0_1;U|S] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_1]). \] Further applications of \Cref{second-useful} give \begin{align*} d[X^0_2;U|S] - d[X^0_2; X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_2]) \\ d[X^0_1;V|S] - d[X^0_1;X_1] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_1])\\ d[X^0_2;V|S] - d[X^0_2;X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_2]) \end{align*} and \[d[X^0_1;W|S] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] + \bbH[W] - \bbH[X_1] - \bbH[W']),\] where $W' := X_2 + \tilde X_2$. To treat $d[X^0_2;W|S]$, first note that this equals $d[X^0_2;W'|S]$, since for a fixed choice $s$ of $S$ we have $W' = W + s$ (here we need some helper lemma about Ruzsa distance). Now we may apply \Cref{second-useful} to obtain \[d[X^0_2;W'|S] - d[X^0_2;X_2] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] + \bbH[W'] - \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[W]).\] Summing these six estimates and using \Cref{foursum-bound}, we conclude that \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \big(d[X^0_i;A|S] & - d[X^0_i;X_i]\big) \\ &\leq 3 \bbH[S] - \tfrac{3}{2} \bbH[X_1] - \tfrac{3}{2} \bbH[X_2]\\ &\leq (6 - 3\eta) k + 3(2 \eta k - I_1) \end{align*} as required.
nodes.name: Proof of Bound on distance increments
nodes.statement_short: Six applications of the second comparison lemma, summed with the four-sum bound.

nodes.statement: We have $U+V+W=0$.
nodes.name: Key identity
nodes.label: key-ident

nodes.statement: Obvious because we are in characteristic two.
nodes.name: Proof of Key identity
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic two.

nodes.statement: For the next two lemmas, let $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically.
nodes.name: Zero-sum triple $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$
also_stated_at: For the next two lemmas, let $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically.

nodes.statement: Set \begin{equation} \delta := \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} \bbI[T_i;T_j]. \end{equation}
nodes.name: $\delta$
nodes.statement_short: delta is the sum of pairwise mutual informations of the triple.

nodes.statement: \delta := \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq 3} \bbI[T_i;T_j].
nodes.name: Equation (5.3)
nodes.label: delta-t1t2t3-def

nodes.statement: One has \begin{align*} k \leq \delta + \eta (& d[X^0_1;T_1]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2]-d[X^0_2;X_2]) \\ & + \tfrac12 \eta \bbI[T_1:T_3] + \tfrac12 \eta \bbI[T_2:T_3]. \end{align*}
nodes.name: Constructing good variables, I
nodes.statement_short: k bounded by delta plus eta-weighted distance increments for a zero-sum triple.
nodes.label: construct-good-prelim

nodes.statement: (Note: in the paper, this lemma was phrased in a more intuitive formulation that is basically the contrapositive of the one here. Similarly for the next two lemmas.)
nodes.name: Contrapositive phrasing

nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{entropic-bsg} with $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there. Since $T_1 + T_2 = T_3$, the conclusion is that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] & d[(T_1 | T_3 = t_3); (T_2 | T_3 = t_3)] \\ & \leq 3 \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + 2 \bbH[T_3] - \bbH[T_1] - \bbH[T_2]. \end{align} The right-hand side in~\eqref{bsg-t1t2} can be rearranged as \begin{align*} & 2( \bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - 3 \bbH[T_1,T_2] \\ & = 2(\bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - \bbH[T_1,T_2] - \bbH[T_2,T_3] - \bbH[T_1, T_3] = \delta,\end{align*} using the fact (from \Cref{relabeled-entropy}) that all three terms $\bbH[T_i,T_j]$ are equal to $\bbH[T_1,T_2,T_3]$ and hence to each other. We also have \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} P[T_3 = t_3] \bigl(d[X^0_1; (T_1 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_1;X_1]\bigr) \\ &\quad = d[X^0_1; T_1 | T_3] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq d[X^0_1;T_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[T_1 : T_3] \end{align*} by \Cref{cond-dist-fact}, and similarly \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] (d[X^0_2;(T_2 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_2; X_2]) \\ &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \leq d[X^0_2;T_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[T_2 : T_3]. \end{align*} Putting the above observations together, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3=t_3] \psi[(T_1 | T_3=t_3); (T_2 | T_3=t_3)] \leq \delta + \eta (d[X^0_1;T_1]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) \\ + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2]-d[X^0_2;X_2]) + \tfrac12 \eta \bbI[T_1:T_3] + \tfrac12 \eta \bbI[T_2:T_3] \end{align*} where we introduce the notation \[\psi[Y_1; Y_2] := d[Y_1;Y_2] + \eta (d[X_1^0;Y_1] - d[X_1^0;X_1]) + \eta(d[X_2^0;Y_2] - d[X_2^0;X_2]).\] On the other hand, from \Cref{distance-lower} we have $k \leq \psi[Y_1;Y_2]$, and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Constructing good variables, I
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG on (T_1,T_2), conditional distance bound, and minimality via psi.

nodes.statement: One has \begin{align*} k & \leq \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (d[X^0_i;T_j] - d[X^0_i; X_i]) \biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.name: Constructing good variables, II
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrized bound on k via a zero-sum triple T_1,T_2,T_3.
nodes.label: construct-good

nodes.statement: Average \Cref{construct-good-prelim} over all six permutations of $T_1,T_2,T_3$.
nodes.name: Proof of Constructing good variables, II
nodes.statement_short: Average the previous lemma over permutations of T_1,T_2,T_3.

nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2$ be tau-minimizers. Then $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
nodes.name: $\tau$-decrement
nodes.statement_short: tau-minimizers have zero Ruzsa distance.
assumptions: $X_1, X_2$ be tau-minimizers
nodes.label: de-prop

nodes.statement: Set $k := d[X_1;X_2]$. Applying \Cref{construct-good} with any random variables $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically, we deduce that \[ k \leq \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (d[X^0_1;T_j] - d[X^0_i;X_i]) \biggr). \] Note that $\delta$ is still defined by~\eqref{delta-t1t2t3-def} and thus depends on $T_1,T_2,T_3$. In particular we may apply this for \[ T_1 = (U | S = s),\qquad T_2 = (V | S = s), \qquad T_3 = (W | S = s) \] for $s$ in the range of $S$ (which is a valid choice by \Cref{key-ident}) and then average over $s$ with weights $p_S(s)$, to obtain \[k \leq \tilde \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \tilde \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \bigl( d[X^0_i;A|S] - d[X^0_i;X_i]\bigr) \biggr),\] where \[ \tilde \delta := \bbI[U : V | S] + \bbI[V : W | S] + \bbI[W : U | S]. \] Putting this together with \Cref{uvw-s} and \Cref{total-dist}, we conclude that \begin{align*} k &\leq \Bigl(1+\frac{\eta}{3}\Bigr)\Bigl(6\eta k-\frac{1-5\eta}{1-\eta}(2\eta k-I_1)\Bigr)+\frac{\eta}{3}\Bigl((6-3\eta)k+3(2\eta k-I_1)\Bigr)\\ &= (8\eta + \eta^2) k - \biggl( \frac{1 - 5 \eta}{1-\eta}\Bigl(1 + \frac{\eta}{3}\Bigr) - \eta \biggr)(2 \eta k - I_1)\\ &\leq (8 \eta + \eta^2) k \end{align*} since the quantity $2 \eta k - I_1$ is non-negative (by \Cref{first-estimate}), and its coefficient in the above expression is non-positive provided that $\eta(2\eta + 17) \le 3$, which is certainly the case with \Cref{eta-def}. Moreover, from \Cref{eta-def} we have $8 \eta + \eta^2 < 1$. It follows that $k=0$, as desired.
nodes.name: Proof of $\tau$-decrement
nodes.statement_short: Apply the good-variable construction to (U,V,W) conditioned on S and combine bounds to get k <= (8 eta + eta^2) k. The key step averages the construction over values of S.

nodes.statement: Let $G = \F_2^n$, and suppose that $X^0_1, X^0_2$ are $G$-valued random variables. Then there is some subgroup $H \leq G$ such that \[ d[X^0_1;U_H] + d[X^0_2;U_H] \le 11 d[X^0_1;X^0_2], \] where $U_H$ is uniformly distributed on $H$. Furthermore, both $d[X^0_1;U_H]$ and $d[X^0_2;U_H]$ are at most $6 d[X^0_1;X^0_2]$.
nodes.name: Entropy version of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Entropic PFR over F_2^n: some subgroup H has d[X^0_1;U_H]+d[X^0_2;U_H] <= 11 d[X^0_1;X^0_2].
assumptions: $G = \F_2^n$, and suppose that $X^0_1, X^0_2$ are $G$-valued random variables
conclusions: there is some subgroup $H \leq G$ such that \[ d[X^0_1;U_H] + d[X^0_2;U_H] \le 11 d[X^0_1;X^0_2], \] where $U_H$ is uniformly distributed on $H$. Furthermore, both $d[X^0_1;U_H]$ and $d[X^0_2;U_H]$ are at most $6 d[X^0_1;X^0_2]$
nodes.label: entropy-pfr

nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2$ be the $\tau$-minimizer from \Cref{tau-min}. From \Cref{de-prop}, $d[X_1;X_2]=0$. From \Cref{lem:100pc}, $d[X_1;U_H] = d[X_2; U_H] = 0$. Also from $\tau$-minimization we have $\tau[X_1;X_2] \leq \tau[X^0_2;X^0_1]$. Using this and the Ruzsa triangle inequality we can conclude.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy version of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Take a tau-minimizer, use tau-decrement and the 100% inverse theorem, then the triangle inequality.

nodes.statement: Let $\pi : H \to H'$ be a homomorphism additive groups, and let $Z_1,Z_2$ be $H$-valued random variables. Then we have \[ d[Z_1; Z_2] \geq d[\pi(Z_1);\pi(Z_2)] + d[Z_1|\pi(Z_1); Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)]. \] Moreover, if $Z_1,Z_2$ are taken to be independent, then the difference between the two sides is $$I( Z_1 - Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1), \pi(Z_2)) | \pi(Z_1 - Z_2) ).$$
nodes.name: General fibring identity
nodes.statement_short: Ruzsa distance splits along a homomorphism into image distance plus conditional distance, with mutual information defect.
assumptions: $\pi : H \to H'$ be a homomorphism additive groups, and let $Z_1,Z_2$ be $H$-valued random variables
conclusions: \[ d[Z_1; Z_2] \geq d[\pi(Z_1);\pi(Z_2)] + d[Z_1|\pi(Z_1); Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)]. \] Moreover, if $Z_1,Z_2$ are taken to be independent, then the difference between the two sides is $$I( Z_1 - Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1), \pi(Z_2)) | \pi(Z_1 - Z_2) ).$$
nodes.label: fibring-ident

nodes.statement: Let $Z_1,Z_2$ be independent throughout (this is possible by \Cref{ruz-copy} and \Cref{independent-exist}). By \Cref{cond-dist-alt}, We have \begin{align*} & d[Z_1 |\pi(Z_1); Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)] \\ & = \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)] \\ & \leq \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1+Z_2)] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)] - \tfrac{1}{2}H[Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)] \\ & = d[Z_1;Z_2] - d[\pi(Z_1);\pi(Z_2)]. \end{align*} In the middle step, we used \Cref{submodularity}, and in the last step we used the fact that \[\bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1-Z_2)] = \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2] - \bbH[\pi(Z_1-Z_2)]\] (thanks to \Cref{chain-rule} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy}) and that \[\bbH[Z_i| \pi(Z_i)] = \bbH[Z_i] - \bbH[\pi(Z_i)]\] (since $Z_i$ determines $\pi(Z_i)$). This gives the claimed inequality. The difference between the two sides is precisely \[\bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)] - \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)].\] To rewrite this in terms of (conditional) mutual information, we use the identity \[\bbH[A|B] - \bbH[A | B,C] = \bbI[A : C | B],\] (which follows \Cref{conditional-mutual-alt}) taking $A := Z_1 - Z_2$, $B := \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)$ and $C := (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_{2}))$, and noting that in this case $\bbH[A | B,C] = \bbH[A | C]$ since $C$ uniquely determines $B$ (this may require another helper lemma about entropy). This completes the proof.
nodes.name: Proof of General fibring identity
nodes.statement_short: Expand conditional distance, use submodularity, and express the defect as conditional mutual information.

nodes.statement: If $\pi:G\to H$ is a homomorphism of additive groups and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables then \[d[X;Y]\geq d[\pi(X);\pi(Y)].\]
nodes.name: Ruzsa distance decreases under homomorphisms
