assumptions: $\pi:G\to H$ is a homomorphism of additive groups and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: fibring-ineq

nodes.statement: By \Cref{fibring-ident} and the nonnegativity of conditional Ruzsa distance (from \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg}) we have \[d[X;Y]\geq d[\pi(X);\pi(Y)]+d[X\mid \pi(X);Y\mid \pi(Y)].\] The inequality follows from $d[X\mid \pi(X);Y\mid \pi(Y)]\geq 0$ (\Cref{ruzsa-nonneg}).
nodes.name: Proof of Ruzsa distance decreases under homomorphisms
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity plus nonnegativity of conditional distance.

nodes.statement: Let $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3$ and $Y_4$ be independent $G$-valued random variables. Then \begin{align*} & d[Y_1+Y_3; Y_2+Y_4] + d[Y_1|Y_1+Y_3; Y_2|Y_2+Y_4] \\ &\qquad + \bbI[Y_1+Y_2 : Y_2 + Y_4 | Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4] = d[Y_1; Y_2] + d[Y_3; Y_4]. \end{align*}
nodes.name: Specific fibring identity
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity for four independent variables under the addition map.
assumptions: $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3$ and $Y_4$ be independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: cor-fibre

nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{fibring-ident} with $H := G \times G$, $H' := G$, $\pi$ the addition homomorphism $\pi(x,y) := x+y$, and with the random variables $Z_1 := (Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Z_2 := (Y_2,Y_4)$. Then by independence (\Cref{add-entropy}) \[ d[Z_1; Z_2] = d[Y_1; Y_2] + d[Y_3; Y_4] \] while by definition \[ d[\pi(Z_1); \pi(Z_2)] = d[Y_1+Y_3; Y_2+Y_4]. \] Furthermore, \[ d[Z_1|\pi(Z_1); Z_2|\pi(Z_2)] = d[Y_1|Y_1+Y_3;Y_2|Y_2+Y_4], \] since $Z_1=(Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Y_1$ are linked by an invertible affine transformation once $\pi(Z_1)=Y_1+Y_3$ is fixed, and similarly for $Z_2$ and $Y_2$. (This has to do with \Cref{relabeled-entropy-cond}) Finally, we have \begin{align*} &\bbI[Z_1 + Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)) \,|\, \pi(Z_1) + \pi(Z_2)] \\ &\ = \bbI[(Y_1+Y_2, Y_3+Y_4) : (Y_1+Y_3, Y_2+Y_4) \,|\, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4] \\ &\ = \bbI[Y_1+Y_2 : Y_2+Y_4 \,|\, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4] \end{align*} where in the last line we used the fact that $(Y_1+Y_2, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_3+Y_4$ and similarly $(Y_2+Y_4, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_1+Y_3$. (This requires another helper lemma about entropy.)
nodes.name: Proof of Specific fibring identity
nodes.statement_short: Apply the general fibring identity to the addition map on G x G.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are two $G$-valued random variables, the Kullback--Leibler divergence is defined as $$ D_{KL}(X\Vert Y) := \sum_x \mathbf{P}(X=x) \log \frac{\mathbf{P}(X=x)}{\mathbf{P}(Y=x)}.$$
nodes.name: Kullback--Leibler divergence
nodes.label: kl-div

nodes.statement: If $X'$ is a copy of $X$, and $Y'$ is a copy of $Y$, then $D_{KL}(X'\Vert Y') = D_{KL}(X\Vert Y)$.
nodes.name: Kullback--Leibler divergence of copy
assumptions: $X'$ is a copy of $X$, and $Y'$ is a copy of $Y$
nodes.label: kl-div-copy

nodes.statement: Clear from definition.
nodes.name: Proof of Kullback--Leibler divergence of copy
nodes.statement_short: Clear from definition.

nodes.statement: $D_{KL}(X\Vert Y) \geq 0$.
nodes.name: Gibbs inequality
nodes.label: Gibbs

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{log-sum} on the definition.
nodes.name: Proof of Gibbs inequality
nodes.statement_short: Log sum inequality.

nodes.statement: If $D_{KL}(X\Vert Y) = 0$, then $Y$ is a copy of $X$.
nodes.name: Converse Gibbs inequality
assumptions: $D_{KL}(X\Vert Y) = 0$
nodes.label: Gibbs-converse

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{converse-log-sum}.
nodes.name: Proof of Converse Gibbs inequality
nodes.statement_short: Converse log sum inequality.

nodes.statement: If $S$ is a finite set, $\sum_{s \in S} w_s = 1$ for some non-negative $w_s$, and ${\bf P}(X=x) = \sum_{s\in S} w_s {\bf P}(X_s=x)$, ${\bf P}(Y=x) = \sum_{s\in S} w_s {\bf P}(Y_s=x)$ for all $x$, then $$D_{KL}(X\Vert Y) \le \sum_{s\in S} w_s D_{KL}(X_s\Vert Y_s).$$
nodes.name: Convexity of Kullback--Leibler
nodes.statement_short: KL divergence is jointly convex under mixtures.
assumptions: $S$ is a finite set, $\sum_{s \in S} w_s = 1$ for some non-negative $w_s$, and ${\bf P}(X=x) = \sum_{s\in S} w_s {\bf P}(X_s=x)$, ${\bf P}(Y=x) = \sum_{s\in S} w_s {\bf P}(Y_s=x)$ for all $x$
nodes.label: kl-div-convex

nodes.statement: For each $x$, replace $\log \frac{\mathbf{P}(X_s=x)}{\mathbf{P}(Y_s=x)}$ in the definition with $\log \frac{w_s\mathbf{P}(X_s=x)}{w_s\mathbf{P}(Y_s=x)}$ for each $s$, and apply \Cref{log-sum}.
nodes.name: Proof of Convexity of Kullback--Leibler
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite with weights and apply the log sum inequality.

nodes.statement: If $f:G \to H$ is an injection, then $D_{KL}(f(X)\Vert f(Y)) = D_{KL}(X\Vert Y)$.
nodes.name: Kullback--Leibler and injections
assumptions: $f:G \to H$ is an injection
nodes.label: kl-div-inj

nodes.statement: Clear from definition.
nodes.name: Proof of Kullback--Leibler and injections
nodes.statement_short: Clear from definition.

nodes.statement: If $X, Y, Z$ are independent $G$-valued random variables, then $$D_{KL}(X+Z\Vert Y+Z) \leq D_{KL}(X\Vert Y).$$
nodes.name: Kullback--Leibler and sums
assumptions: $X, Y, Z$ are independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: kl-sums

nodes.statement: For each $z$, $D_{KL}(X+z\Vert Y+z)=D_{KL}(X\Vert Y)$ by \Cref{kl-div-inj}. Then apply \Cref{kl-div-convex} with $w_z=\mathbf{P}(Z=z)$.
nodes.name: Proof of Kullback--Leibler and sums
nodes.statement_short: Translation invariance plus convexity with weights P(Z=z).

nodes.statement: If $X,Y,Z$ are random variables, with $X,Z$ defined on the same sample space, we define $$ D_{KL}(X|Z \Vert Y) := \sum_z \mathbf{P}(Z=z) D_{KL}( (X|Z=z) \Vert Y).$$
nodes.name: Conditional Kullback--Leibler divergence
nodes.label: ckl-div

nodes.statement: If $X, Y$ are independent $G$-valued random variables, and $Z$ is another random variable defined on the same sample space as $X$, then $$D_{KL}((X|Z)\Vert Y) = D_{KL}(X\Vert Y) + \bbH[X] - \bbH[X|Z].$$
nodes.name: Kullback--Leibler and conditioning
nodes.statement_short: Conditional KL divergence equals KL divergence plus the entropy drop from conditioning.
assumptions: $X, Y$ are independent $G$-valued random variables, and $Z$ is another random variable defined on the same sample space as $X$
nodes.label: kl-cond

nodes.statement: Compare the terms correspond to each $x\in G$ on both sides.
nodes.name: Proof of Kullback--Leibler and conditioning
nodes.statement_short: Compare terms for each x.

nodes.statement: $D_{KL}((X|W)\Vert Y) \geq 0$.
nodes.name: Conditional Gibbs inequality
nodes.label: Conditional-Gibbs

nodes.statement: Clear from Definition \ref{ckl-div} and Lemma \ref{Gibbs}.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional Gibbs inequality
nodes.statement_short: Definition plus Gibbs inequality.

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be an additive group, and let $A$ be a non-empty subset of $G$.
nodes.name: Reference set $A$

nodes.statement: For any $G$-valued random variable $X$, we define $\rho^-(X)$ to be the infimum of $D_{KL}(X \Vert U_A + T)$, where $U_A$ is uniform on $A$ and $T$ ranges over $G$-valued random variables independent of $U_A$.
nodes.name: Rho minus
nodes.statement_short: rho^-(X): infimal KL divergence of X from U_A+T over independent T.
nodes.label: rhominus-def

nodes.statement: For any $G$-valued random variable $X$, we define $\rho^+(X) := \rho^-(X) + \bbH(X) - \bbH(U_A)$.
nodes.name: Rho plus
nodes.statement_short: rho^+(X) = rho^-(X) + H(X) - H(U_A).
nodes.label: rhoplus-def

nodes.statement: We have $\rho^-(X) \geq 0$.
nodes.name: Rho minus non-negative
nodes.label: rhominus-nonneg

nodes.statement: Clear from Lemma \ref{Conditional-Gibbs}.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho minus non-negative
nodes.statement_short: Conditional Gibbs inequality.

nodes.statement: If $H$ is a finite subgroup of $G$, then $\rho^-(U_H) = \log |A| - \log \max_t |A \cap (H+t)|$.
nodes.name: Rho minus of subgroup
nodes.statement_short: rho^- of a uniform subgroup variable equals log|A| minus log of the largest coset intersection.
assumptions: $H$ is a finite subgroup of $G$
nodes.label: rhominus-subgroup

nodes.statement: For every $G$-valued random variable $T$ that is independent of $Y$, $$D_{KL}(U_H \Vert U_A+T) = \sum_{h\in H} \frac{1}{|H|}\log\frac{1/|H|}{\mathbf{P}[U_A+T=h]}\ge -\log(\mathbf{P}[U_A+T\in H]),$$ by \Cref{log-sum}. Then observe that $$-\log(\mathbf{P}[U_A+T\in H])=-\log(\mathbf{P}[U_A\in H-T])\ge -\log(\max_{t\in G} \mathbf{P}[U_A\in H+t]).$$ This proves $\ge$. To get the equality, let $t^*:=\arg\max_t |A \cap (H+t)|$ and observe that $$\rho^-(U_H)\le D_{KL}(U_H \Vert U_A+(U_H-t^*))= \log |A| - \log \max_t|A \cap (H+t)|.$$
nodes.name: Proof of Rho minus of subgroup
nodes.statement_short: Log sum lower bound for every T, and equality via T = U_H - t*.

nodes.statement: If $H$ is a finite subgroup of $G$, then $\rho^+(U_H) = \log |H| - \log \max_t |A \cap (H+t)|$.
nodes.name: Rho plus of subgroup
nodes.statement_short: rho^+ of a uniform subgroup variable equals log|H| minus log of the largest coset intersection.
assumptions: $H$ is a finite subgroup of $G$
nodes.label: rhoplus-subgroup

nodes.statement: Straightforward by definition and \Cref{rhominus-subgroup}.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho plus of subgroup
nodes.statement_short: Definition and rho^- of a subgroup.

nodes.statement: We define $\rho(X) := (\rho^+(X) + \rho^-(X))/2$.
nodes.name: Rho functional
nodes.label: rho-def

nodes.statement: We have $\rho(U_A) = 0$.
nodes.name: Rho of uniform distribution on $A$
nodes.label: rho-init

nodes.statement: $\rho^-(U_A)\le 0$ by the choice $T=0$. The claim then follows from \Cref{rhominus-nonneg}.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho of uniform distribution on $A$
nodes.statement_short: T=0 gives rho^-(U_A) <= 0, then nonnegativity.

nodes.statement: If $H$ is a finite subgroup of $G$, and $\rho(U_H) \leq r$, then there exists $t$ such that $|A \cap (H+t)| \geq e^{-r} \sqrt{|A||H|}$, and $|H|/|A|\in[e^{-2r},e^{2r}]$.
nodes.name: Rho of subgroup
nodes.statement_short: Small rho(U_H) gives a large coset intersection of A and H and comparable sizes.
assumptions: $H$ is a finite subgroup of $G$, and $\rho(U_H) \leq r$
conclusions: there exists $t$ such that $|A \cap (H+t)| \geq e^{-r} \sqrt{|A||H|}$, and $|H|/|A|\in[e^{-2r},e^{2r}]$
nodes.label: rho-subgroup

nodes.statement: The first claim is a direct corollary of \Cref{rhominus-subgroup} and \Cref{rhoplus-subgroup}. To see the second claim, observe that \Cref{rhominus-nonneg} and \Cref{rhoplus-subgroup} imply $\rho^-(U_H),\rho^+(U_H)\ge 0$. Therefore $$|H(U_A)-H(U_H)|=|\rho^+(U_H)-\rho^-(U_H)|\le \rho^-(U_H)+\rho^+(U_H)= 2\rho(U_H)\le 2r,$$ which implies the second claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho of subgroup
nodes.statement_short: Combine the subgroup formulas for rho^- and rho^+ with nonnegativity.

nodes.statement: For any $s \in G$, $\rho(X+s) = \rho(X)$.
nodes.name: Rho invariant
nodes.label: rho-invariant

nodes.statement: Observe that by \Cref{kl-div-inj}, $$\inf_T D_{KL}(X\Vert U_A+T)=\inf_T D_{KL}(X+s\Vert U_A+T+s)=\inf_{T'} D_{KL}(X+s\Vert U_A+T').$$
nodes.name: Proof of Rho invariant
nodes.statement_short: Translation invariance of KL divergence under injections.

nodes.statement: $\rho(X)$ depends continuously on the distribution of $X$.
nodes.name: Rho continuous
conclusions: $\rho(X)$ depends continuously on the distribution of $X$
nodes.label: rho-cts

nodes.statement: Clear from definition.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho continuous
nodes.statement_short: Clear from definition.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are independent, one has $$ \rho^-(X+Y) \leq \rho^-(X)$$ $$ \rho^+(X+Y) \leq \rho^+(X) + \bbH[X+Y] - \bbH[X]$$ and $$ \rho(X+Y) \leq \rho(X) + \frac{1}{2}( \bbH[X+Y] - \bbH[X] ).$$
nodes.name: Rho and sums
nodes.statement_short: Rho functionals increase under independent sums by at most the entropy increase.
assumptions: $X,Y$ are independent
nodes.label: rho-sums

nodes.statement: The first inequality follows from \Cref{kl-sums}. The second and third inequalities are direct corollaries of the first.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho and sums
nodes.statement_short: KL divergence decreases under independent sums; the rest follows.

nodes.statement: We define $\rho(X|Y) := \sum_y {\bf P}(Y=y) \rho(X|Y=y)$.
nodes.name: Conditional Rho functional
nodes.label: rho-cond-def

nodes.statement: For any $s\in G$, $\rho(X+s|Y)=\rho(X|Y)$.
nodes.name: Conditional rho and translation
nodes.label: rho-cond-invariant

nodes.statement: Direct corollary of \Cref{rho-invariant}.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional rho and translation
nodes.statement_short: Direct from translation invariance of rho.

nodes.statement: If $f$ is injective, then $\rho(X|f(Y))=\rho(X|Y)$.
nodes.name: Conditional rho and relabeling
assumptions: $f$ is injective
nodes.label: rho-cond-relabeled

nodes.statement: Clear from the definition.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional rho and relabeling
nodes.statement_short: Clear from the definition.

nodes.statement: If $X,Z$ are defined on the same space, one has $$ \rho^-(X|Z) \leq \rho^-(X) + \bbH[X] - \bbH[X|Z]$$ $$ \rho^+(X|Z) \leq \rho^+(X)$$ and $$ \rho(X|Z) \leq \rho(X) + \frac{1}{2}( \bbH[X] - \bbH[X|Z] ).$$
nodes.name: Rho and conditioning
nodes.statement_short: Rho functionals under conditioning are bounded by the entropy loss.
assumptions: $X,Z$ are defined on the same space
nodes.label: rho-cond

nodes.statement: The first inequality follows from \Cref{kl-cond}. The second and third inequalities are direct corollaries of the first.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho and conditioning
nodes.statement_short: KL divergence under conditioning; the rest follows.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are independent, then $$ \rho(X+Y) \leq \frac{1}{2}(\rho(X)+\rho(Y) + d[X;Y]).$$
nodes.name: Rho and sums, symmetrized
nodes.statement_short: rho(X+Y) is at most the average of rho(X), rho(Y) and d[X;Y].
assumptions: $X,Y$ are independent
nodes.label: rho-sums-sym

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{rho-sums} for $(X,Y)$ and $(Y,X)$ and take their average.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho and sums, symmetrized
nodes.statement_short: Average rho-and-sums over both orders.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are independent, then $$ \rho(X | X+Y) \leq \frac{1}{2}(\rho(X)+\rho(Y) + d[X;Y]).$$
nodes.name: Rho and conditioning, symmetrized
nodes.statement_short: rho(X|X+Y) is at most the average of rho(X), rho(Y) and d[X;Y].
assumptions: $X,Y$ are independent
nodes.label: rho-cond-sym

nodes.statement: First apply \Cref{rho-cond} to get $\rho(X|X+Y)\le \rho(X) + \frac{1}{2}(\bbH[X+Y]-\bbH[Y])$, and $\rho(Y|X+Y)\le \rho(Y)+\frac{1}{2}(\bbH[X+Y]-\bbH[X])$. Then apply \Cref{rho-invariant} to get $\rho(Y|X+Y)=\rho(X|X+Y)$ and take the average of the two inequalities.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho and conditioning, symmetrized
nodes.statement_short: Apply rho-and-conditioning to both variables, use translation invariance, and average.

nodes.statement: Set $\eta < 1/8$.
nodes.name: $\eta < 1/8$

nodes.statement: Given $G$-valued random variables $X,Y$, define $$ \phi[X;Y] := d[X;Y] + \eta(\rho(X) + \rho(Y))$$ and define a \emph{$\phi$-minimizer} to be a pair of random variables $X,Y$ which minimizes $\phi[X;Y]$.
nodes.name: $\phi$ functional and $\phi$-minimizer
nodes.statement_short: phi[X;Y] = d[X;Y] + eta(rho(X)+rho(Y)); a phi-minimizer minimizes it.
nodes.label: phi-min-def

nodes.statement: There exists a $\phi$-minimizer.
nodes.name: $\phi$-minimizers exist
nodes.label: phi-min-exist

nodes.statement: Clear from compactness.
nodes.name: Proof of $\phi$-minimizers exist
nodes.statement_short: Compactness.

nodes.statement: Let $(X_1, X_2)$ be a $\phi$-minimizer, and $\tilde X_1, \tilde X_2$ be independent copies of $X_1,X_2$ respectively.
nodes.name: $\phi$-minimizer $(X_1,X_2)$ and copies

nodes.statement: Similar to the original proof we define $$ I_1 := I [X_1+X_2 : \tilde X_1 + X_2 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2], I_2 := \bbI[X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2].$$
nodes.name: $I_1, I_2$ for $\phi$-minimizers

nodes.statement: Similar to \Cref{first-estimate}: get upper bounds for $d[X_1;X_2]$ by $\phi[X_1;X_2]\le \phi[X_1+X_2;\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2]$ and $\phi[X_1;X_2]\le \phi[X_1|X_1+X_2;\tilde X_2|\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2]$, and then apply \Cref{first-fibre} to get an upper bound for $I_1$.
nodes.name: Proof of First estimate for $\phi$-minimizers
nodes.statement_short: As in the first estimate, using phi-minimality and the first fibring identity.

nodes.statement: Compare \Cref{first-fibre} with the identity obtained from applying \Cref{cor-fibre} on $(X_1,\tilde X_1, X_2, \tilde X_2)$.
nodes.name: Proof of Identity relating $I_1$, $I_2$ and self-distances
nodes.statement_short: Compare two instances of the specific fibring identity.

nodes.statement: $I_2\le 2\eta d[X_1;X_2] + \frac{\eta}{1-\eta}(2\eta d[X_1;X_2]-I_1)$.
nodes.name: Second estimate for $\phi$-minimizers
nodes.label: phi-second-estimate

nodes.statement: First of all, by $\phi[X_1;X_2]\le \phi[X_1+\tilde X_1;X_2+\tilde X_2]$, $\phi[X_1;X_2]\le \phi[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1;X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2]$, and the fibring identity obtained by applying \Cref{cor-fibre} on $(X_1,X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2)$, we have $I_2\le \eta (d[X_1;X_1]+d[X_2;X_2])$. Then apply \Cref{I1-I2-diff} to get $I_2\le 2\eta d[X_1;X_2] +\eta(I_2-I_1)$, and rearrange.
nodes.name: Proof of Second estimate for $\phi$-minimizers
nodes.statement_short: phi-minimality with the fibring identity, then the I_1-I_2 identity and rearranging.

nodes.statement: If $G$-valued random variables $T_1,T_2,T_3$ satisfy $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$, then $$d[X_1;X_2]\le 3\bbI[T_1:T_2] + (2\bbH[T_3]-\bbH[T_1]-\bbH[T_2])+ \eta(\rho(T_1|T_3)+\rho(T_2|T_3)-\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2)).$$
nodes.name: BSG bound with rho for a zero-sum triple
nodes.statement_short: For a zero-sum triple, d[X_1;X_2] is bounded via BSG plus eta times rho increments.
assumptions: $G$-valued random variables $T_1,T_2,T_3$ satisfy $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$
nodes.label: rho-BSG-triplet

nodes.statement: Conditioned on every $T_3=t$, $d[X_1;X_2]\le d[T_1|T_3=t;T_2|T_3=t]+\eta(\rho(T_1|T_3=t)+\rho(T_2|T_3=t)-\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2))$ by \Cref{phi-min-def}. Then take the weighted average with weight $\mathbf{P}(T_3=t)$ and then apply \Cref{entropic-bsg} to bound the RHS.
nodes.name: Proof of BSG bound with rho for a zero-sum triple
nodes.statement_short: phi-minimality conditioned on T_3, averaged, then entropic BSG.

nodes.statement: If $G$-valued random variables $T_1,T_2,T_3$ satisfy $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$, then $$d[X_1;X_2] \leq \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} \bbI[T_i:T_j] + \frac{\eta}{3} \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j) + \rho(T_j|T_i) -\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2))$$
nodes.name: Symmetrized BSG bound with rho for a zero-sum triple
nodes.statement_short: Permutation-averaged version of the rho BSG triplet bound.
assumptions: $G$-valued random variables $T_1,T_2,T_3$ satisfy $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$
nodes.label: rho-BSG-triplet-symmetrized

nodes.statement: Take the average of \Cref{rho-BSG-triplet} over all $6$ permutations of $T_1,T_2,T_3$.
nodes.name: Proof of Symmetrized BSG bound with rho for a zero-sum triple
nodes.statement_short: Average over permutations of T_1,T_2,T_3.

nodes.statement: For independent random variables $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4$ over $G$, define $S:=Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4$, $T_1:=Y_1+Y_2$, $T_2:=Y_1+Y_3$. Then $$\rho(T_1|T_2,S)+\rho(T_2|T_1,S) - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i} \rho(Y_i)\le \frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1;Y_2]+d[Y_3;Y_4]+d[Y_1;Y_3]+d[Y_2;Y_4]).$$
nodes.name: Rho increment bound for four independent variables
nodes.statement_short: Conditional rho of pairwise sums of four independent variables bounded by Ruzsa distances.
conclusions: For independent random variables $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4$ over $G$, define $S:=Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4$, $T_1:=Y_1+Y_2$, $T_2:=Y_1+Y_3$. Then $$\rho(T_1|T_2,S)+\rho(T_2|T_1,S) - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i} \rho(Y_i)\le \frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1;Y_2]+d[Y_3;Y_4]+d[Y_1;Y_3]+d[Y_2;Y_4]).$$
nodes.label: rho-increase

nodes.statement: Let $T_1':=Y_3+Y_4$, $T_2':=Y_2+Y_4$. First note that \begin{align*} \rho(T_1|T_2,S) &\le \rho(T_1|S) + \frac{1}{2}\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S) \\ &\le \frac{1}{2}(\rho(T_1)+\rho(T_1'))+\frac{1}{2}(d[T_1;T_1']+\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S)) \\ &\le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_2]+d[Y_3;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[T_1;T_1']+\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S)). \end{align*} by \Cref{rho-cond}, \Cref{rho-cond-sym}, \Cref{rho-sums-sym} respectively. On the other hand, observe that \begin{align*} \rho(T_1|T_2,S) &=\rho(Y_1+Y_2|T_2,T_2') \\ &\le \frac{1}{2}(\rho(Y_1|T_2)+\rho(Y_2|T_2'))+\frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1|T_2;Y_2|T_2']) \\ &\le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_3]+d[Y_2;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1|T_2;Y_2|T_2']). \end{align*} by \Cref{rho-cond-relabeled}, \Cref{rho-sums-sym}, \Cref{rho-cond-sym} respectively. By replacing $(Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4)$ with $(Y_1,Y_3,Y_2,Y_4)$ in the above inequalities, one has $$\rho(T_2|T_1,S) \le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_3]+d[Y_2;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[T_2;T_2']+\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S))$$ and $$\rho(T_2|T_1,S) \le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_2]+d[Y_3;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1|T_1;Y_3|T_1']).$$ Finally, take the sum of all four inequalities, apply \Cref{cor-fibre} on $(Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4)$ and $(Y_1,Y_3,Y_2,Y_4)$ to rewrite the sum of last terms in the four inequalities, and divide the result by $2$.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho increment bound for four independent variables
nodes.statement_short: Two chains of rho inequalities for each term, symmetrized and combined via the fibring identity.

nodes.statement: For independent random variables $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4$ over $G$, define $T_1:=Y_1+Y_2,T_2:=Y_1+Y_3,T_3:=Y_2+Y_3$ and $S:=Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4$. Then $$\sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i} \rho(Y_i))\le \sum_{1\leq i < j \leq 4}d[Y_i;Y_j]$$
nodes.name: Symmetrized rho increment bound
nodes.statement_short: Sum over pairs of conditional rho increments bounded by all pairwise Ruzsa distances.
conclusions: For independent random variables $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4$ over $G$, define $T_1:=Y_1+Y_2,T_2:=Y_1+Y_3,T_3:=Y_2+Y_3$ and $S:=Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4$. Then $$\sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i} \rho(Y_i))\le \sum_{1\leq i < j \leq 4}d[Y_i;Y_j]$$
nodes.label: rho-increase-symmetrized

nodes.statement: Apply Lemma \ref{rho-increase} on $(Y_i,Y_j,Y_k,Y_4)$ for $(i,j,k)=(1,2,3),(2,3,1),(1,3,2)$, and take the sum.
nodes.name: Proof of Symmetrized rho increment bound
nodes.statement_short: Sum the rho increment bound over three orderings.

nodes.statement: If $X_1,X_2$ is a $\phi$-minimizer, then $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
nodes.name: $\phi$-minimizers have zero distance
assumptions: $X_1,X_2$ is a $\phi$-minimizer
nodes.label: phi-minimizer-zero-distance

nodes.statement: Consider $T_1:=X_1+X_2,T_2:=X_1+\tilde X_1, T_3:=\tilde X_1 + X_2$, and $S=X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2$. Note that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$. First apply \Cref{rho-BSG-triplet-symmetrized} on $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ when conditioned on $S$ to get \begin{align} d[X_1;X_2] &\leq \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} \bbI[T_i:T_j\mid S] + \frac{\eta}{3} \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) -\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2))\nonumber\\ &= (I_1+2I_2) + \frac{\eta}{3} \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) -\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2)). \end{align} Then apply \Cref{rho-increase-symmetrized} on $(X_1,X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2)$ and get $$\sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) - \rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2))\le (4d[X_1;X_2]+d[X_1;X_2]+d[X_2;X_2])= 6 d[X_1;X_2]+(I_2-I_1)$$ by \Cref{I1-I2-diff}. Plug in the inequality above to (\ref{eq:further-bsg}), we get $$d[X_1;X_2] \le (I_1+2I_2)+2\eta d[X_1;X_2]+\frac{\eta}{3}(I_2-I_1).$$ By \Cref{phi-second-estimate} we can conclude that $$d[X_1;X_2] \le 8\eta d[X_1;X_2]-\frac{3-10\eta}{3-3\eta} (2\eta d[X_1;X_2]-I_1).$$ Finally by \Cref{phi-first-estimate} and $\eta<1$ we get that the second term is $\le 0$, and thus $d[X_1;X_2] \le 8\eta d[X_1;X_2]$. By the choice $\eta<1/8$ and the non-negativity of $d$ we have $d[X_1;X_2]=0$.
nodes.name: Proof of $\phi$-minimizers have zero distance
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrized rho-BSG bound plus the rho increment bound yields d <= 8 eta d. The key step applies both to the triple (X_1+X_2, X_1+X~_1, X~_1+X_2) conditioned on S.

nodes.statement: d[X_1;X_2] &\leq \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} \bbI[T_i:T_j\mid S] + \frac{\eta}{3} \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) -\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2))\nonumber\\ &= (I_1+2I_2) + \frac{\eta}{3} \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) -\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2)).
nodes.name: Equation (7.1)
nodes.label: eq:further-bsg

nodes.statement: For any random variables $Y_1,Y_2$, there exist a subgroup $H$ such that $$ 2\rho(U_H) \leq \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + 8 d[Y_1;Y_2].$$
nodes.name: Rho form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Some subgroup H has 2 rho(U_H) <= rho(Y_1)+rho(Y_2)+8 d[Y_1;Y_2].
conclusions: For any random variables $Y_1,Y_2$, there exist a subgroup $H$ such that $$ 2\rho(U_H) \leq \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + 8 d[Y_1;Y_2].$$
nodes.label: pfr-rho

nodes.statement: Let $X_1,X_2$ be a $\phi$-minimizer. By \Cref{phi-minimizer-zero-distance} $d[X_1;X_2]=0$, which by \Cref{phi-min-def} implies $\rho(X_1)+\rho(X_2)\le \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + \frac{1}{\eta} d[Y_1;Y_2]$ for every $\eta<1/8$. Take the limit at $\eta=1/8$ to get $\rho(X_1)+\rho(X_2)\le \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + 8 d[Y_1;Y_2]$. By \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} and \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg} we have $d[X_1;X_1]=d[X_2;X_2]=0$, and by \Cref{sym-zero} there are $H_1:=\mathrm{Sym}[X_1],H_2:=\mathrm{Sym}[X_2]$ such that $X_1=U_{H_1}+x_1$ and $X_2=U_{H_2}+x_2$ for some $x_2$. By \Cref{rho-invariant} we get $\rho(U_{H_1})+\rho(U_{H_2})\le \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + 8 d[Y_1;Y_2]$, and thus the claim holds for $H=H_1$ or $H=H_2$.
nodes.name: Proof of Rho form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Take a phi-minimizer, use zero distance, let eta -> 1/8, and identify minimizers with uniform subgroup translates.

nodes.statement: If $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then there exists a subgroup $H$ and $t\in G$ such that $|A \cap (H+t)| \geq K^{-4} \sqrt{|A||H|}$, and $|H|/|A|\in[K^{-8},K^8]$.
nodes.name: Large intersection with a subgroup coset
nodes.statement_short: Small doubling gives a subgroup H of comparable size with a large coset intersection with A.
assumptions: $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: there exists a subgroup $H$ and $t\in G$ such that $|A \cap (H+t)| \geq K^{-4} \sqrt{|A||H|}$, and $|H|/|A|\in[K^{-8},K^8]$
nodes.label: pfr-9-aux

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{pfr-rho} on $U_A,U_A$ to get a subspace such that $2\rho(U_H)\le 2\rho(U_A)+8d[U_A;U_A]$. Recall that $d[U_A;U_A]\le \log K$ as proved in \Cref{pfr_aux}, and $\rho(U_A)=0$ by \Cref{rho-init}. Therefore $\rho(U_H)\le 4\log(K)$. The claim then follows from \Cref{rho-subgroup}.
nodes.name: Proof of Large intersection with a subgroup coset
nodes.statement_short: Apply the rho form of PFR to U_A and convert via rho of subgroups.

nodes.statement: If $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then there exist a subgroup $H$ and a subset $c$ of $G$ with $A \subseteq c + H$, such that $|c| \leq K^{5} |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ and $|H|/|A|\in[K^{-8},K^8]$.
nodes.name: Covering by translates of a subgroup (rho version)
nodes.statement_short: Small doubling A is covered by few translates of a comparable subgroup.
assumptions: $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: there exist a subgroup $H$ and a subset $c$ of $G$ with $A \subseteq c + H$, such that $|c| \leq K^{5} |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ and $|H|/|A|\in[K^{-8},K^8]$
nodes.label: pfr-9-aux'

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{pfr-9-aux} and \Cref{ruz-cov} to get the result, as in the proof of \Cref{pfr_aux}.
nodes.name: Proof of Covering by translates of a subgroup (rho version)
nodes.statement_short: Large coset intersection plus the Ruzsa covering lemma.

nodes.statement: If $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is finite non-empty with $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then there exists a subgroup $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $|H| \leq |A|$ such that $A$ can be covered by at most $2K^9$ translates of $H$.
nodes.name: PFR with $C=9$
nodes.statement_short: PFR with exponent 9: A is covered by at most 2K^9 translates of a subgroup no larger than A.
assumptions: $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is finite non-empty with $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: there exists a subgroup $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $|H| \leq |A|$ such that $A$ can be covered by at most $2K^9$ translates of $H$
nodes.label: pfr-9

nodes.statement: Given \Cref{pfr-9-aux'}, the proof is the same as that of \Cref{pfr}.
nodes.name: Proof of PFR with \texorpdfstring{$C=9$}{C=9}
nodes.statement_short: Same as the proof of PFR, using the rho covering lemma.

nodes.statement: In this section, $G, G'$ are finite abelian $2$-groups.
nodes.name: $G, G'$ finite abelian $2$-groups

nodes.statement: Let $H_0$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then every homomorphism $\phi: H_0 \to G'$ can be extended to a homomorphism $\tilde \phi: G \to G'$.
nodes.name: Hahn-Banach type theorem
assumptions: $H_0$ be a subgroup of $G$
conclusions: every homomorphism $\phi: H_0 \to G'$ can be extended to a homomorphism $\tilde \phi: G \to G'$
nodes.label: hb-thm

nodes.statement: By induction it suffices to treat the case where $H_0$ has index $2$ in $G$, but then the extension can be constructed by hand.
nodes.name: Proof of Hahn-Banach type theorem
nodes.statement_short: Induction on index, extending across index-2 subgroups by hand.

nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G \times G'$. Then there exists a subgroup $H_0$ of $G$, a subgroup $H_1$ of $G'$, and a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ such that $$ H := \{ (x, \phi(x) + y): x \in H_0, y \in H_1 \}.$$ In particular, $|H| = |H_0| |H_1|$.
nodes.name: Goursat type theorem
nodes.statement_short: Subgroups of G x G' are graphs of homomorphisms over a subgroup, plus a fibre subgroup.
assumptions: $H$ be a subgroup of $G \times G'$
conclusions: there exists a subgroup $H_0$ of $G$, a subgroup $H_1$ of $G'$, and a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ such that $$ H := \{ (x, \phi(x) + y): x \in H_0, y \in H_1 \}.$$ In particular, $|H| = |H_0| |H_1|$
nodes.label: goursat

nodes.statement: We can take $H_0$ to be the projection of $H$ to $G$, and $H_1$ to be the slice $H_1 := \{ y: (0,y) \in H \}$. One can construct $\phi$ on $H_0$ one generator at a time by the greedy algorithm, and then extend to $G$ by \Cref{hb-thm}. The cardinality bound is clear from direct counting.
nodes.name: Proof of Goursat type theorem
nodes.statement_short: Projection and slice subgroups; construct phi greedily and extend by Hahn-Banach.

nodes.statement: Let $f: G \to G'$ be a function, and let $S$ denote the set $$ S := \{ f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y): x,y \in G \}.$$ Then there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ such that $$ |\{ f(x) - \phi(x): x \in G \}| \leq |S|^{10}.$$
nodes.name: Homomorphism form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Every function between finite 2-groups is a homomorphism up to at most |S|^10 values, S the set of additive errors.
conclusions: Let $f: G \to G'$ be a function, and let $S$ denote the set $$ S := \{ f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y): x,y \in G \}.$$ Then there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ such that $$ |\{ f(x) - \phi(x): x \in G \}| \leq |S|^{10}.$$
nodes.label: hom-pfr

nodes.statement: Consider the graph $A \subset G \times G'$ defined by $$ A := \{ (x,f(x)): x \in G \}.$$ Clearly, $|A| = |G|$. By hypothesis, we have $$ A+A \subset \{ (x,f(x)+s): x \in G, s \in S\}$$ and hence $|A+A| \leq |S| |A|$. Applying \Cref{pfr-9-aux'}, we may find a subspace $H \subset G \times G'$ such that $|H|/ |A| \in [|S|^{-8}, |S|^{8}]$ and $A$ is covered by $c + H$ with $|c| \le |S|^5|A|^{1/2} / |H|^{1/2}$. If we let $H_0, H_1$ be as in \Cref{goursat}, this implies on taking projections that $G$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H_0$. This implies that $$ |c| |H_0| \geq |G|;$$ since $|H_0| |H_1| = |H|$, we conclude that $$ |H_1| \leq |c| |H|/|G| = |c| |H|/|A|.$$ By hypothesis, $A$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H$, and hence by at most $|c| |H_1|$ translates of $\{ (x,\phi(x)): x \in G \}$. As $\phi$ is a homomorphism, each such translate can be written in the form $\{ (x,\phi(x)+d): x \in G \}$ for some $d \in G'$. Since $$ |c| |H_1| \le |c|^2 \frac{|H|}{|A|} \le \left(|S|^5 \frac{|A|^{1/2}}{|H|^{1/2}}\right)^2 \frac{|H|}{|A|} = |S|^{10}, $$ the result follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Homomorphism form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Apply PFR covering to the graph of f and use Goursat to extract a homomorphism.

nodes.statement: $\eta$ is a real parameter with $\eta > 0$.
nodes.name: New definition of $\eta$
nodes.label: eta-def-new

nodes.statement: Previously in \Cref{eta-def} we had set $\eta=1/9$. To implement this chapter, one should refactor the previous arguments so that $\eta$ is now free to be a positive number, though the specific hypothesis $\eta=1/9$ would now need to be added to \Cref{de-prop}.
nodes.name: Refactoring $\eta$

nodes.statement: Let $X^0_1, X^0_2$ be $G$-valued random variables, and let $X_1, X_2$ be $\tau$-minimizers as defined in \Cref{tau-min-def}.
nodes.name: $\tau$-minimizers for the improved argument

nodes.statement: One has \begin{align*} k \leq \delta + \eta (& d[X^0_1;T_1|T_3]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2|T_3]-d[X^0_2;X_2]). \end{align*}
nodes.name: Constructing good variables, I'
nodes.statement_short: Variant of the zero-sum triple bound with conditional reference distances.
nodes.label: construct-good-prelim-improv

nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{entropic-bsg} with $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there. Since $T_1 + T_2 = T_3$, the conclusion is that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] & d[(T_1 | T_3 = t_3); (T_2 | T_3 = t_3)] \\ & \leq 3 \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + 2 \bbH[T_3] - \bbH[T_1] - \bbH[T_2]. \end{align} The right-hand side in~\eqref{bsg-t1t2'} can be rearranged as \begin{align*} & 2( \bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - 3 \bbH[T_1,T_2] \\ & = 2(\bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - \bbH[T_1,T_2] - \bbH[T_2,T_3] - \bbH[T_1, T_3] = \delta,\end{align*} using the fact (from \Cref{relabeled-entropy}) that all three terms $\bbH[T_i,T_j]$ are equal to $\bbH[T_1,T_2,T_3]$ and hence to each other. We also have \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} P[T_3 = t_3] \bigl(d[X^0_1; (T_1 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_1;X_1]\bigr) \\ &\quad = d[X^0_1; T_1 | T_3] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \end{align*} and similarly \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] (d[X^0_2;(T_2 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_2; X_2]) \\ &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \leq d[X^0_2;T_2|T_3] - d[X^0_2;X_2]. \end{align*} Putting the above observations together, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3=t_3] \psi[(T_1 | T_3=t_3); (T_2 | T_3=t_3)] \leq \delta + \eta (d[X^0_1;T_1|T_3]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) \\ + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2|T_3]-d[X^0_2;X_2]) \end{align*} where we introduce the notation \[\psi[Y_1; Y_2] := d[Y_1;Y_2] + \eta (d[X_1^0;Y_1] - d[X_1^0;X_1]) + \eta(d[X_2^0;Y_2] - d[X_2^0;X_2]).\] On the other hand, from \Cref{distance-lower} we have $k \leq \psi[Y_1;Y_2]$, and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Constructing good variables, I'
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG on (T_1,T_2) and minimality via psi, keeping conditional distances.

nodes.statement: (One could in fact refactor \Cref{construct-good-prelim} to follow from \Cref{construct-good-prelim-improv} and \Cref{cond-dist-fact})
nodes.name: Possible refactoring

nodes.statement: One has \begin{align*} k & \leq \delta + \frac{\eta}{6} \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{1 \leq j,l \leq 3; j \neq l} (d[X^0_i;T_j|T_l] - d[X^0_i; X_i]) \end{align*}
nodes.name: Constructing good variables, II'
nodes.statement_short: Permutation-averaged variant bound on k.
conclusions: \begin{align*} k & \leq \delta + \frac{\eta}{6} \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{1 \leq j,l \leq 3; j \neq l} (d[X^0_i;T_j|T_l] - d[X^0_i; X_i]) \end{align*}
nodes.label: construct-good-improv

nodes.statement: Average \Cref{construct-good-prelim-improv} over all six permutations of $T_1,T_2,T_3$.
nodes.name: Proof of Constructing good variables, II'
nodes.statement_short: Average over permutations.

nodes.statement: Now let $X_1, X_2, \tilde X_1, \tilde X_2$ be independent copies of $X_1, X_2, X_1, X_2$, and set \[U := X_1 + X_2, \qquad V := \tilde X_1 + X_2, \qquad W := X_1 + \tilde X_1\] and \[ S := X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2\] and introduce the quantities $$ k = d[X_1;X_2]$$ and $$ I_1 = I(U : V \, | \, S).$$
nodes.name: $U,V,W,S,k,I_1$ for the improved argument

nodes.statement: One has \begin{align*} k & \leq I(U : V \, | \, S) + I(V : W \, | \,S) + I(W : U \, | \, S) + \frac{\eta}{6} \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} (d[X^0_i;A|B,S] - d[X^0_i; X_i]). \end{align*}
nodes.name: Constructing good variables, III'
nodes.statement_short: k bounded by the three conditional mutual informations of U,V,W plus distance increments.
conclusions: \begin{align*} k & \leq I(U : V \, | \, S) + I(V : W \, | \,S) + I(W : U \, | \, S) + \frac{\eta}{6} \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} (d[X^0_i;A|B,S] - d[X^0_i; X_i]). \end{align*}
nodes.label: averaged-construct-good

nodes.statement: For each $s$ in the range of $S$, apply \Cref{construct-good-improv} with $T_1,T_2,T_3$ equal to $(U|S=s)$, $(V|S=s)$, $(W|S=s)$ respectively (which works thanks to \Cref{key-ident}), multiply by $\bbP[S=s]$, and sum in $s$ to conclude.
nodes.name: Proof of Constructing good variables, III'
nodes.statement_short: Apply to (U,V,W) conditioned on S=s and average.

nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4$ be independent $G$-valued random variables, and let $Y$ be another $G$-valued random variable. Set $S := X_1+X_2+X_3+X_4$. Then \begin{align*} & d[Y; X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] - d[Y; X_1] \\ &\quad \leq \tfrac{1}{4} (d[X_1;X_2] + 2d[X_1;X_3] + d[X_2;X_4])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (d[X_1|X_1+X_3;X_2|X_2+X_4] - d[X_3|X_3+X_4; X_1|X_1+X_2])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{8} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4] + \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[X_3]\\ &\qquad \qquad \qquad + \bbH[X_2|X_2+X_4] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_3]). \end{align*}
nodes.name: General inequality
nodes.statement_short: General bound on d[Y; X_1+X_2 | X_1+X_3, S] - d[Y;X_1] for four independent variables.
assumptions: $X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4$ be independent $G$-valued random variables, and let $Y$ be another $G$-valued random variable. Set $S := X_1+X_2+X_3+X_4$
conclusions: \begin{align*} & d[Y; X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] - d[Y; X_1] \\ &\quad \leq \tfrac{1}{4} (d[X_1;X_2] + 2d[X_1;X_3] + d[X_2;X_4])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (d[X_1|X_1+X_3;X_2|X_2+X_4] - d[X_3|X_3+X_4; X_1|X_1+X_2])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{8} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4] + \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[X_3]\\ &\qquad \qquad \qquad + \bbH[X_2|X_2+X_4] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_3]). \end{align*}
nodes.label: gen-ineq

nodes.statement: On the one hand, by \Cref{cond-dist-fact} and two applications of \Cref{first-useful} we have \begin{align*} &d[Y;X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1+X_2|S] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[X_1 + X_2 : X_1 + X_3|S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1+X_2]\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1+X_2;X_3+X_4] + \bbI[X_1 + X_2 : X_1 + X_3|S])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4])\\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1;X_2] + d[X_1+X_2;X_3+X_4] + \bbI[X_1 + X_2 : X_1 + X_3|S])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4] + \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[X_1]). \end{align*} From \Cref{cor-fibre} (with $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4$ set equal to $X_3, X_1, X_4, X_2$ respectively) one has $$ d[X_3+X_4; X_1+X_2] + d[X_3|X_3+X_4; X_1|X_1+X_2] $$ $$ + \bbI[X_3 + X_1 : X_1 + X_2|S] = d[X_3;X_1] + d[X_4;X_2].$$ Rearranging the mutual information and Ruzsa distances slightly, we conclude that \begin{align*} &d[Y;X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1;X_2] + d[X_1;X_3] + d[X_2;X_4] - d[X_3|X_3+X_4; X_1|X_1+X_2])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4] + \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[X_1]). \end{align*} On the other hand, $(X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S)$ has an identical distribution to the independent sum of $(X_1|X_1+X_3)$ and $(X_2|X_2+X_4)$. We may therefore apply \Cref{first-useful} to conditioned variables $(X_1|X_1+X_3=s)$ and $(X_2|X_2+X_4=t)$ and average in $s,t$ to obtain the alternative bound \begin{align*} & d[Y;X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1|X_1+X_3] + \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_1|X_1+X_3; X_2|X_2+X_4] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_2|X_2+X_4] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_3]) \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1;X_3] + d[X_1|X_1+X_3;X_2|X_2+X_4])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_2|X_2+X_4] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_3] + \bbH[X_1] - \bbH[X_3]). \end{align*} If one takes the arithmetic mean of these two bounds and simplifies using \Cref{cor-fibre}, one obtains the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of General inequality
nodes.statement_short: Two bounds: one via conditional distance and fibring, one via conditioned sums; take their mean.

nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} &\sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} d[X_i^0;A|B, S] - d[X_i^0;X_i]\\ &\qquad \leq 12 k + \frac{4(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \end{align*}
nodes.name: Bound on distance differences
nodes.statement_short: Summed conditional distance increments bounded by 12k plus a multiple of 2 eta k - I_1.
conclusions: \begin{align*} &\sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} d[X_i^0;A|B, S] - d[X_i^0;X_i]\\ &\qquad \leq 12 k + \frac{4(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \end{align*}
nodes.label: dist-diff-bound

nodes.statement: If we apply \Cref{gen-ineq} with $X_1:=X_1$, $Y:=X_1^0$ and $(X_2,X_3,X_4)$ equal to the $3!$ permutations of $(X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2)$, and sums (using the symmetry $\bbH[X|X+Y] = \bbH[Y|X+Y]$, which follows from \Cref{relabeled-entropy-cond}), we can bound $$ \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} d[X_1^0;A|B, S] - d[X_1^0;X_1]$$ by \begin{align*} &\quad \tfrac{1}{4} (6d[X_1;X_2] + 6d[X_1;\tilde X_2]\\ &\qquad + 6d[X_1;\tilde X_1] + 2d[\tilde X_1;\tilde X_2] + 2 d[\tilde X_1;X_2] + 2d[X_2;\tilde X_2])\\ &\quad + \tfrac{1}{8} (2\bbH[X_1+X_2] + 2\bbH[X_1+\tilde X_1] + 2 \bbH[X_1+\tilde X_2] \\ &\qquad - 2\bbH[\tilde X_1+X_2] - 2\bbH[X_2+\tilde X_2] - 2\bbH[\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] + \bbH[\tilde X_1|\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] + \bbH[\tilde X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2] \\ &\qquad \qquad \qquad - \bbH[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2]), \end{align*} which simplifies to \begin{align*} &\quad \tfrac{1}{4} (16k + 6d[X_1;X_1] + 2d[X_2;X_2])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (H[X_1+\tilde X_1] - H[X_2+\tilde X_2] + d[X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] - d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1]). \end{align*} A symmetric argument also bounds $$ \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} d[X_2^0;A|B, S] - d[X_2^0;X_2]$$ by \begin{align*} &\quad \tfrac{1}{4} (16k + 6d[X_2;X_2] + 2d[X_1;X_1])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (H[X_2+\tilde X_2] - H[X_1+\tilde X_1] + d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1] - d[X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2]). \end{align*} On the other hand, from \Cref{second-estimate-aux} one has $$ d[X_1;X_1] + d[X_2;X_2] \leq 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}.$$ Summing the previous three estimates, we obtain the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Bound on distance differences
nodes.statement_short: Apply the general inequality over permutations for both reference variables and add the self-distance bound.

nodes.statement: Suppose $0 < \eta < 1/8$. Let $X_1, X_2$ be tau-minimizers. Then $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
nodes.name: Improved $\tau$-decrement
assumptions: $0 < \eta < 1/8$. Let $X_1, X_2$ be tau-minimizers
nodes.label: de-prop-improv

nodes.statement: From \Cref{averaged-construct-good}, \Cref{dist-diff-bound}, and \Cref{uvw-s} one has \[ k \leq 8\eta k - \frac{(1 -5 \eta - \frac{4}{6} \eta)(2 \eta k - I_1)}{(1-\eta)}.\] For any $\eta < 1/8$, we see from \Cref{first-estimate} that the expression $\frac{(1 -5 \eta - \frac{4}{6} \eta)(2 \eta k - I_1)}{(1-\eta)}$ is nonnegative, and hence $k = 0$ as required.
nodes.name: Proof of Improved $\tau$-decrement
nodes.statement_short: Combine the averaged construction with the distance-difference bound and the mutual information bound.

nodes.statement: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
nodes.name: Limiting improved $\tau$-decrement
conclusions: For $\eta = 1/8$, there exist tau-minimizers $X_1, X_2$ satisfying $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$
nodes.label: de-prop-lim-improv

nodes.statement: For each $\eta<1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta$ and $X_2^\eta$ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta; X_2^\eta]=0$. By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta$ and $X_2^\eta$ as $\eta \to 1/8$. By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
nodes.name: Proof of Limiting improved $\tau$-decrement
nodes.statement_short: Compactness: take limits of minimizers as eta -> 1/8.

nodes.statement: Let $G = \F_2^n$, and suppose that $X^0_1, X^0_2$ are $G$-valued random variables. Then there is some subgroup $H \leq G$ such that \[ d[X^0_1;U_H] + d[X^0_2;U_H] \le 10 d[X^0_1;X^0_2], \] where $U_H$ is uniformly distributed on $H$. Furthermore, both $d[X^0_1;U_H]$ and $d[X^0_2;U_H]$ are at most $\tfrac{11}{2} d[X^0_1;X^0_2]$.
nodes.name: Improved entropy version of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Improved entropic PFR with constant 10.
assumptions: $G = \F_2^n$, and suppose that $X^0_1, X^0_2$ are $G$-valued random variables
conclusions: there is some subgroup $H \leq G$ such that \[ d[X^0_1;U_H] + d[X^0_2;U_H] \le 10 d[X^0_1;X^0_2], \] where $U_H$ is uniformly distributed on $H$. Furthermore, both $d[X^0_1;U_H]$ and $d[X^0_2;U_H]$ are at most $\tfrac{11}{2} d[X^0_1;X^0_2]$
nodes.label: entropy-pfr-improv

nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2$ be the good $\tau$-minimizer from \Cref{de-prop-lim-improv}. By construction, $d[X_1;X_2]=0$. From \Cref{lem:100pc}, $d[X_1;U_H] = d[X_2; U_H] = 0$. Also from $\tau$-minimization we have $\tau[X_1;X_2] \leq \tau[X^0_2;X^0_1]$. Using this and the Ruzsa triangle inequality we can conclude.
nodes.name: Proof of Improved entropy version of PFR
nodes.statement_short: As for entropic PFR, using the limiting tau-decrement.

nodes.statement: If $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then $A$ can be covered by at most $K^6 |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $$ |H|/|A| \in [K^{-10}, K^{10}]. $$
nodes.name: Improved covering lemma for PFR
nodes.statement_short: Covering by K^6 |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2} translates of a subspace of comparable size.
assumptions: $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by at most $K^6 |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $$ |H|/|A| \in [K^{-10}, K^{10}]. $$
nodes.label: pfr_aux-improv

nodes.statement: By repeating the proof of \Cref{pfr_aux} and using \Cref{entropy-pfr-improv} one can obtain the claim with $13/2$ replaced with $6$ and $11$ replaced by $10$.
nodes.name: Proof of Improved covering lemma for PFR
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the auxiliary covering proof with the improved entropic PFR.

nodes.statement: If $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then $A$ can be covered by most $2K^{11}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $|H| \leq |A|$.
nodes.name: Improved PFR
nodes.statement_short: PFR with 2K^{11} translates.
assumptions: $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by most $2K^{11}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $|H| \leq |A|$
nodes.label: pfr-improv

nodes.statement: By repeating the proof of \Cref{pfr} and using \Cref{pfr_aux-improv} one obtains $2K^{11}$ in place of $2K^{12}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Improved PFR
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the PFR proof with the improved covering lemma.

nodes.statement: Of course, by replacing \Cref{pfr} with \Cref{pfr-improv} we may also improve constants in downstream theorems in a straightforward manner.
nodes.name: Downstream improvements

nodes.statement: In this chapter, $h$ denotes the function $h(x) := x \log \frac{1}{x}$ for $x \in [0,1]$.
nodes.name: Function $h(x) = x\log(1/x)$

nodes.statement: $h$ is strictly concave on $[0,\infty)$.
nodes.name: Concavity
nodes.label: concave

nodes.statement: Check that $h'$ is strictly monotone decreasing.
nodes.name: Proof of Concavity
nodes.statement_short: h' is strictly decreasing.

nodes.statement: If $S$ is a finite set, and $a_s,b_s$ are non-negative for $s\in S$, then $$\sum_{s\in S} a_s \log\frac{a_s}{b_s}\ge \left(\sum_{s\in S}a_s\right)\log\frac{\sum_{s\in S} a_s}{\sum_{s\in S} b_s},$$ with the convention $0\log\frac{0}{b}=0$ for any $b\ge 0$ and $0\log\frac{a}{0}=\infty$ for any $a>0$.
nodes.name: log sum inequality
nodes.statement_short: Log sum inequality.
assumptions: $S$ is a finite set, and $a_s,b_s$ are non-negative for $s\in S$
conclusions: $$\sum_{s\in S} a_s \log\frac{a_s}{b_s}\ge \left(\sum_{s\in S}a_s\right)\log\frac{\sum_{s\in S} a_s}{\sum_{s\in S} b_s},$$ with the convention $0\log\frac{0}{b}=0$ for any $b\ge 0$ and $0\log\frac{a}{0}=\infty$ for any $a>0$
nodes.label: log-sum

nodes.statement: Let $B:=\sum_{s\in S} b_s$. Apply Jensen and \Cref{concave} to show that $\sum_{s\in S} \frac{b_s}{B} h(\frac{a_s}{b_s})\ge h(\frac{\sum_{s\in S} a_s}{B})$.
nodes.name: Proof of log sum inequality
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality for h with weights b_s/B.

nodes.statement: If equality holds in \Cref{log-sum}, then $a_s=r\cdot b_s$ for every $s\in S$, for some constant $r\in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.name: converse log sum
assumptions: equality holds in \Cref{log-sum}
conclusions: $a_s=r\cdot b_s$ for every $s\in S$, for some constant $r\in \mathbb{R}$
nodes.label: converse-log-sum

nodes.statement: By the fact that $h$ is strictly concave and the equality condition of Jensen.
nodes.name: Proof of converse log sum
nodes.statement_short: Equality case of Jensen for strictly concave h.

nodes.statement: If $A,B$ are finite non-empty subsets of a group $G$, then $A$ can be covered by at most $|A+B|/|B|$ translates of $B-B$.
nodes.name: Ruzsa covering lemma
assumptions: $A,B$ are finite non-empty subsets of a group $G$
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by at most $|A+B|/|B|$ translates of $B-B$
nodes.label: ruz-cov

nodes.statement: Cover $A$ greedily by disjoint translates of $B$.
nodes.name: Proof of Ruzsa covering lemma
nodes.statement_short: Greedy cover by disjoint translates of B.

nodes.statement: If $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then $A$ can be covered by at most $K ^ {13/2}|A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with \begin{equation} |H|/|A| \in [K^{-11}, K^{11}]. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Auxiliary covering lemma for PFR
nodes.statement_short: Small doubling A is covered by K^{13/2}|A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2} translates of a subspace with |H|/|A| in [K^-11,K^11].
assumptions: $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by at most $K ^ {13/2}|A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with \begin{equation} |H|/|A| \in [K^{-11}, K^{11}]. \end{equation}
nodes.label: pfr_aux

nodes.statement: Let $U_A$ be the uniform distribution on $A$ (which exists by \Cref{unif-exist}), thus $\bbH[U_A] = \log |A|$ by \Cref{uniform-entropy-II}. By \Cref{jensen-bound} and the fact that $U_A + U_A$ is supported on $A + A$, $\bbH[U_A + U_A] \leq \log|A+A|$. By \Cref{ruz-dist-def}, the doubling condition $|A+A| \leq K|A|$ therefore gives \[d[U_A;U_A] \leq \log K.\] By \Cref{entropy-pfr}, we may thus find a subspace $H$ of $\F_2^n$ such that \begin{equation} d[U_A;U_H] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} C' \log K\end{equation} with $C' = 11$. By \Cref{ruzsa-diff} we conclude that \begin{equation*} |\log |H| - \log |A|| \leq C' \log K, \end{equation*} proving~\eqref{ah}. From \Cref{ruz-dist-def},~\eqref{uauh} is equivalent to \[\bbH[U_A - U_H] \leq \log( |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}) + \tfrac{1}{2} C' \log K.\] By \Cref{bound-conc} we conclude the existence of a point $x_0 \in \F_p^n$ such that \[p_{U_A-U_H}(x_0) \geq |A|^{-1/2} |H|^{-1/2} K^{-C'/2},\] or equivalently \[|A \cap (H + x_0)| \geq K^{-C'/2} |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}.\] Applying \Cref{ruz-cov}, we may thus cover $A$ by at most \[\frac{|A + (A \cap (H+x_0))|}{|A \cap (H + x_0)|} \leq \frac{K|A|}{K^{-C'/2} |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}} = K^{C'/2+1} \frac{|A|^{1/2}}{|H|^{1/2}}\] translates of \[\bigl(A \cap (H + x_0)\bigr) - \bigl(A \cap (H + x_0)\bigr) \subseteq H.\] This proves the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Auxiliary covering lemma for PFR
nodes.statement_short: Entropic PFR for U_A, entropy concentration to find a heavy coset, then Ruzsa covering.

nodes.statement: d[U_A;U_H] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} C' \log K
nodes.name: Equation (11.2)
nodes.label: uauh

nodes.statement: If $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then $A$ can be covered by most $2K^{12}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $|H| \leq |A|$.
nodes.name: PFR
nodes.statement_short: Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa: a set of doubling K in F_2^n is covered by 2K^{12} cosets of a subspace no larger than it.
assumptions: $A \subset {\bf F}_2^n$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by most $2K^{12}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of ${\bf F}_2^n$ with $|H| \leq |A|$
nodes.label: pfr

nodes.statement: Let $H$ be given by \Cref{pfr_aux}. If $|H| \leq |A|$ then we are already done thanks to~\eqref{ah}. If $|H| > |A|$ then we can cover $H$ by at most $2 |H|/|A|$ translates of a subspace $H'$ of $H$ with $|H'| \leq |A|$. We can thus cover $A$ by at most \[2K^{13/2} \frac{|H|^{1/2}}{|A|^{1/2}}\] translates of $H'$, and the claim again follows from~\eqref{ah}.
nodes.name: Proof of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Take H from the auxiliary lemma and, if too large, split it into a smaller subspace.

nodes.statement: If $G$ is an abelian $2$-torsion group, $A \subset G$ is non-empty finite, and $|A+A| \leq K|A| $, then $A$ can be covered by most $2K^{12}$ translates of a finite group $H$ of $G$ with $|H| \leq |A|$.
nodes.name: PFR in infinite groups
nodes.statement_short: PFR in arbitrary abelian 2-torsion groups.
assumptions: $G$ is an abelian $2$-torsion group, $A \subset G$ is non-empty finite, and $|A+A| \leq K|A| $
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by most $2K^{12}$ translates of a finite group $H$ of $G$ with $|H| \leq |A|$
nodes.label: pfr-cor

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{pfr} to the group generated by $A$, which is isomorphic to $\F_2^n$ for some $n$.
nodes.name: Proof of PFR in infinite groups
nodes.statement_short: Apply PFR in the group generated by A.

nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a random variable. Then for any function $f$ on the range of $X$, one has $\bbH[f(X)] \leq \bbH[X]$.
nodes.name: Data processing for a single variable
assumptions: $X$ be a random variable
conclusions: for any function $f$ on the range of $X$, one has $\bbH[f(X)] \leq \bbH[X]$
nodes.label: data-process-single

nodes.statement: We have $$ \bbH[X] = \bbH[X,f(X)] = \bbH[f(X)] + \bbH[X|f(X)]$$ thanks to \Cref{relabeled-entropy} and \Cref{chain-rule}, giving the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Data processing for a single variable
nodes.statement_short: Relabeling and chain rule.

nodes.statement: Let $X,Y$ be random variables. For any function $f, g$ on the range of $X$, we have $\bbI[f(X) : Y] \leq \bbI[X:Y]$.
nodes.name: One-sided unconditional data processing inequality
assumptions: $X,Y$ be random variables. For any function $f, g$ on the range of $X$
nodes.label: data-process-unc-one

nodes.statement: By \Cref{alternative-mutual} it suffices to show that $\bbH[Y|X] \leq \bbH[Y|f(X)]$. But this follows from \Cref{submodularity} (and \Cref{relabeled-entropy}).
nodes.name: Proof of One-sided unconditional data processing inequality
nodes.statement_short: Alternative mutual information formula plus submodularity.

nodes.statement: Let $X,Y$ be random variables. For any functions $f, g$ on the ranges of $X, Y$ respectively, we have $\bbI[f(X) : g(Y )] \leq \bbI[X : Y]$.
nodes.name: Unconditional data processing inequality
assumptions: $X,Y$ be random variables. For any functions $f, g$ on the ranges of $X, Y$ respectively
nodes.label: data-process-unc

nodes.statement: From \Cref{data-process-unc-one}, \Cref{entropy-comm} we have $\bbI[f(X) : Y] \leq \bbI[X:Y]$ and $\bbI[f(X): g(Y)] \leq \bbI[f(X):Y]$, giving the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Unconditional data processing inequality
nodes.statement_short: Apply the one-sided inequality twice.

nodes.statement: Let $X,Y,Z$. For any functions $f, g$ on the ranges of $X, Y$ respectively, we have $\bbI[f(X) : g(Y )|Z] \leq \bbI[X :Y |Z]$.
nodes.name: Data processing inequality
assumptions: $X,Y,Z$. For any functions $f, g$ on the ranges of $X, Y$ respectively
nodes.label: data-process

nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{data-process-unc} to $X,Y$ conditioned to the event $Z=z$, multiply by ${\bf P}[Z=z]$, and sum using \Cref{conditional-mutual-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Data processing inequality
nodes.statement_short: Unconditional data processing for each Z=z, averaged.

nodes.statement: If $X,Y$ are $G$-valued, then $$ d[X ; -Y] \leq 3 d[X;Y].$$
nodes.name: Flipping a sign
assumptions: $X,Y$ are $G$-valued
nodes.label: sign-flip

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality (using \Cref{ruz-copy} and \Cref{independent-exist}) we may take $X,Y$ to be independent. By $(X_1,Y_1)$, $(X_2,Y_2)$ be copies of $(X,Y)$ that are conditionally independent over $X_1-Y_1=X_2-Y_2$ (this exists thanks to \Cref{cond-indep-exist}). By \Cref{independent-exist}, we can also find another copy $(X_3,Y_3)$ of $(X,Y)$ that is independent of $X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2$. From \Cref{alt-submodularity}, one has $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3, Y_3, X_3+Y_3] + \bbH[X_3+Y_3] \leq \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] + \bbH[X_3, Y_3, X_3+Y_3].$$ From \Cref{ruz-indep}, \Cref{neg-ent}, \Cref{ruz-copy} we have $$ \bbH[X_3+Y_3] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X_3] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[-Y_3] + d[X_3;-Y_3] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[Y] + d[X;-Y].$$ Since $X_3+Y_3$ is a function of $X_3,Y_3$, we see from \Cref{relabeled-entropy} and \Cref{add-entropy} that $$ \bbH[X_3,Y_3,X_3+Y_3] = \bbH[X_3,Y_3] = \bbH[X,Y] = \bbH[X]+\bbH[Y].$$ Because $X_1-Y_1=X_2-Y_2$, we have $$ X_3+Y_3 = (X_3-Y_2) - (X_1-Y_3) + (X_2+Y_1)$$ and thus by \Cref{relabeled-entropy} $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] = \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1]$$ and hence by \Cref{subadditive} $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] \leq \bbH[X_3-Y_2] + \bbH[X_1-Y_3] + \bbH[X_2] + \bbH[Y_1].$$ Since $X_3,Y_2$ are independent, we see from \Cref{ruz-indep}, \Cref{ruz-copy} that $$\bbH[X_3-Y_2] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[Y] + d[X; Y].$$ Similarly $$ \bbH[X_1-Y_3] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[Y] + d[X; Y].$$ We conclude that $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] \leq 2\bbH[X] + 2\bbH[Y] + 2d[X; Y].$$ Finally, from \Cref{data-process-single} we have $$ \bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,X_3,Y_3] \leq \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3, Y_3, X_3+Y_3].$$ From \Cref{add-entropy} followed by \Cref{cond-trial-ent}, we have $$\bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,X_3,Y_3] = \bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_1-Y_1] + \bbH[X_2,Y_2,X_2-Y_2] - \bbH[X_1-Y_1] + \bbH[X_3,Y_3]$$ and thus by \Cref{ruz-indep}, \Cref{ruz-copy}, \Cref{relabeled-entropy}, \Cref{add-entropy} $$\bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,X_3,Y_3] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y] + \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y] -\left(\frac{1}{2}\bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2}\bbH[Y] + d[X; Y]\right) + \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y].$$ Applying all of these estimates, the claim now follows from linear arithmetic.
nodes.name: Proof of Flipping a sign
nodes.statement_short: Conditionally independent trials and a third copy, then submodularity and linear arithmetic. The key step uses X_3+Y_3 = (X_3-Y_2)-(X_1-Y_3)+(X_2+Y_1).

nodes.statement: If $n \geq 0$ and $X, Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables, then $$\bbH\left[X + \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right] - \bbH[X] \leq \sum_{i=1}^n \left(\bbH[X+Y_i] - \bbH[X]\right).$$
nodes.name: Kaimonovich--Vershik--Madiman inequality
nodes.statement_short: Entropy increment of adding several independent variables is subadditive.
assumptions: $n \geq 0$ and $X, Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: klm-1

nodes.statement: This is trivial for $n=0,1$, while the $n=2$ case is \Cref{kv}. Now suppose inductively that $n > 2$, and the claim was already proven for $n-1$. By a further application of \Cref{kv} one has $$ \bbH\left[X + \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right] - \bbH\left[X + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} Y_i\right] \leq \bbH[X+Y_n] - \bbH[X].$$ By induction hypothesis one has $$ \bbH\left[X + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} Y_i\right] - \bbH[X] \leq \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \bbH[X+Y_i] - \bbH[X].$$ Summing the two inequalities, we obtain the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Kaimonovich--Vershik--Madiman inequality
nodes.statement_short: Induction on n using Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman.

nodes.statement: If $n \geq 1$ and $X, Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables, then $$ d[X; \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] \leq 2 \sum_{i=1}^n d[X; Y_i].$$
nodes.name: Kaimonovich--Vershik--Madiman inequality, II
nodes.statement_short: d[X; sum Y_i] <= 2 sum d[X;Y_i].
assumptions: $n \geq 1$ and $X, Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: klm-2

nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{klm-1} with all the $Y_i$ replaced by $-Y_i$, and using \Cref{neg-ent} and \Cref{ruz-indep}, we obtain after some rearranging $$ d[X; \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] + \frac{1}{2} (\bbH[\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] - \bbH[X]) \leq \sum_{i=1}^n \left(d[X;Y_i] + \frac{1}{2} (\bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X])\right).$$ From \Cref{sumset-lower} we have $$ \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] \geq \bbH[Y_i]$$ for all $i$; subtracting $\bbH[X]$ and averaging, we conclude that $$ \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] - \bbH[X] \geq \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X]$$ and thus $$ d[X; \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] \leq \sum_{i=1}^n d[X;Y_i] + \frac{n-1}{2n} (\bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X]).$$ From \Cref{ruzsa-diff} we have $$ \bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X] \leq 2 d[X;Y_i].$$ Since $0 \leq \frac{n-1}{2n} \leq \frac{1}{2}$, the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Kaimonovich--Vershik--Madiman inequality, II
nodes.statement_short: Apply KVM with negated Y_i, then sumset lower bound and entropy difference bound.

nodes.statement: If $n \geq 1$ and $X, Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables, then $$d\left[X; \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right] \leq d\left[X; Y_1\right] + \frac{1}{2}\left(\bbH\left[ \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right] - \bbH[Y_1]\right).$$
nodes.name: Kaimonovich--Vershik--Madiman inequality, III
nodes.statement_short: d[X; sum Y_i] <= d[X;Y_1] + half the entropy increase of the sum over Y_1.
assumptions: $n \geq 1$ and $X, Y_1, \dots, Y_n$ are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: klm-3

nodes.statement: From \Cref{kv} one has $$ \bbH\left[-X + \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right] \leq \bbH[ - X + Y_1 ] + \bbH\left[ \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i \right] - \bbH[Y_1].$$ The claim then follows from \Cref{ruz-indep} and some elementary algebra.
nodes.name: Proof of Kaimonovich--Vershik--Madiman inequality, III
nodes.statement_short: Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman plus algebra.

nodes.statement: Let $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $(Y_j)_{1 \leq j \leq l}$ be tuples of jointly independent random variables (so the $X$'s and $Y$'s are also independent of each other), and let $f: \{1,\dots,l\} \to \{1,\dots,m\}$ be a function, then $$ \bbH[\sum_{j=1}^l Y_j] \leq \bbH[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_i ] + \sum_{j=1}^l (\bbH[ Y_j - X_{f(j)}] - \bbH[X_{f(j)}]).$$
nodes.name: Comparing sums
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of one independent sum bounded by another sum plus pairwise entropy increments.
assumptions: $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $(Y_j)_{1 \leq j \leq l}$ be tuples of jointly independent random variables (so the $X$'s and $Y$'s are also independent of each other), and let $f: \{1,\dots,l\} \to \{1,\dots,m\}$ be a function
nodes.label: compare-sums

nodes.statement: Write $W := \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$. From \Cref{sumset-lower} we have $$ \bbH[\sum_{j=1}^l Y_j] \leq \bbH[-W + \sum_{j=1}^l Y_j]$$ while from \Cref{klm-1} one has $$ \bbH[-W + \sum_{j=1}^l Y_j] \leq \bbH[-W] + \sum_{j=1}^l \bbH[-W + Y_j] - \bbH[-W].$$ From \Cref{kv} one has $$ \bbH[-W + Y_j] - \bbH[-W] \leq \bbH[-X_{f(j)} + Y_j] - \bbH[-X_{f(j)}].$$ The claim now follows from \Cref{neg-ent} and some elementary algebra.
nodes.name: Proof of Comparing sums
nodes.statement_short: Sumset lower bound, iterated KVM, then KVM for each term.

nodes.statement: Let $X,Y,X'$ be independent $G$-valued random variables, with $X'$ a copy of $X$, and let $a$ be an integer. Then $$\bbH[X-(a+1)Y] \leq \bbH[X-aY] + \bbH[X-Y-X'] - \bbH[X]$$ and $$\bbH[X-(a-1)Y] \leq \bbH[X-aY] + \bbH[X-Y-X'] - \bbH[X].$$
nodes.name: Sums of dilates I
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of X-(a±1)Y bounded by entropy of X-aY plus an increment.
assumptions: $X,Y,X'$ be independent $G$-valued random variables, with $X'$ a copy of $X$, and let $a$ be an integer
nodes.label: sum-dilate-I

nodes.statement: From \Cref{ruzsa-triangle-improved} we have $$ \bbH[(X-Y)-aY] \leq \bbH[(X-Y) - X'] + \bbH[X'-aY] - \bbH[X']$$ which gives the first inequality. Similarly from \Cref{ruzsa-triangle-improved} we have $$ \bbH[(X+Y)-aY] \leq \bbH[(X+Y) - X'] + \bbH[X'-aY] - \bbH[X']$$ which (when combined with \Cref{neg-ent}) gives the second inequality.
nodes.name: Proof of Sums of dilates I
nodes.statement_short: Improved Ruzsa triangle inequality applied twice.

nodes.statement: Let $X,Y$ be independent $G$-valued random variables, and let $a$ be an integer. Then $$\bbH[X-aY] - \bbH[X] \leq 4 |a| d[X;Y].$$
nodes.name: Sums of dilates II
nodes.statement_short: H[X-aY]-H[X] <= 4|a| d[X;Y].
assumptions: $X,Y$ be independent $G$-valued random variables, and let $a$ be an integer
nodes.label: sum-dilate-II

nodes.statement: From \Cref{kv} one has $$\bbH[Y-X+X'] - \bbH[Y-X] \leq \bbH[Y+X'] - \bbH[Y] = \bbH[Y+X] - \bbH[Y]$$ which by \Cref{ruz-indep} gives $$\bbH[X-Y-X'] -\bbH[X] \leq d[X;Y] + d[X;-Y]$$ and hence by \Cref{sign-flip} $$\bbH[X-Y-X'] - \bbH[X] \leq 4d[X;Y].$$ From \Cref{sum-dilate-I} we then have $$\bbH[X-(a\pm 1)Y] \leq \bbH[X-aY] + 4 d[X;Y]$$ and the claim now follows by an induction on $|a|$.
nodes.name: Proof of Sums of dilates II
nodes.statement_short: KVM and sign flip bound the step increment, then induction on |a|.

nodes.statement: We remark that in the paper [GGMT2024] the variant estimate $$\bbH[X-aY] - \bbH[X] \leq (4 + 10 \lfloor \log_2 |a| \rfloor) d[X;Y]$$ is also proven by a similar method.
nodes.name: Logarithmic sums of dilates estimate
nodes.statement_short: H[X-aY]-H[X] <= (4+10 floor(log2|a|)) d[X;Y].

nodes.statement: Let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ be an $m$-tuple of $G$-valued random variables $X_i$. Then we define \[ D[X_{[m]}] := \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m \tilde X_i] - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[\tilde X_i], \] where the $\tilde X_i$ are independent copies of the $X_i$.
nodes.name: Multidistance
nodes.statement_short: Multidistance D[X_[m]]: entropy of the sum of independent copies minus the average entropy.
nodes.label: multidist-def

nodes.statement: If $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $Y_{[m]} = (Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ are such that $X_i$ and $Y_i$ have the same distribution for each $i$, then $D[X_{[m]}] = D[Y_{[m]}]$.
nodes.name: Multidistance of copy
assumptions: $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $Y_{[m]} = (Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ are such that $X_i$ and $Y_i$ have the same distribution for each $i$
nodes.label: multidist-copy

nodes.statement: Clear from Lemma \ref{copy-ent}.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance of copy
nodes.statement_short: Copies have equal entropy.

nodes.statement: If $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ are jointly independent, then $D[X_{[m]}] = \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i] - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i]$.
nodes.name: Multidistance of independent variables
assumptions: $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ are jointly independent
nodes.label: multidist-indep

nodes.statement: Clear from definition.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance of independent variables
nodes.statement_short: Clear from definition.

nodes.statement: For any such tuple, we have $D[X_{[m]}] \geq 0$.
nodes.name: Nonnegativity
assumptions: such tuple
nodes.label: multidist-nonneg

nodes.statement: From \Cref{sumset-lower} one has $$ \bbH[\sum_{i =1}^m \tilde X_i] \geq \bbH[\tilde X_i]$$ for each $1 \leq i \leq m$. Averaging over $i$, we obtain the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Nonnegativity
nodes.statement_short: Sumset lower bound for each i, averaged.

nodes.statement: If $\phi: \{1,\dots,m\} \to \{1,\dots,m\}$ is a bijection, then $D[X_{[m]}] = D[(X_{\phi(j)})_{1 \leq j \leq m}]$.
nodes.name: Relabeling
assumptions: $\phi: \{1,\dots,m\} \to \{1,\dots,m\}$ is a bijection
nodes.label: multidist-perm

nodes.statement: Trivial.
nodes.name: Proof of Relabeling
nodes.statement_short: Trivial.

nodes.statement: Let $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables. Then $$\sum_{1 \leq j,k \leq m: j \neq k} d[X_j; -X_k] \leq m(m-1) D[X_{[m]}].$$
nodes.name: Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, I
nodes.statement_short: Sum of d[X_j;-X_k] over distinct pairs is at most m(m-1) D[X_[m]].
assumptions: $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables
conclusions: $$\sum_{1 \leq j,k \leq m: j \neq k} d[X_j; -X_k] \leq m(m-1) D[X_{[m]}].$$
nodes.label: multidist-ruzsa-I

nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruz-copy}, \Cref{multidist-copy} we may take the $X_i$ to be jointly independent. From \Cref{sumset-lower}, we see that for any distinct $1 \leq j,k \leq m$, we have \[ \bbH[X_j+X_k] \leq \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i], \] and hence by \Cref{ruz-indep} \[ d[X_j;-X_k] \leq \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i] - \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X_j] - \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X_k]. \] Summing this over all pairs $(j,k)$, $j \neq k$ and using Lemma \ref{multidist-indep}, we obtain the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, I
nodes.statement_short: Sumset lower bound for each pair, summed.

nodes.statement: Let $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables. Then $$\sum_{j=1}^m d[X_j;X_j] \leq 2 m D[X_{[m]}].$$
nodes.name: Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, II
nodes.statement_short: Sum of self-distances is at most 2m D[X_[m]].
assumptions: $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: multidist-ruzsa-II

nodes.statement: From \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} we have $d[X_j;X_j] \leq 2 d[X_j;-X_k]$, and applying this to every summand in \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-I}, we obtain the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, II
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality plus the first comparison.

nodes.statement: Let $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables. If the $X_i$ all have the same distribution, then $D[X_{[m]}] \leq m d[X_i;X_i]$ for any $1 \leq i \leq m$.
nodes.name: Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, III
nodes.statement_short: For identically distributed X_i, D[X_[m]] <= m d[X_i;X_i].
assumptions: $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables. If the $X_i$ all have the same distribution
conclusions: $D[X_{[m]}] \leq m d[X_i;X_i]$ for any $1 \leq i \leq m$
nodes.label: multidist-ruzsa-III

nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruz-copy}, \Cref{multidist-copy} we may take the $X_i$ to be jointly independent. Let $X_0$ be a further independent copy of the $X_i$. From \Cref{klm-1}, we have $$ \bbH[-X_0 + \sum_{i=1}^m X_i] - \bbH[-X_0] \leq \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_0 - X_i] - \bbH[-X_0]$$ and hence by \Cref{neg-ent} and \Cref{ruz-indep} $$ \bbH[-X_0 + \sum_{i=1}^m X_i] - \bbH[X_0] \leq m d[X_i,X_i].$$ On the other hand, by \Cref{sumset-lower} we have $$ \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i] \leq \bbH[-X_0 + \sum_{i=1}^m X_i]$$ and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, III
nodes.statement_short: KVM with an extra independent copy, then the sumset lower bound.

nodes.statement: Let $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of independent $G$-valued random variables. Let $W := \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$. Then $$ d[W;-W] \leq 2 D[X_i].$$
nodes.name: Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, IV
nodes.statement_short: For the sum W of an independent tuple, d[W;-W] <= 2 D.
assumptions: $m \ge 2$, and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of independent $G$-valued random variables. Let $W := \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$
nodes.label: multidist-ruzsa-IV

nodes.statement: Take $(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ to be further independent copies of $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ (which exist by \Cref{independent-exist}), and write $W' := \sum_{i=1}^m X'_i$. Fix any distinct $a,b \in I$. From \Cref{kv} one has \begin{equation} \bbH[W + W'] \leq \bbH[W] + \bbH[X_{a} + W'] - \bbH[X_{a}] \end{equation} and also \[ \bbH[X_a + W'] \leq \bbH[X_a + X_b] + \bbH[W'] - \bbH[X'_b].\] Combining this with~\eqref{7922} and then applying \Cref{sumset-lower} we have \begin{align*} \bbH[W + W'] & \leq 2\bbH[W] + \bbH[X_a + X_b] - \bbH[X_a] - \bbH[X_b] \\ & \leq 3 \bbH[W] - \bbH[X_a] - \bbH[X_b]. \end{align*} Averaging this over all choices of $(a,b)$ gives $\bbH[W] + 2 D[X_{[m]}]$, and the claim follows from \Cref{ruz-indep}.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance and Ruzsa distance, IV
nodes.statement_short: KVM twice with an independent copy of the tuple, then average over pairs.

nodes.statement: \bbH[W + W'] \leq \bbH[W] + \bbH[X_{a} + W'] - \bbH[X_{a}]
nodes.name: Equation (12.1)

nodes.statement: If $D[X_{[m]}]=0$, then for each $1 \leq i \leq m$ there is a finite subgroup $H_i \leq G$ such that $d[X_i; U_{H_i}] = 0$.
nodes.name: Vanishing
nodes.statement_short: Zero multidistance forces each X_i to be at distance zero from a uniform subgroup variable.
conclusions: for each $1 \leq i \leq m$ there is a finite subgroup $H_i \leq G$ such that $d[X_i; U_{H_i}] = 0$
nodes.label: multi-zero

nodes.statement: From \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-II} and \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg} we have $d[X_j; X_j]=0$ for all $1 \leq j \leq m$. The claim now follows from \Cref{lem:100pc}.
nodes.name: Proof of Vanishing
nodes.statement_short: Zero multidistance gives zero self-distances, then the 100% inverse theorem.

nodes.statement: With more effort one can show that $H_i$ is independent of $i$, but we will not need to do so here.
nodes.name: Common subgroup

nodes.statement: Fix $m \geq 2$, and a reference variable $X^0$ in $G$.
nodes.name: Reference variable $X^0$

nodes.statement: We set $\eta := \frac{1}{32m^3}$.
nodes.name: $\eta$
nodes.label: eta-def-multi

nodes.statement: If $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ is a tuple, we define its $\tau$-functional $$ \tau[ (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] := D[(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] + \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X^0].$$
nodes.name: $\tau$-functional
nodes.statement_short: tau functional: multidistance plus eta times distances to the reference variable.
nodes.label: tau-def-multi

nodes.statement: A $\tau$-minimizer is a tuple $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ that minimizes the $\tau$-functional among all tuples of $G$-valued random variables.
nodes.name: $\tau$-minimizer
nodes.label: tau-min-multi

nodes.statement: If $G$ is finite, then a $\tau$-minimizer exists.
nodes.name: Existence of $\tau$-minimizer
assumptions: $G$ is finite
nodes.label: tau-min-exist-multi

nodes.statement: This is similar to the proof of \Cref{tau-min}.
nodes.name: Proof of Existence of $\tau$-minimizer
nodes.statement_short: Similar to the existence of tau-minimizers.

nodes.statement: If $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ is a $\tau$-minimizer, then $\sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X^0] \leq \frac{2m}{\eta} d[X^0; X^0]$.
nodes.name: Minimizer close to reference variables
nodes.statement_short: A tau-minimizer stays within 2m/eta d[X^0;X^0] of the reference variable.
assumptions: $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ is a $\tau$-minimizer
nodes.label: tau-ref

nodes.statement: By \Cref{tau-min-multi} we have $$ \tau[ (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \leq \tau[ (X^0)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]$$ and hence by \Cref{tau-def-multi} and \Cref{multidist-nonneg} $$ \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X^0] \leq D[(X^0)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] + m d[X^0; X^0].$$ The claim now follows from \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-III}.
nodes.name: Proof of Minimizer close to reference variables
nodes.statement_short: Compare with the constant tuple X^0 and bound its multidistance.

nodes.statement: If $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ is a $\tau$-minimizer, and $k := D[(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]$, then for any other tuple $(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$, one has $$ k - D[(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \leq \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X'_i].$$
nodes.name: Lower bound on multidistance
nodes.statement_short: For a tau-minimizer, any other tuple has multidistance at least k minus eta times the distances.
assumptions: $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ is a $\tau$-minimizer, and $k := D[(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]$
conclusions: for any other tuple $(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$, one has $$ k - D[(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \leq \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X'_i].$$
nodes.label: multidist-lower

nodes.statement: By \Cref{tau-min-multi} we have $$ \tau[ (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \leq \tau[ (X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]$$ and hence by \Cref{tau-def-multi} $$ k + \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X^0] \leq D[(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] + \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X'_i; X^0].$$ On the other hand, by \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} we have $$ d[X'_i; X^0] \leq d[X_i; X^0] + d[X_i; X'_i].$$ The claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Lower bound on multidistance
nodes.statement_short: Minimality of tau plus the triangle inequality.

nodes.statement: If $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $Y_{[m]} = (Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ are tuples of random variables, with the $X_i$ being $G$-valued (but the $Y_i$ need not be), then we define \begin{equation} D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]} ] = \sum_{(y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}} \biggl(\prod_{1 \leq i \leq m} p_{Y_i}(y_i)\biggr) D[ (X_i \,|\, Y_i \mathop{=}y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \end{equation} where each $y_i$ ranges over the support of $p_{Y_i}$ for $1 \leq i \leq m$.
nodes.name: Conditional multidistance
nodes.statement_short: Conditional multidistance as the weighted average over conditioning values.
nodes.label: cond-multidist-def

nodes.statement: D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]} ] = \sum_{(y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}} \biggl(\prod_{1 \leq i \leq m} p_{Y_i}(y_i)\biggr) D[ (X_i \,|\, Y_i \mathop{=}y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]
nodes.name: Equation (12.2)
nodes.label: multi-def-cond-alt

nodes.statement: If the $(X_i,Y_i)$ are independent, \begin{equation} D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]}] := \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i \big| (Y_j)_{1 \leq j \leq m} ] - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[ X_i | Y_i]. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Alternate form of conditional multidistance
nodes.statement_short: Conditional multidistance as a conditional-entropy expression for independent pairs.
conclusions: If the $(X_i,Y_i)$ are independent, \begin{equation} D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]}] := \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i \big| (Y_j)_{1 \leq j \leq m} ] - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[ X_i | Y_i]. \end{equation}
nodes.label: cond-multidist-alt

nodes.statement: D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]}] := \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i \big| (Y_j)_{1 \leq j \leq m} ] - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[ X_i | Y_i].
nodes.name: Equation (12.3)
nodes.label: multi-def-cond

nodes.statement: This is routine from \Cref{conditional-entropy-def} and Definitions \ref{multidist-def} and \ref{cond-multidist-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Alternate form of conditional multidistance
nodes.statement_short: Routine from the definitions.

nodes.statement: If $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $Y_{[m]} = (Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ are tuples of random variables, then $D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]} ] \geq 0$.
nodes.name: Conditional multidistance nonnegative
assumptions: $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $Y_{[m]} = (Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ are tuples of random variables
nodes.label: cond-multidist-nonneg

nodes.statement: Clear from \Cref{multidist-nonneg} and \Cref{cond-multidist-def}, except that some care may need to be taken to deal with the $y_i$ where $p_{Y_i}$ vanish.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional multidistance nonnegative
nodes.statement_short: Clear from nonnegativity of multidistance.
