nodes.statement: If $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ is a $\tau$-minimizer, and $k := D[(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]$, then for any other tuples $(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $(Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ with the $X'_i$ $G$-valued, one has $$ k - D[(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m} | (Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \leq \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X'_i|Y_i].$$
nodes.name: Lower bound on conditional multidistance
nodes.statement_short: Conditional version of the multidistance lower bound for tau-minimizers.
assumptions: $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ is a $\tau$-minimizer, and $k := D[(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]$
conclusions: for any other tuples $(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ and $(Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ with the $X'_i$ $G$-valued, one has $$ k - D[(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m} | (Y_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \leq \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X'_i|Y_i].$$
nodes.label: cond-multidist-lower

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{multidist-lower}, \Cref{cond-multidist-alt}, and \Cref{cond-dist-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Lower bound on conditional multidistance
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the unconditional lower bound and the alternate form.

nodes.statement: With the notation of the previous lemma, we have \begin{equation} k - D[ X'_{[m]} | Y_{[m]} ] \leq \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_{\sigma(i)};X'_i|Y_i] \end{equation} for any permutation $\sigma : \{1,\dots,m\} \rightarrow \{1,\dots,m\}$.
nodes.name: Lower bound on conditional multidistance, II
nodes.statement_short: Permuted version of the conditional multidistance lower bound.
conclusions: With the notation of the previous lemma, we have \begin{equation} k - D[ X'_{[m]} | Y_{[m]} ] \leq \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_{\sigma(i)};X'_i|Y_i] \end{equation} for any permutation $\sigma : \{1,\dots,m\} \rightarrow \{1,\dots,m\}$
nodes.label: cond-multidist-lower-II

nodes.statement: This follows from \Cref{cond-multidist-lower} and \Cref{multidist-perm}.
nodes.name: Proof of Lower bound on conditional multidistance, II
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound plus relabeling invariance.

nodes.statement: Let $\pi \colon G \to H$ be a homomorphism of abelian groups and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of jointly independent $G$-valued random variables. Then $D[X_{[m]}]$ is equal to \begin{equation} D[ X_{[m]} | \pi(X_{[m]}) ] +D[ \pi(X_{[m]}) ] + \bbI[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_i : \pi(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_i\bigr) ] \end{equation} where $\pi(X_{[m]}) := (\pi(X_i))_{1 \leq i \leq m}$.
nodes.name: Multidistance chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Multidistance splits along a homomorphism into conditional and image multidistance plus a mutual information.
assumptions: $\pi \colon G \to H$ be a homomorphism of abelian groups and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of jointly independent $G$-valued random variables
conclusions: $D[X_{[m]}]$ is equal to \begin{equation} D[ X_{[m]} | \pi(X_{[m]}) ] +D[ \pi(X_{[m]}) ] + \bbI[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_i : \pi(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_i\bigr) ] \end{equation} where $\pi(X_{[m]}) := (\pi(X_i))_{1 \leq i \leq m}$
nodes.label: multidist-chain-rule

nodes.statement: D[ X_{[m]} | \pi(X_{[m]}) ] +D[ \pi(X_{[m]}) ] + \bbI[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_i : \pi(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_i\bigr) ]
nodes.name: Equation (12.5)
nodes.label: chain-eq

nodes.statement: For notational brevity during this proof, write $S := \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$. From \Cref{conditional-mutual-alt} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy}, noting that $\pi(S)$ is determined both by $S$ and by $\pi(X_{[m]})$, we have \begin{equation*} \bbI[S:\pi(X_{[m]})|\pi(S)] = \bbH[S]+\bbH[\pi(X_{[m]})]-\bbH[S,\pi(X_{[m]})]-\bbH[\pi(S)], \end{equation*} and by \Cref{chain-rule} the right-hand side is equal to \begin{equation*} \bbH[S]-\bbH[S|\pi(X_{[m]})]-\bbH[\pi(S)]. \end{equation*} Therefore, \begin{equation} \bbH[S]=\bbH[S|\pi(X_{[m]})]+\bbH[\pi(S)]+\bbI[S:\pi(X_{[m]})|\pi(S)]. \end{equation} From a further application of \Cref{chain-rule} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy} we have \begin{equation} \bbH[X_i] = \bbH[X_i \, | \, \pi(X_i)] + \bbH[\pi(X_i)] \end{equation} for all $1 \leq i \leq m$. Averaging~\eqref{chain-2} in $i$ and subtracting this from~\eqref{chain-1}, we obtain the claim from \Cref{multidist-def}.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Express the conditional mutual information in entropies and subtract averaged chain rules.

nodes.statement: \bbH[S]=\bbH[S|\pi(X_{[m]})]+\bbH[\pi(S)]+\bbI[S:\pi(X_{[m]})|\pi(S)].
nodes.name: Equation (12.6)
nodes.label: chain-1

nodes.statement: \bbH[X_i] = \bbH[X_i \, | \, \pi(X_i)] + \bbH[\pi(X_i)]
nodes.name: Equation (12.7)
nodes.label: chain-2

nodes.statement: Let $\pi \colon G \to H$ be a homomorphism of abelian groups. Let $I$ be a finite index set and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables. Let $Y_{[m]}$ be another tuple of random variables (not necessarily $G$-valued). Suppose that the pairs $(X_i, Y_i)$ are jointly independent of one another (but $X_i$ need not be independent of $Y_i$). Then \begin{align}\nonumber D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]} ] &= D[ X_{[m]} \,|\, \pi(X_{[m]}), Y_{[m]}] + D[ \pi(X_{[m]}) \,|\, Y_{[m]}] \\ &\quad\qquad + \bbI[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_i : \pi(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_i \bigr), Y_{[m]} ]. \end{align}
nodes.name: Conditional multidistance chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Conditional version of the multidistance chain rule.
assumptions: $\pi \colon G \to H$ be a homomorphism of abelian groups. Let $I$ be a finite index set and let $X_{[m]}$ be a tuple of $G$-valued random variables. Let $Y_{[m]}$ be another tuple of random variables (not necessarily $G$-valued). Suppose that the pairs $(X_i, Y_i)$ are jointly independent of one another (but $X_i$ need not be independent of $Y_i$)
conclusions: \begin{align}\nonumber D[ X_{[m]} | Y_{[m]} ] &= D[ X_{[m]} \,|\, \pi(X_{[m]}), Y_{[m]}] + D[ \pi(X_{[m]}) \,|\, Y_{[m]}] \\ &\quad\qquad + \bbI[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_i : \pi(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_i \bigr), Y_{[m]} ]. \end{align}
nodes.label: multidist-chain-rule-cond

nodes.statement: For each $y_i$ in the support of $p_{Y_i}$, apply \Cref{multidist-chain-rule} with $X_i$ replaced by the conditioned random variable $(X_i|Y_i=y_i)$, and the claim~\eqref{chain-eq-cond} follows by averaging~\eqref{chain-eq} in the $y_i$ using the weights $p_{Y_i}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Conditional multidistance chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Apply the chain rule to conditioned variables and average.

nodes.statement: Let $m$ be a positive integer. Suppose one has a sequence \begin{equation} G_m \to G_{m-1} \to \dots \to G_1 \to G_0 = \{0\} \end{equation} of homomorphisms between abelian groups $G_0,\dots,G_m$, and for each $d=0,\dots,m$, let $\pi_d : G_m \to G_d$ be the homomorphism from $G_m$ to $G_d$ arising from this sequence by composition (so for instance $\pi_m$ is the identity homomorphism and $\pi_0$ is the zero homomorphism). Let $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ be a jointly independent tuple of $G_m$-valued random variables. Then \begin{equation} \begin{split} D[ X_{[m]} ] &= \sum_{d=1}^m D[ \pi_d(X_{[m]}) \,|\, \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]})] \\ &\quad + \sum_{d=1}^{m-1} \bbI[ \sum_i X_i : \pi_d(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi_d\big(\sum_i X_i\big), \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ]. \end{split} \end{equation} In particular, by \Cref{conditional-nonneg}, \begin{align}\nonumber D[ X_{[m]} ] \geq & \sum_{d=1}^m D[ \pi_d(X_{[m]})|\pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ] \\ & + \bbI[ \sum_i X_i : \pi_1(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi_1\bigl(\sum_i X_i\bigr) ]. \end{align}
nodes.name: Iterated multidistance chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Iterated multidistance chain rule along a tower of homomorphisms.
assumptions: $m$ be a positive integer. Suppose one has a sequence \begin{equation} G_m \to G_{m-1} \to \dots \to G_1 \to G_0 = \{0\} \end{equation} of homomorphisms between abelian groups $G_0,\dots,G_m$, and for each $d=0,\dots,m$, let $\pi_d : G_m \to G_d$ be the homomorphism from $G_m$ to $G_d$ arising from this sequence by composition (so for instance $\pi_m$ is the identity homomorphism and $\pi_0$ is the zero homomorphism). Let $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ be a jointly independent tuple of $G_m$-valued random variables
conclusions: \begin{equation} \begin{split} D[ X_{[m]} ] &= \sum_{d=1}^m D[ \pi_d(X_{[m]}) \,|\, \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]})] \\ &\quad + \sum_{d=1}^{m-1} \bbI[ \sum_i X_i : \pi_d(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi_d\big(\sum_i X_i\big), \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ]. \end{split} \end{equation} In particular, by \Cref{conditional-nonneg}, \begin{align}\nonumber D[ X_{[m]} ] \geq & \sum_{d=1}^m D[ \pi_d(X_{[m]})|\pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ] \\ & + \bbI[ \sum_i X_i : \pi_1(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi_1\bigl(\sum_i X_i\bigr) ]. \end{align}
nodes.label: multidist-chain-rule-iter

nodes.statement: G_m \to G_{m-1} \to \dots \to G_1 \to G_0 = \{0\}
nodes.name: Equation (12.9)
nodes.label: g-seq

nodes.statement: \begin{split} D[ X_{[m]} ] &= \sum_{d=1}^m D[ \pi_d(X_{[m]}) \,|\, \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]})] \\ &\quad + \sum_{d=1}^{m-1} \bbI[ \sum_i X_i : \pi_d(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi_d\big(\sum_i X_i\big), \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ]. \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (12.10)
nodes.label: chain-eq-cond'

nodes.statement: \nonumber D[ X_{[m]} ] \geq & \sum_{d=1}^m D[ \pi_d(X_{[m]})|\pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ] \\ & + \bbI[ \sum_i X_i : \pi_1(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi_1\bigl(\sum_i X_i\bigr) ].
nodes.name: Equation (12.11)
nodes.label: chain-eq-cond''

nodes.statement: From \Cref{multidist-chain-rule-cond} (taking $Y_{[m]} = \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]})$ and $\pi = \pi_d$ there, and noting that $\pi_d(X_{[m]})$ determines $Y_{[m]}$) we have \begin{align*} D[ X_{[m]} \,|\, \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ] &= D[ X_{[m]} \,|\, \pi_d(X_{[m]}) ] + D[ \pi_d(X_{[m]})\,|\,\pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ] \\ &\quad + \bbI[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_i : \pi_d(X_{[m]}) \; \big| \; \pi_d\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_i\bigr), \pi_{d-1}(X_{[m]}) ] \end{align*} for $d=1,\dots,m$. The claim follows by telescoping series, noting that $D[X_{[m]} | \pi_0(X_{[m]})] = D[X_{[m]}]$ and that $\pi_m(X_{[m]})=X_{[m]}$ (and also $\pi_m( \sum_i X_i ) = \sum_i X_i$).
nodes.name: Proof of Iterated multidistance chain rule
nodes.statement_short: Telescope the conditional chain rule along the tower.

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $m \geq 2$. Suppose that $X_{i,j}$, $1 \leq i, j \leq m$, are independent $G$-valued random variables. Then \begin{align*} &\bbI[ \bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{j =1}^{m} : \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j = 1}^m X_{i,j} ] \\ &\quad \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} \Bigl(D[(X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m] - D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; (X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m})_{i =1}^m ]\Bigr) \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad + D[(X_{i,m})_{i=1}^m] - D[ \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i=1}^m ], \end{align*} where all the multidistances here involve the indexing set $\{1,\dots, m\}$.
nodes.name: Multidistance chain rule for a matrix of variables
nodes.statement_short: Mutual information between row and column sums of an m x m array bounded by multidistance differences.
assumptions: $G$ be an abelian group and let $m \geq 2$. Suppose that $X_{i,j}$, $1 \leq i, j \leq m$, are independent $G$-valued random variables
conclusions: \begin{align*} &\bbI[ \bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{j =1}^{m} : \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j = 1}^m X_{i,j} ] \\ &\quad \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} \Bigl(D[(X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m] - D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; (X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m})_{i =1}^m ]\Bigr) \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad + D[(X_{i,m})_{i=1}^m] - D[ \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i=1}^m ], \end{align*} where all the multidistances here involve the indexing set $\{1,\dots, m\}$
nodes.label: cor-multid

nodes.statement: In \Cref{multidist-chain-rule-iter} we take $G_d := G^d$ with the maps $\pi_d \colon G^m \to G^d$ for $d=1,\dots,m$ defined by \[ \pi_d(x_1,\dots,x_m) := (x_1,\dots,x_{d-1}, x_d + \cdots + x_m) \] with $\pi_0=0$. Since $\pi_{d-1}(x)$ can be obtained from $\pi_{d}(x)$ by applying a homomorphism, we obtain a sequence of the form~\eqref{g-seq}. Now we apply \Cref{multidist-chain-rule-iter} with $I = \{1,\dots, m\}$ and $X_i := (X_{i,j})_{j = 1}^m$. Using joint independence and \Cref{add-entropy}, we find that \[ D[ X_{[m]} ] = \sum_{j=1}^m D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ]. \] On the other hand, for $1 \leq j \leq m-1$, we see that once $\pi_{j}(X_i)$ is fixed, $\pi_{j+1}(X_i)$ is determined by $X_{i, j}$ and vice versa, so \[ D[ \pi_{j+1}(X_{[m]}) \; | \; \pi_{j}(X_{[m]}) ] = D[ (X_{i, j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; \pi_{j}(X_{[m]} )]. \] Since the $X_{i,j}$ are jointly independent, we may further simplify: \[ D[ (X_{i, j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; \pi_{j}(X_{[m]})] = D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; ( X_{i, j} + \cdots + X_{i, m})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ]. \] Putting all this into the conclusion of \Cref{multidist-chain-rule-iter}, we obtain \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m} D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ] \geq \begin{aligned}[t] &\sum_{j=1}^{m-1} D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; (X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ] \\ &\!\!\!+ D[ \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \\ &\!\!\!+\bbI[ \bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{j =1}^{m} : \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j = 1}^m X_{i,j} ] \end{aligned} \] and the claim follows by rearranging.
nodes.name: Proof of Multidistance chain rule for a matrix of variables
nodes.statement_short: Iterated chain rule for the partial-sum maps pi_d, then simplify by independence.

nodes.statement: We let $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{i =1}^m$ be a $\tau$-minimizer.
nodes.name: $X_{[m]}$ is a $\tau$-minimizer

nodes.statement: Suppose that $X_{i,j}$, $1 \leq i,j \leq m$, are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables, such that for each $j = 1,\dots,m$, the random variables $(X_{i,j})_{i = 1}^m$ coincide in distribution with some permutation of $X_{[m]}$. Write \[ {\mathcal I} := \bbI[ \bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{j =1}^{m} : \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j = 1}^m X_{i,j} ]. \] Then \begin{equation} {\mathcal I} \leq m(4m+1) \eta k. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Bounding mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Mutual information between row and column sums of an array of minimizer copies is at most m(4m+1) eta k.
conclusions: Suppose that $X_{i,j}$, $1 \leq i,j \leq m$, are jointly independent $G$-valued random variables, such that for each $j = 1,\dots,m$, the random variables $(X_{i,j})_{i = 1}^m$ coincide in distribution with some permutation of $X_{[m]}$. Write \[ {\mathcal I} := \bbI[ \bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{j =1}^{m} : \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j = 1}^m X_{i,j} ]. \] Then \begin{equation} {\mathcal I} \leq m(4m+1) \eta k. \end{equation}
nodes.label: key

nodes.statement: {\mathcal I} \leq m(4m+1) \eta k.
nodes.name: Equation (12.12)
nodes.label: I-ineq

nodes.statement: For each $j \in \{1,\dots,m\}$ we call the tuple $(X_{i,j})_{i = 1}^m$ a \emph{column} and for each $i \in \{1,\dots, m\}$ we call the tuple $(X_{i,j})_{j = 1}^m$ a \emph{row}. Hence, by hypothesis, each column is a permutation of $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{i=1}^m$. From \Cref{cor-multid} we have \begin{equation} {\mathcal I} \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} A_j + B,\end{equation} where \[ A_j := D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m] - D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; (X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m})_{i =1}^m ] \] and \[ B := D[ (X_{i,m})_{i=1}^m ] - D[ \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i=1}^m ]. \] We first consider the $A_j$, for fixed $j \in \{1,\dots, m-1\}$. By \Cref{multidist-perm} and our hypothesis on columns, we have \[ D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m ]= D[ (X_i)_{i=1}^m ] = k. \] Let $\sigma = \sigma_j \colon I \to I$ be a permutation such that $X_{i,j} \equiv X_{\sigma(i)}$, and write $X'_i := X_{i,j}$ and $Y_i := X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m}$. By \Cref{cond-multidist-lower-II}, we have \begin{align} A_j & \leq \eta (\sum_{i = 1}^{m} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i, j}|X_{i, j} + \cdots + X_{i,m}]). \end{align} We similarly consider $B$. By \Cref{multidist-perm} applied to the $m$-th column, \[ D[ (X_{i, m})_{i = 1}^m ] = D[X_{[m]}] = k. \] For $1 \leq i \leq m$, denote the sum of row $i$ by \[ V_i := \sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}; \] if we apply \Cref{cond-multidist-lower-II} again, now with $X_{\sigma(i)} = X_{i,m}$, $X'_i := V_i$, and with the variable $Y_i$ being trivial, we obtain \begin{equation} B \leq \eta \sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_{i,m}; V_i]. \end{equation} It remains to bound the distances appearing in~\eqref{54a} and~\eqref{55a} further using Ruzsa calculus. For $1 \leq j \leq m-1$ and $1 \leq i \leq m$, by \Cref{first-useful} we have \begin{align*} &d[ X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}| X_{i,j}+\cdots+X_{i,m}] \leq d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}] \\ &\quad + \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\bbH[X_{i,j}+\cdots+X_{i,m}] - \bbH[X_{i,{j+1}}+\cdots+X_{i,m}]\bigr). \end{align*} For each $i$, summing over $j = 1,\dots, m-1$ gives \begin{align} \nonumber &\sum_{j=1}^{m-1} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}| X_{i,j}+\cdots+X_{i,m}] \\ &\qquad \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}] + \frac12 \bigl( \bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}] \bigr). \end{align} On the other hand, by \Cref{klm-3} (since $X_{i,m}$ appears in the sum $V_i$) we have \begin{align} d[X_{i,m}; V_i] &\leq d[X_{i,m}; X_{i,m}] + \frac12 \bigl( \bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}] \bigr). \end{align} Combining~\eqref{441},~\eqref{54a} and~\eqref{55a} with~\eqref{eq:distbnd1} and~\eqref{eq:distbnd2} (the latter two summed over $i$), we get \begin{align} \nonumber \frac1{\eta} {\mathcal I} &\leq \sum_{i,j=1}^m d[X_{i,j};X_{i,j}] + \sum_{i=1}^m (\bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}]) \\ &= m \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X_i] + \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[V_i] - \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i]. \end{align} By \Cref{compare-sums} (with $f$ taking each $j$ to the index $j'$ such that $X_{i,j}$ is a copy of $X_{j'}$) we obtain the bound \[ \bbH[V_i] \leq \bbH[\sum_{j=1}^m X_j] + \sum_{j=1}^m d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}]. \] Finally, summing over $i$ and using $D[X_{[m]}] = k$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[V_i] - \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i] & \leq \sum_{i,j=1}^m d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}] + m k \\ & = m\sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_i; X_i] + mk, \end{align*} where in the second step we used the permutation hypothesis. Combining this with~\eqref{eq:distbnd3} gives the $$ {\mathcal I} \leq 2\eta m \biggl( \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i;X_i] \biggr) + mk.$$ The claim \eqref{I-ineq} is now immediate from \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-II}.
nodes.name: Proof of Bounding mutual information
nodes.statement_short: Chain-rule corollary splits the information into A_j and B terms, bounded by minimality and Ruzsa calculus. The key step compares row sums with the minimizer via compare-sums.

nodes.statement: {\mathcal I} \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} A_j + B,
nodes.name: Equation (12.13)

nodes.statement: A_j & \leq \eta (\sum_{i = 1}^{m} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i, j}|X_{i, j} + \cdots + X_{i,m}]).
nodes.name: Equation (12.14)
nodes.label: 54a

nodes.statement: B \leq \eta \sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_{i,m}; V_i].
nodes.name: Equation (12.15)
nodes.label: 55a

nodes.statement: \nonumber &\sum_{j=1}^{m-1} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}| X_{i,j}+\cdots+X_{i,m}] \\ &\qquad \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}] + \frac12 \bigl( \bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}] \bigr).
nodes.name: Equation (12.16)
nodes.label: eq:distbnd1

nodes.statement: d[X_{i,m}; V_i] &\leq d[X_{i,m}; X_{i,m}] + \frac12 \bigl( \bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}] \bigr).
nodes.name: Equation (12.17)
nodes.label: eq:distbnd2

nodes.statement: \nonumber \frac1{\eta} {\mathcal I} &\leq \sum_{i,j=1}^m d[X_{i,j};X_{i,j}] + \sum_{i=1}^m (\bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}]) \\ &= m \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X_i] + \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[V_i] - \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i].
nodes.name: Equation (12.18)
nodes.label: eq:distbnd3

nodes.statement: Now let $m \geq 2$, let $G$ be an $m$-torsion abelian group, and let $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ be a $\tau$-minimizer.
nodes.name: $m$-torsion setting with $\tau$-minimizer

nodes.statement: By a slight abuse of notation, we identify $\Z/m\Z$ and $\{1,\dots,m\}$ in the obvious way, and let $Y_{i,j}$ be an independent copy of $X_i$ for $i,j \in \Z/m\Z$. Then also define: \[ W := \sum_{i,j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} \] and \[ Z_1 := \sum_{i,j \in \Z/m\Z} i Y_{i,j},\ \ \ Z_2 := \sum_{i,j \in \Z/m\Z} j Y_{i,j},\ \ \ Z_3 := \sum_{i,j \in \Z/m\Z} (-i-j) Y_{i,j}. \] The addition $(-i-j)$ takes place over $\Z/m\Z$. Note that, because we are assuming $G$ is $m$-torsion, it is well-defined to multiply elements of $G$ by elements of $\Z/m\Z$. We will also define for $i,j,r \in \Z/m\Z$ the variables \begin{equation} P_i := \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} , \quad Q_j := \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} , \quad R_r := \sum_{\substack{i,j \in \Z/m\Z \\ i+j=-r}} Y_{i,j} .\end{equation}
nodes.name: Additional random variables
nodes.statement_short: Copies Y_{i,j} of X_i indexed by Z/mZ, with sums W, Z_1, Z_2, Z_3, P_i, Q_j, R_r.
nodes.label: more-random

nodes.statement: P_i := \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} , \quad Q_j := \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} , \quad R_r := \sum_{\substack{i,j \in \Z/m\Z \\ i+j=-r}} Y_{i,j} .
nodes.name: Equation (12.19)
nodes.label: pqr-defs

nodes.statement: We have \begin{equation} Z_1+Z_2+Z_3= 0 \end{equation}
nodes.name: Zero-sum
nodes.label: Zero-sum

nodes.statement: Clear from definition.
nodes.name: Proof of Zero-sum
nodes.statement_short: Clear from definition.

nodes.statement: We have \[ \bbI[Z_1 : Z_2\, |\, W],\ \bbI[Z_2 : Z_3\, |\, W],\ \bbI[Z_1 : Z_3\, |\, W] \leq t \] where \begin{equation} t := m(4m+1) \eta k. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Mutual information bound
nodes.statement_short: Pairwise conditional mutual informations of Z_1,Z_2,Z_3 given W are at most t.
conclusions: \[ \bbI[Z_1 : Z_2\, |\, W],\ \bbI[Z_2 : Z_3\, |\, W],\ \bbI[Z_1 : Z_3\, |\, W] \leq t \] where \begin{equation} t := m(4m+1) \eta k. \end{equation}
nodes.label: prop:52

nodes.statement: t := m(4m+1) \eta k.
nodes.name: Equation (12.21)
nodes.label: t-def

nodes.statement: We analyze these variables by \Cref{key} in several different ways. In the first application, take $X_{i,j}=Y_{i,j}$. Note that each column $(X_{i,j})_{i=1}^m$ is indeed a permutation of $X_1,\dots,X_m$; in fact, the trivial permutation. Note also that for each $i \in \Z/m\Z$, the row sum is \[ \sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j} = \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} = P_i \] and for each $j \in \Z/m\Z$, the column sum is \[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j} = \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} = Q_j. \] Finally note that $\sum_{i,j=1}^m X_{i,j} = W$. From \Cref{key} we then have \[ \bbI[ (P_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z} : (Q_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z } \,\big|\, W ] \leq t, \] with $t$ as in~\eqref{t-def}. Since $Z_1$ is a function of $(P_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z}$ by~\eqref{pqr-defs}, and similarly $Z_2$ is a function of $(Q_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z}$, it follows immediately from \Cref{data-process} that \[ \bbI[ Z_1 : Z_2 \,|\, W ] \leq t. \] In the second application of \Cref{key}, we instead consider $X'_{i,j} = Y_{i-j,j}$. Again, for each fixed $j$, the tuple $(X'_{i,j})_{i=1}^m$ is a permutation of $X_1,\dots,X_m$. This time the row sums for $i \in \{1,\dots, m\}$ are \[ \sum_{j=1}^m X'_{i,j} = \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i-j,j} = R_{-i}. \] Similarly, the column sums for $j \in \{1,\dots, m\}$ are \[ \sum_{i=1}^m X'_{i,j} = \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i-j,j} = Q_j. \] As before, $\sum_{i,j=1}^m X'_{i,j} = W$. Hence, using~\eqref{pqr-defs} and \Cref{data-process} again, \Cref{key} tells us \[ \bbI[ Z_3 : Z_2 \,|\, W] \leq \bbI[ (R_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z} : (Q_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z } \,\big|\, W ] \leq t. \] In the third application\footnote{In fact, by permuting the variables $(Y_{i,j})_{i,j \in \Z/m\Z}$, one can see that the random variables $(W, Z_1, Z_2)$ and $(W, Z_1, Z_3)$ have the same distribution, so this is in some sense identical to -- and can be deduced from -- the first application.} of \Cref{key}, take $X''_{i,j} = Y_{i,j-i}$. The column and row sums are respectively \[ \sum_{j=1}^m X''_{i,j} = \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j-i} = P_i \] and \[ \sum_{i=1}^m X''_{i,j} = \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j-i} = R_{-j}. \] Hence, \Cref{key} and \Cref{data-process} give \[ \bbI[ Z_1 : Z_3 \,|\, W] \leq \bbI[ (P_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z} : (R_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z } \,\big|\, W ] \leq t, \] which completes the proof.
nodes.name: Proof of Mutual information bound
nodes.statement_short: Three applications of the mutual information bound to rearranged arrays, plus data processing.

nodes.statement: We have $\bbH[W] \leq (2m-1)k + \frac1m \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i]$.
nodes.name: Entropy of $W$
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of W is at most (2m-1)k plus the average entropy.
nodes.label: ent-w

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we may take $X_1,\dots,X_m$ to be independent. Write $S = \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$. Note that for each $j \in \Z/m\Z$, the sum $Q_j$ from~\eqref{pqr-defs} above has the same distribution as $S$. By \Cref{klm-1} we have \begin{align*} \bbH[W] = \bbH[\sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Q_j] & \leq \bbH[S] + \sum_{j=2}^m (\bbH[Q_1+Q_j] - \bbH[S]) \\ & = \bbH[S] + (m-1) d[S;-S]. \end{align*} By \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-IV}, we have \begin{equation} d[S; -S] \leq 2 k \end{equation} and hence \[ \bbH[W] \leq 2 k (m-1) + \bbH[S]. \] From \Cref{multidist-def} we have \begin{equation} \bbH[S] = k + \frac1m \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i], \end{equation} and the claim follows.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy of $W$
nodes.statement_short: KVM on the column sums and the bound d[S;-S] <= 2k.

nodes.statement: d[S; -S] \leq 2 k
nodes.name: Equation (12.22)
nodes.label: eq:s-bound

nodes.statement: \bbH[S] = k + \frac1m \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i],
nodes.name: Equation (12.23)
nodes.label: eq:ent-s

nodes.statement: We have $\bbH[Z_2] \leq (8m^2-16m+1) k + \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i]$.
nodes.name: Entropy of $Z_2$
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of Z_2 is at most (8m^2-16m+1)k plus the average entropy.
nodes.label: ent-z2

nodes.statement: We observe \[ \bbH[Z_2] = \bbH[\sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} j Q_j]. \] Applying \Cref{klm-1} one has \begin{align*} \bbH[Z_2] &\leq \sum_{i=2}^{m-1} \bbH[Q_1 + i Q_i] - (m-2) \bbH[S]. \end{align*} Using \Cref{sum-dilate-II} and~\eqref{eq:s-bound} we get \begin{align*} \bbH[Z_2] &\leq \bbH[S] + 4m (m-2) d[S;-S] \\ &\leq \bbH[S] + 8m (m-2) k. \end{align*} Applying~\eqref{eq:ent-s} gives the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy of $Z_2$
nodes.statement_short: KVM on the dilated column sums and the sums-of-dilates bound.

nodes.statement: We have $\bbI[W : Z_2] \leq 2 (m-1) k$.
nodes.name: Mutual information bound
nodes.label: mutual-w-z2

nodes.statement: From \Cref{alternative-mutual} we have $\bbI[W : Z_2] = \bbH[W] - \bbH[W | Z_2]$, and since $Z_2 = \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} j Q_j$ and $W = \sum_{j=1}^m Q_j$, \[ \bbH[W | Z_2] \geq \bbH[W \,|\, Q_1,\dots,Q_{m-1}] = \bbH[Q_m] = \bbH[S]. \] Hence, by \Cref{ent-w}, \[ \bbI[W : Z_2] \leq \bbH[W] - \bbH[S] \leq 2 (m-1) k, \] as claimed.
nodes.name: Proof of Mutual information bound
nodes.statement_short: Alternative formula and conditioning reduces entropy, then the bound on H[W].

nodes.statement: We have $\sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i;Z_2|W] \leq 4(m^3-m^2) k$.
nodes.name: Distance bound
nodes.statement_short: Sum of d[X_i;Z_2|W] is at most 4(m^3-m^2)k.
nodes.label: xi-z2-w-dist

nodes.statement: For each $i \in \{1,\dots, m\}$, using \Cref{klm-3} (noting the sum $Z_2$ contains $X_i$ as a summand) we have \begin{equation} d[X_i;Z_2] \leq d[X_i;X_i] + \tfrac12 (\bbH[Z_2] - \bbH[X_i]) \end{equation} and using \Cref{cond-dist-fact} we have \[ d[X_i;Z_2 | W] \leq d[X_i;Z_2] + \tfrac12 \bbI[W : Z_2]. \] Combining with~\eqref{in-a-bit-6} and \Cref{mutual-w-z2} gives \[ d[X_i;Z_2 | W] \leq d[X_i;X_i] + \tfrac12 (\bbH[Z_2] - \bbH[X_i]) + (m-1)k.\] Summing over $i$ and applying \Cref{ent-z2} gives \[ \sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_i;Z_2 | W] \leq \sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_i;X_i] + m(8m^2-16m+1) k/2 + m(m-1) k.\] Finally, applying \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-II} (and dropping some lower order terms) gives the claim.
nodes.name: Proof of Distance bound
nodes.statement_short: KVM-III and conditional distance bound, summed and combined with entropy bounds.

nodes.statement: d[X_i;Z_2] \leq d[X_i;X_i] + \tfrac12 (\bbH[Z_2] - \bbH[X_i])
nodes.name: Equation (12.24)
nodes.label: in-a-bit-6

nodes.statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically, and write \[ \delta := \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + \bbI[T_1 : T_3] + \bbI[T_2 : T_3]. \] Let $Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ be some further $G$-valued random variables and let $\alpha>0$ be a constant. Then there exists a random variable $U$ such that \begin{equation} d[U;U] + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;U] \leq \Bigl(2 + \frac{\alpha n}{2} \Bigr) \delta + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;T_2]. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Application of BSG
nodes.statement_short: From a zero-sum triple one can extract U with small self-distance and controlled distance to the Y_i.
assumptions: $G$ be an abelian group, let $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically, and write \[ \delta := \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + \bbI[T_1 : T_3] + \bbI[T_2 : T_3]. \] Let $Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ be some further $G$-valued random variables and let $\alpha>0$ be a constant
conclusions: there exists a random variable $U$ such that \begin{equation} d[U;U] + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;U] \leq \Bigl(2 + \frac{\alpha n}{2} \Bigr) \delta + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;T_2]. \end{equation}
nodes.label: lem:get-better

nodes.statement: d[U;U] + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;U] \leq \Bigl(2 + \frac{\alpha n}{2} \Bigr) \delta + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;T_2].
nodes.name: Equation (12.25)
nodes.label: eq:get-better

nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{entropic-bsg} with $X=T_1$ and $Y=T_2$. Since $T_1+T_2=-T_3$, we find that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{z} p_{T_3}(z) & d[T_1 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z;T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] \\ &\leq 3 \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + 2 \bbH[T_3] - \bbH[T_1] - \bbH[T_2] \\ &\ = \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + \bbI[T_1 : T_3] + \bbI[T_2 : T_3] = \delta, \end{split} \end{equation} where the last line follows from \Cref{relabeled-entropy} by observing \[ \bbH[T_1,T_2] = \bbH[T_1,T_3] = \bbH[T_2,T_3] = \bbH[T_1,T_2,T_3] \] since any two of $T_1,T_2,T_3$ determine the third. By~\eqref{514a} and the triangle inequality, \[ \sum_z p_{T_3}(z) d[T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z; T_2 \,|\, T_3\mathop{=}z] \leq 2 \delta \] and by \Cref{first-useful}, for each $Y_i$, \begin{align*} &\sum_z p_{T_3}(z) d[Y_i; T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] \\ &\qquad= d[Y_i; T_2 \,|\, T_3] \leq d[Y_i;T_2] + \frac12 \bbI[T_2 : T_3] \leq d[Y_i;T_2] + \frac{\delta}{2}. \end{align*} Hence, \begin{align*} &\sum_z p_{T_3}(z) \bigg( d[T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z; T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] \bigg) \\ &\qquad \leq \Bigl(2 + \frac{\alpha n}{2} \Bigr) \delta + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i; T_2], \end{align*} and the result follows by setting $U=(T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z)$ for some $z$ such that the quantity in parentheses on the left-hand side is at most the weighted average value.
nodes.name: Proof of Application of BSG
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG on (T_1,T_2), triangle inequality and averaging to pick a good fibre.

nodes.statement: \begin{split} \sum_{z} p_{T_3}(z) & d[T_1 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z;T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] \\ &\leq 3 \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + 2 \bbH[T_3] - \bbH[T_1] - \bbH[T_2] \\ &\ = \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + \bbI[T_1 : T_3] + \bbI[T_2 : T_3] = \delta, \end{split}
nodes.name: Equation (12.26)
nodes.label: 514a

nodes.statement: We have $k = 0$.
nodes.name: Vanishing entropy
nodes.label: k-vanish

nodes.statement: For each value $W=w$, apply \Cref{lem:get-better} (and \Cref{Zero-sum}) to \[ T_1 = (Z_1 \,|\, W \mathop{=} w),\ T_2 = (Z_2 \,|\, W \mathop{=} w),\ T_3 = (Z_3 \,|\, W \mathop{=} w) \] with $Y_i=X_i$ and $\alpha=\eta/m$. Write \[ \delta_w := \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + \bbI[T_1 : T_3] + \bbI[T_2 : T_3] \] for this choice, and note that \begin{align} \nonumber \delta_\ast := \sum_w p_W(w) \delta_w &= \bbI[Z_1 : Z_2 \,|\, W] + \bbI[Z_1 : Z_3 \,|\, W] + \bbI[Z_2 : Z_3 \,|\, W] \\ & \leq 3 m (4m+1) \eta k \end{align} by \Cref{prop:52}. Write $U_w$ for the random variable guaranteed to exist by \Cref{lem:get-better}, so that~\eqref{eq:get-better} gives \begin{equation} d[U_w; U_w] \leq \Bigl( 2 + \frac{\alpha m}{2} \Bigr) \delta_w + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^m \bigl( d[X_i; T_2] - d[X_i; U_w] \bigr). \end{equation} Let $(U_w)_I$ denote the tuple consisting of the same variable $U_w$ repeated $m$ times. By \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-III} \begin{equation} D[(U_w)_I] \leq m d[U_w; U_w]. \end{equation} On the other hand, from \Cref{multidist-lower} one has \begin{equation} D[(U_w)_I] \geq k - \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i;U_w]. \end{equation} Combining~\eqref{eq:uw1},~\eqref{eq:uw2} and~\eqref{eq:uw3} and averaging over $w$ (with weight $p_W(w)$), and recalling the value $\alpha=\eta/m$, gives \[ m \Bigl( 2 + \frac{\eta}{2} \Bigr) \delta_\ast + \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; Z_2 | W] \geq k \] since the terms $d[X_i; U_w]$ cancel by our choice of $\alpha$. Substituting in \Cref{xi-z2-w-dist} and~\eqref{eq:delta-w}, and using the fact that $2 + \frac{\eta}{2} < 3$, we have \[ 3 m^2 (4m+1) (2+\frac{\eta}{2}) \eta k + \eta 8(m^3-m^2) k \geq k. \] From \Cref{eta-def-multi} we have we have $$ 3 m^2 (4m+1) (2+\frac{\eta}{2}) \eta + \eta 8(m^3-m^2) < 1$$ and hence $k \leq 0$. The claim now follows from \Cref{multidist-nonneg}.
nodes.name: Proof of Vanishing entropy
nodes.statement_short: Apply the BSG extraction for each W=w and compare with minimality to get k <= c k with c < 1.

nodes.statement: \nonumber \delta_\ast := \sum_w p_W(w) \delta_w &= \bbI[Z_1 : Z_2 \,|\, W] + \bbI[Z_1 : Z_3 \,|\, W] + \bbI[Z_2 : Z_3 \,|\, W] \\ & \leq 3 m (4m+1) \eta k
nodes.name: Equation (12.27)
nodes.label: eq:delta-w

nodes.statement: d[U_w; U_w] \leq \Bigl( 2 + \frac{\alpha m}{2} \Bigr) \delta_w + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^m \bigl( d[X_i; T_2] - d[X_i; U_w] \bigr).
nodes.name: Equation (12.28)
nodes.label: eq:uw1

nodes.statement: D[(U_w)_I] \leq m d[U_w; U_w].
nodes.name: Equation (12.29)
nodes.label: eq:uw2

nodes.statement: D[(U_w)_I] \geq k - \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i;U_w].
nodes.name: Equation (12.30)
nodes.label: eq:uw3

nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ is a finite abelian group of torsion $m$. Suppose that $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable. Then there exists a subgroup $H \leq G$ such that \[ d[X;U_H] \leq 64 m^3 d[X;X].\]
nodes.name: Entropy form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Entropic PFR for m-torsion groups: d[X;U_H] <= 64 m^3 d[X;X].
assumptions: $G$ is a finite abelian group of torsion $m$. Suppose that $X$ is a $G$-valued random variable
conclusions: there exists a subgroup $H \leq G$ such that \[ d[X;U_H] \leq 64 m^3 d[X;X].\]
nodes.label: main-entropy

nodes.statement: Set $X^0 := X$. By \Cref{tau-min-exist-multi}, there exists a $\tau$-minimizer $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$. By \Cref{k-vanish}, we have $D[X_{[m]}]=0$. By \Cref{tau-ref} and the pigeonhole principle, there exists $1 \leq i \leq m$ such that $d[X_i; X] \leq \frac{2}{\eta} d[X;X]$. By \Cref{multi-zero}, we have $d[X_i;U_H]=0$ for some subgroup $H \leq G$, hence by \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} we have $d[U_H; X] \leq \frac{2}{\eta} d[X;X]$. The claim then follows from \Cref{eta-def-multi}.
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy form of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Take a tau-minimizer with reference X, show zero multidistance, then use pigeonhole and the vanishing proposition.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ is a finite abelian group of torsion $m$. If $A \subset G$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then $A$ can be covered by at most $K ^ {128m^3+1}|A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of $G$ with \begin{equation} |H|/|A| \in [K^{-256m^3}, K^{256m^3}]. \end{equation}
nodes.name: Auxiliary covering lemma for torsion PFR
nodes.statement_short: Covering lemma for torsion PFR with exponents polynomial in m.
assumptions: $G$ is a finite abelian group of torsion $m$. If $A \subset G$ is non-empty and $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by at most $K ^ {128m^3+1}|A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}$ translates of a subspace $H$ of $G$ with \begin{equation} |H|/|A| \in [K^{-256m^3}, K^{256m^3}]. \end{equation}
nodes.label: pfr_aux_torsion

nodes.statement: Repeat the proof of \Cref{pfr_aux}, but with \Cref{main-entropy} in place of \Cref{entropy-pfr}. Because of the lack of $2$-torsion, one has to use the Ruzsa triangle inequality to bound $d[U,U]$ by $2d[U,-U]$, costing an additional factor of $2$ in the estimates.
nodes.name: Proof of Auxiliary covering lemma for torsion PFR
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the auxiliary covering proof with the torsion entropic PFR.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ is an abelian group of torsion $m$ (not necessarily finite). If $A \subset G$ is a finite non-empty set with $|A+A| \leq K|A|$, then $A$ can be covered by at most $mK^{256m^3+1}$ translates of a finite subspace $H$ of $G$ with $|H| \leq |A|$.
nodes.name: PFR
nodes.statement_short: PFR for m-torsion groups: cover by m K^{256 m^3+1} translates of a finite subgroup no larger than A.
assumptions: $G$ is an abelian group of torsion $m$ (not necessarily finite). If $A \subset G$ is a finite non-empty set with $|A+A| \leq K|A|$
conclusions: $A$ can be covered by at most $mK^{256m^3+1}$ translates of a finite subspace $H$ of $G$ with $|H| \leq |A|$
nodes.label: pfr-torsion

nodes.statement: If $G$ is finite, repeat the proof of \Cref{pfr}, but with \Cref{pfr_aux_torsion} in place of \Cref{pfr_aux}. In general, reduce to the finite span of $A$ over $\mathrm{Z}/m\mathrm{Z}$.
nodes.name: Proof of PFR
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the PFR proof for finite G; reduce to the span of A in general.

nodes.statement: If $G$ is torsion-free and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables then $d[X;2Y]\leq 5d[X;Y]$.
nodes.name: Distance to $2Y$ in torsion-free groups
nodes.statement_short: In torsion-free groups, d[X;2Y] <= 5 d[X;Y].
assumptions: $G$ is torsion-free and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables
nodes.label: torsion-free-doubling

nodes.statement: Let $Y_1,Y_2$ be independent copies of $Y$ (also independent of $X$). Since $G$ is torsion-free we know $X,Y_1-Y_2,X-2Y_1$ uniquely determine $X,Y_1,Y_2$ and so \[\mathbb{H}(X,Y_1,Y_2,X-2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(X,Y_1,Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(X)+2\mathbb{H}(Y).\] Similarly \[\mathbb{H}(X,X-2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y).\] Furthermore \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2,X-2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2).\] By submodularity (\Cref{alt-submodularity}) \[\mathbb{H}(X,Y_1,Y_2,X-2Y_1)+\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)\leq \mathbb{H}(X,X-2Y_1)+\mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2,X-2Y_1).\] Combining these inequalities \[\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2)-\mathbb{H}(Y).\] Similarly we have \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1,Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(X)+2\mathbb{H}(Y),\] \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1,X-Y_1-Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(Y)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_2),\] and \[\mathbb{H}(Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(Y)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1)\] and by submodularity (\Cref{alt-submodularity}) again \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1,Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)+ \mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1,X-Y_1-Y_2)+\mathbb{H}(Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2).\] Combining these inequalities (and recalling the definition of Ruzsa distance) gives \[\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2)\leq \mathbb{H}(X-Y_1)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_2)-\mathbb{H}(X)=2d[X;Y]+\mathbb{H}(Y).\] It follows that \[\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+2d[X;Y]\] and so (using $\mathbb{H}(2Y)=\mathbb{H}(Y)$) \begin{align*} d[X;2Y] &=\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)-\mathbb{H}(X)/2-\mathbb{H}(2Y)/2\\ &\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+2d[X;Y]-\mathbb{H}(X)/2-\mathbb{H}(Y)/2\\ &= d[Y_1;Y_2]+\frac{\mathbb{H}(Y)-\mathbb{H}(X)}{2}+2d[X;Y]. \end{align*} Finally note that by the triangle inequality (\Cref{ruzsa-triangle}) we have \[d[Y_1;Y_2]\leq d[Y_1;X]+d[X;Y_2]=2d[X;Y].\] The result follows from $(\mathbb{H}(Y)-\mathbb{H}(X))/2\leq d[X;Y]$ (\Cref{ruzsa-diff}).
nodes.name: Proof of Distance to $2Y$ in torsion-free groups
nodes.statement_short: Two submodularity estimates using torsion-freeness, then triangle inequality.

nodes.statement: If $G$ is a torsion-free group and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables and $\phi:G\to \mathbb{F}_2^d$ is a homomorphism then \[\mathbb{H}(\phi(X))\leq 10d[X;Y].\]
nodes.name: Entropy of mod-2 projection in torsion-free groups
nodes.statement_short: The entropy of a homomorphic image in F_2^d is at most 10 d[X;Y].
assumptions: $G$ is a torsion-free group and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables and $\phi:G\to \mathbb{F}_2^d$ is a homomorphism
nodes.label: torsion-dist-shrinking

nodes.statement: By \Cref{fibring-ineq} and \Cref{torsion-free-doubling} we have \[d[\phi(X);\phi(2Y)]\leq d[X;2Y]\leq 5d[X;Y]\] and $\phi(2Y)=2\phi(Y)\equiv 0$ so the left-hand side is equal to $d[\phi(X);0]=\mathbb{H}(\phi(X))/2$ (using \Cref{dist-zero}).
nodes.name: Proof of Entropy of mod-2 projection in torsion-free groups
nodes.statement_short: Distance decreases under homomorphisms and phi(2Y)=0.

nodes.statement: Let $G=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$ and let $X,Y$ be $G$-valued random variables such that \[\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)> \frac{20}{\alpha} d[X;Y].\] There is a non-trivial subgroup $H\leq G$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert <\frac{1+\alpha}{2}(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))< \alpha (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] where $\psi:G\to G/H$ is the natural projection homomorphism.
nodes.name: Projection lemma from entropic PFR
nodes.statement_short: When entropies dominate distance, some nontrivial subgroup H is small and the quotient entropies shrink.
conclusions: Let $G=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$ and let $X,Y$ be $G$-valued random variables such that \[\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)> \frac{20}{\alpha} d[X;Y].\] There is a non-trivial subgroup $H\leq G$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert <\frac{1+\alpha}{2}(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))< \alpha (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] where $\psi:G\to G/H$ is the natural projection homomorphism
nodes.label: app-ent-pfr

nodes.statement: By \Cref{entropy-pfr-improv} there exists a subgroup $H$ such that $d[X;U_H] + d[Y;U_H] \leq 10 d[X;Y]$. Using \Cref{dist-projection} we deduce that $\mathbb{H}(\psi(X)) + \mathbb{H}(\psi(X)) \leq 20 d[X;Y]$. The second claim follows adding these inequalities and using the assumption on $\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)$. Furthermore we have by \Cref{ruzsa-diff} \[\log \lvert H \rvert-\mathbb{H}(X)\leq 2d[X;U_H]\] and similarly for $Y$ and thus \begin{align*} \log \lvert H\rvert &\leq \frac{\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)}{2}+d[X;U_H] + d[Y;U_H] \leq \frac{\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)}{2}+ 10d[X;Y] \\& < \frac{1+\alpha}{2}(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)). \end{align*} Finally note that if $H$ were trivial then $\psi(X)=X$ and $\psi(Y)=Y$ and hence $\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)=0$, which contradicts \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg}.
nodes.name: Proof of Projection lemma from entropic PFR
nodes.statement_short: Improved entropic PFR plus projection entropy bound; nontriviality by contradiction.

nodes.statement: If $G=\mathbb{F}_2^d$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$ and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables then there is a subgroup $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq \frac{1+\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)} (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and if $\psi:G \to G/H$ is the natural projection then \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\leq \frac{20}{\alpha} d[\psi(X);\psi(Y)].\]
nodes.name: Projection to small doubling quotient (general $\alpha$)
nodes.statement_short: There is a subgroup H with log|H| bounded and the quotient images having entropy at most 20/alpha times their distance.
assumptions: $G=\mathbb{F}_2^d$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$ and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables
conclusions: there is a subgroup $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq \frac{1+\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)} (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and if $\psi:G \to G/H$ is the natural projection then \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\leq \frac{20}{\alpha} d[\psi(X);\psi(Y)].\]
nodes.label: pfr-projection'

nodes.statement: Let $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ be a maximal subgroup such that \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))> \frac{20}{\alpha} d[\psi(X);\psi(Y)]\] and such that there exists $c \ge 0$ with \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq \frac{1+\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)}(1-c)(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\leq c (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)).\] Note that this exists since $H=\{0\}$ is an example of such a subgroup or we are done with this choice of $H$. We know that $G/H$ is a $2$-elementary group and so by Lemma \ref{app-ent-pfr} there exists some non-trivial subgroup $H'\leq G/H$ such that \[\log \lvert H'\rvert < \frac{1+\alpha}{2}(\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi' \circ\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi' \circ \psi(Y))< \alpha(\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y)))\] where $\psi':G/H\to (G/H)/H'$. By group isomorphism theorems we know that there exists some $H''$ with $H\leq H''\leq G$ such that $H'\cong H''/H$ and $\psi' \circ \psi(X)=\psi''(X)$ where $\psi'':G\to G/H''$ is the projection homomorphism. Since $H'$ is non-trivial we know that $H$ is a proper subgroup of $H''$. On the other hand we know that \[\log \lvert H''\rvert=\log \lvert H'\rvert+\log \lvert H\rvert< \frac{1+\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)}(1-\alpha c)(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi''(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi''(Y))< \alpha (\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y)))\leq \alpha c (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)).\] Therefore (using the maximality of $H$) it must be the first condition that fails, whence \[\mathbb{H}(\psi''(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi''(Y))\leq \frac{20}{\alpha}d[\psi''(X);\psi''(Y)].\]
nodes.name: Proof of Projection to small doubling quotient (general $\alpha$)
nodes.statement_short: Choose a maximal subgroup and extend it via the projection lemma, contradicting maximality.

nodes.statement: We could use the previous lemma for any value of $\alpha \in (0,1)$, which would give a whole range of estimates in Theorem~\ref{weak-pfr-int}. For definiteness, we specialize only to $\alpha=3/5$, which gives a constant $2$ in the first bound below.
nodes.name: Choice $\alpha=3/5$

nodes.statement: If $G=\mathbb{F}_2^d$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$ and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables then there is a subgroup $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq 2 (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and if $\psi:G \to G/H$ is the natural projection then \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\leq 34 d[\psi(X);\psi(Y)].\]
nodes.name: Projection to small doubling quotient ($\alpha=3/5$)
nodes.statement_short: Specialization with alpha=3/5: log|H| <= 2(H(X)+H(Y)) and quotient entropy at most 34 times distance.
assumptions: $G=\mathbb{F}_2^d$ and $\alpha\in (0,1)$ and $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables
conclusions: there is a subgroup $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq 2 (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and if $\psi:G \to G/H$ is the natural projection then \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\leq 34 d[\psi(X);\psi(Y)].\]
nodes.label: pfr-projection

nodes.statement: Specialize \Cref{pfr-projection'} to $\alpha=3/5$. In the second inequality, it gives a bound $100/3 < 34$.
nodes.name: Proof of Projection to small doubling quotient ($\alpha=3/5$)
nodes.statement_short: Specialize to alpha=3/5.

nodes.statement: Let $\phi:G\to H$ be a homomorphism and $A,B\subseteq G$ be finite subsets. If $x,y\in H$ then let $A_x=A\cap \phi^{-1}(x)$ and $B_y=B\cap \phi^{-1}(y)$. There exist $x,y\in H$ such that $A_x,B_y$ are both non-empty and \[d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\leq (\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_A))+\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_B)))(d(U_A,U_B)-d(U_{A_x},U_{B_y})).\]
nodes.name: Single fibres lemma
nodes.statement_short: Some pair of fibres A_x,B_y has distance decrease controlling their density loss.
assumptions: $\phi:G\to H$ be a homomorphism and $A,B\subseteq G$ be finite subsets. If $x,y\in H$
conclusions: let $A_x=A\cap \phi^{-1}(x)$ and $B_y=B\cap \phi^{-1}(y)$. There exist $x,y\in H$ such that $A_x,B_y$ are both non-empty and \[d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\leq (\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_A))+\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_B)))(d(U_A,U_B)-d(U_{A_x},U_{B_y})).\]
nodes.label: single-fibres

nodes.statement: The random variables $(U_A\mid \phi(U_A)=x)$ and $(U_B\mid \phi(U_B)=y)$ are equal in distribution to $U_{A_x}$ and $U_{B_y}$ respectively (both are uniformly distributed over their respective fibres). It follows from \Cref{fibring-ident} that \begin{align*} \sum_{x,y\in H}\frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}] &=d[U_A\mid \phi(U_A); U_B\mid \phi(U_B)]\\ &\leq d[U_A;U_B]-d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]. \end{align*} Therefore with $M:=\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_A))+\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_B))$ we have \[\left(\sum_{x,y\in H}\frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}Md[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]\right)+Md[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\leq Md[U_A;U_B].\] Since \[M=\sum_{x,y\in H}\frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\] we have \[\sum_{x,y\in H} \frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}\left(Md[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]+d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\right)\leq Md[U_A;U_B].\] It follows that there exists some $x,y\in H$ such that $\lvert A_x\rvert,\lvert B_y\rvert\neq 0$ and \[Md[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]+d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\leq Md[U_A;U_B].\]
nodes.name: Proof of Single fibres lemma
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity averaged over fibres, then pick a good pair of fibres.

nodes.statement: If $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^{d}$ then by $\dim(A)$ we mean the dimension of the span of $A-A$ over the reals -- equivalently, the smallest $d'$ such that $A$ lies in a coset of a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^{d'}$.
nodes.name: Dimension of a subset of $\mathbb{Z}^d$
nodes.label: dimension-def

nodes.statement: If $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ are finite non-empty sets then there exist non-empty $A'\subseteq A$ and $B'\subseteq B$ such that \[\log\frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A'\rvert\lvert B'\rvert}\leq 34d[U_A;U_B]\] such that $\max(\dim A',\dim B')\leq \frac{40}{\log 2} d[U_A;U_B]$.
nodes.name: Asymmetric weak PFR over $\mathbb{Z}^d$
nodes.statement_short: Large subsets A',B' of low dimension, with density loss bounded by 34 d[U_A;U_B].
assumptions: $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ are finite non-empty sets
conclusions: there exist non-empty $A'\subseteq A$ and $B'\subseteq B$ such that \[\log\frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A'\rvert\lvert B'\rvert}\leq 34d[U_A;U_B]\] such that $\max(\dim A',\dim B')\leq \frac{40}{\log 2} d[U_A;U_B]$
nodes.label: weak-pfr-asymm

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality we can assume that $A$ and $B$ are not both inside (possibly distinct) cosets of the same subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, or we just replace $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with that subgroup. We prove the result by induction on $\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert$. Let $\phi:\mathbb{Z}^d\to \mathbb{F}_2^d$ be the natural mod-2 homomorphism. By \Cref{torsion-dist-shrinking} \[\max(\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_A)),\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_B)))\leq 10d[U_A;U_B].\] We now apply \Cref{pfr-projection}, obtaining some subgroup $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq 40d[U_A;U_B]\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\tilde{\phi}(U_A))+\mathbb{H}(\tilde{\phi}(U_B))\leq 34 d[\tilde{\phi}(U_A);\tilde{\phi}(U_B)]\] where $\tilde{\phi}:\mathbb{Z}^d\to \mathbb{F}_2^d/H$ is $\phi$ composed with the projection onto $\mathbb{F}_2^d/H$. By \Cref{single-fibres} there exist $x,y\in \mathbb{F}_2^d/H$ such that, with $A_x=A\cap \tilde{\phi}^{-1}(x)$ and similarly for $B_y$, \[\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\leq 34(d[U_A;U_B]-d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]).\] Suppose first that $\lvert A_x\rvert+\lvert B_y\rvert=\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert$. This means that $\tilde{\phi}(A)=\{x\}$ and $\tilde{\phi}(B)=\{y\}$, and hence both $A$ and $B$ are in cosets of $\ker \tilde{\phi}$. Since by assumption $A,B$ are not in cosets of a proper subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ this means $\ker\tilde{\phi}=\mathbb{Z}^d$, and so (examining the definition of $\tilde{\phi}$) we must have $H=\mathbb{F}_2^d$. Then our bound on $\log\lvert H\rvert$ forces $d\leq \frac{40}{\log 2}d[U_A;U_B]$ and we are done with $A'=A$ and $B'=B$. Otherwise, \[\lvert A_x\rvert+\lvert B_y\rvert <\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert.\] By induction we can find some $A'\subseteq A_x$ and $B'\subseteq B_y$ such that $\dim A',\dim B'\leq \frac{40}{\log 2} d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]\leq \frac{40}{\log 2}d[U_A;U_B]$ and \[\log \frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A'\rvert\lvert B'\rvert}\leq 34d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}].\] Adding these inequalities implies \[\log\frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A'\rvert\lvert B'\rvert}\leq 34d[U_A;U_B]\] as required.
nodes.name: Proof of Asymmetric weak PFR over $\mathbb{Z}^d$
nodes.statement_short: Induction on |A|+|B| using mod-2 projection, the projection lemma and single fibres.

nodes.statement: If $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ is a finite non-empty set with $d[U_A;U_A]\leq \log K$ then there exists a non-empty $A'\subseteq A$ such that \[\lvert A'\rvert\geq K^{-17}\lvert A\rvert\] and $\dim A'\leq \frac{40}{\log 2} \log K$.
nodes.name: Symmetric weak PFR over $\mathbb{Z}^d$
nodes.statement_short: Subset A' of density K^-17 and dimension O(log K) when d[U_A;U_A] <= log K.
assumptions: $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ is a finite non-empty set with $d[U_A;U_A]\leq \log K$
conclusions: there exists a non-empty $A'\subseteq A$ such that \[\lvert A'\rvert\geq K^{-17}\lvert A\rvert\] and $\dim A'\leq \frac{40}{\log 2} \log K$
nodes.label: weak-pfr-symm

nodes.statement: Immediate from \Cref{weak-pfr-asymm} and rearranging.
nodes.name: Proof of Symmetric weak PFR over $\mathbb{Z}^d$
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the asymmetric version.

nodes.statement: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\lvert A-A\rvert\leq K\lvert A\rvert$. There exists $A'\subseteq A$ such that $\lvert A'\rvert \geq K^{-17}\lvert A\rvert$ and $\dim A' \leq \frac{40}{\log 2}\log K$.
nodes.name: Weak PFR over the integers
nodes.statement_short: Weak PFR over Z^d: small difference set gives a dense subset of dimension O(log K).
conclusions: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\lvert A-A\rvert\leq K\lvert A\rvert$. There exists $A'\subseteq A$ such that $\lvert A'\rvert \geq K^{-17}\lvert A\rvert$ and $\dim A' \leq \frac{40}{\log 2}\log K$
nodes.label: weak-pfr-int

nodes.statement: As in the beginning of \Cref{pfr} the doubling condition forces $d[U_A;U_A]\leq \log K$, and then we apply \Cref{weak-pfr-symm}.
nodes.name: Proof of Weak PFR over the integers
nodes.statement_short: Doubling gives d[U_A;U_A] <= log K, then the symmetric version.

nodes.statement: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\lvert A+A\rvert\leq K\lvert A\rvert$. There exists $A'\subseteq A$ such that $\lvert A'\rvert \geq K^{-34}\lvert A\rvert$ and $\dim A' \leq \frac{80}{\log 2}\log K$.
nodes.name: Weak PFR over the integers, sumset version
nodes.statement_short: Weak PFR over Z^d from a small sumset, with exponent 34.
conclusions: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\lvert A+A\rvert\leq K\lvert A\rvert$. There exists $A'\subseteq A$ such that $\lvert A'\rvert \geq K^{-34}\lvert A\rvert$ and $\dim A' \leq \frac{80}{\log 2}\log K$
nodes.label: weak-pfr-int-sumset

nodes.statement: By the Ruzsa triangle inequality one has $\lvert A-A\rvert \leq K^2 \lvert A\rvert$, and then we apply \Cref{weak-pfr-int}.
nodes.name: Proof of Weak PFR over the integers, sumset version
nodes.statement_short: Ruzsa triangle inequality converts the sumset bound, then weak PFR.

nodes.name: Take independent copies of X and its range A
nodes.statement: Let $X_1,X_2$ be independent copies of $X$ (from \Cref{independent-exist}). Let $A$ denote the range of $X$.
nodes.statement_short: Take independent copies of X and its range A

nodes.name: Zero distance gives H[X_1-X_2]=H[X_1]
nodes.statement: From \Cref{ruz-indep} and \Cref{ruz-copy} we have $$ \bbH[X_1-X_2] = \bbH[X_1].$$
nodes.statement_short: Zero distance gives H[X_1-X_2]=H[X_1]

nodes.name: Relabeling shows X_1-X_2 and X_1 have zero mutual informatio
nodes.statement: Observe from \Cref{relabeled-entropy-cond} that $$ \bbH[X_1-X_2|X_2] = \bbH[X_1|X_2] = \bbH[X_1]$$ and hence by \Cref{alternative-mutual} $$ \bbI[X_1-X_2 : X_1] = 0.$$
nodes.statement_short: Relabeling shows X_1-X_2 and X_1 have zero mutual information

nodes.name: Independence makes the conditional law constant, giving the
nodes.statement: By \Cref{vanish-entropy}, $X_1-X_2$ and $X_1$ are therefore independent, thus the law of $(X_1-X_2|X_1=x)$ does not depend on $x \in A$. The claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Independence makes the conditional law constant, giving the claim

nodes.name: WLOG B non-empty
nodes.statement: If $B$ is empty then the claim is trivial (with the Lean convention $0/0$), so without loss of generality $B$ is non-empty.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG B non-empty

nodes.name: Rewrite the pair count via the representation function r
nodes.statement: We can rewrite $$ |\{ (a,a') \in A \times A: a+a' \in B \}| = \sum_{b \in B} r(b)$$ where $r: G \to \N$ is the counting function $$ r(b) := |\{ (a,a') \in A \times A: a+a' = b \}|.$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the pair count via the representation function r

nodes.name: Double counting gives sum of r^2 = |G|^3 E(A)
nodes.statement: From double counting we have $$ \sum_{b \in G} r(b)^2 = |G|^3 E(A).$$
nodes.statement_short: Double counting gives sum of r^2 = |G|^3 E(A)

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz and normalization
nodes.statement: The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality then gives $$ \Bigl( \sum_{b \in B} r(b) \Bigr)^2 \leq |B| \sum_{b \in B} r(b)^2 \leq |B| \sum_{b \in G} r(b)^2 = |B|\, |G|^3 E(A),$$ and the claim follows on dividing both sides by $|G|^4$.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz and normalization

nodes.name: Introduce the graph A of f
nodes.statement: Consider the graph $A \subset G \times G'$ defined by $$ A := \{ (x,f(x)): x \in G \}.$$ Clearly, $|A| = |G|$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the graph A of f

nodes.name: Hypothesis plus Cauchy-Schwarz bound give large energy
nodes.statement: By hypothesis, we have $a+a' \in A$ for at least $|A|^2/K$ pairs $(a,a') \in A^2$. By \Cref{cs-bound}, this implies that $E(A) \geq \frac{1}{K^2} \left( \frac{|A|}{|G \times G'|} \right)^3$.
nodes.statement_short: Hypothesis plus Cauchy-Schwarz bound give large energy

nodes.name: BSG gives a large subset A' with small sumset
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{bsg}, we conclude that there exists a subset $A' \subset A$ with $|A'| \geq |A|/C_1 K^{2C_2}$ and $|A'+A'| \leq C_1C_3 K^{2(C_2+C_4)} |A'|$.
nodes.statement_short: BSG gives a large subset A' with small sumset

nodes.name: PFR covering of A' by translates of a subspace H
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{pfr-9-aux'}, we may find a subspace $H \subset G \times G'$ such that $|H| / |A'| \in [L^{-8}, L^{8}]$ and a subset $c$ of cardinality at most $L^5 |A'|^{1/2} / |H|^{1/2}$ such that $A' \subseteq c + H$, where $L = C_1C_3 K^{2(C_2+C_4)}$.
nodes.statement_short: PFR covering of A' by translates of a subspace H

nodes.name: Goursat decomposition bounds |H_1|
nodes.statement: If we let $H_0,H_1$ be as in \Cref{goursat}, this implies on taking projections the projection of $A'$ to $G$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H_0$. This implies that $$ |c| |H_0| \geq |A'|;$$ since $|H_0| |H_1| = |H|$, we conclude that $$ |H_1| \leq |c| |H|/|A'|.$$
nodes.statement_short: Goursat decomposition bounds |H_1|

nodes.name: Cover A' by translates of the graph of a homomorphism
nodes.statement: By hypothesis, $A'$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H$, and hence by at most $|c| |H_1|$ translates of $\{ (x,\phi(x)): x \in G \}$. As $\phi$ is a homomorphism, each such translate can be written in the form $\{ (x,\phi(x)+c): x \in G \}$ for some $c \in G'$.
nodes.statement_short: Cover A' by translates of the graph of a homomorphism

nodes.name: Bound the number of translates by L^10
nodes.statement: The number of translates is bounded by $$ |c|^2 \frac{|H|}{|A'|} \leq \left(L^5 \frac{|A'|^{1/2}}{|H|^{1/2}}\right)^2 \frac{|H|}{|A'|} = L^{10}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the number of translates by L^10

nodes.name: Pigeonhole gives a translate with many points
nodes.statement: By the pigeonhole principle, one of these translates must then contain at least $|A'|/L^{10} \geq |G| / (C_1C_3 K^{2(C_2+C_4)})^{10} (C_1 K^{2C_2})$ elements of $A'$ (and hence of $A$), and the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Pigeonhole gives a translate with many points

nodes.name: Apply the approximate homomorphism theorem
nodes.statement: By Theorem \ref{approx-hom-pfr}, there exists a homomorphism $\phi: G \to G'$ and a constant $c \in G'$ such that the set $A := \{ x \in G: f(x) = \phi(x) + c\}$ has cardinality at least $|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122})$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the approximate homomorphism theorem

nodes.name: Slicing gives phi' with large intersection
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{gslice}, there exists a homomorphism $\phi': G \to \Z/2\Z$ such that $$ |A \cap \phi'^{-1}(1)| \geq (|A|-1)/2 \geq (|G| / (2 ^ {144} * K ^ {122}) - 1)/2.$$
nodes.statement_short: Slicing gives phi' with large intersection

nodes.name: Take phi'' = phi + phi' c
nodes.statement: Then the claim follows by taking $\phi'' = \phi + \phi' \bullet c$ (where we view $G'$ as a $\Z/2\Z$-module).
nodes.statement_short: Take phi'' = phi + phi' c

nodes.name: WLOG X and U_H independent
nodes.statement: WLOG, we make $X$, $U_H$ independent (\Cref{independent-exist}).
nodes.statement_short: WLOG X and U_H independent

nodes.name: Two-sided bound on H(X-U_H|pi(X))
nodes.statement: Now by Lemmas \ref{submodularity}, \ref{shear-ent}, \ref{jensen-bound} \begin{align*} &\mathbb{H}(X-U_H|\pi(X)) \geq \mathbb{H}(X-U_H|X) &= \mathbb{H}(U_H) \\ &\mathbb{H}(X-U_H|\pi(X)) \leq \log |H| &= \mathbb{H}(U_H) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided bound on H(X-U_H|pi(X))

nodes.name: Chain rule gives a formula for d[X;U_H]
nodes.statement: By \Cref{chain-rule} \[\mathbb{H}(X-U_H)=\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))+\mathbb{H}(X-U_H|\pi(X))=\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))+\mathbb{H}(U_H)\] and therefore \[d[X;U_H]=\mathbb{H}(\pi(X))+\frac{\mathbb{H}(U_H)-\mathbb{H}(X)}{2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule gives a formula for d[X;U_H]

nodes.name: Entropy difference bound on d[X;U_H]
nodes.statement: Furthermore by \Cref{ruzsa-diff} \[d[X;U_H]\geq \frac{\lvert \mathbb{H}(X)-\mathbb{H}(U_H)\rvert}{2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Entropy difference bound on d[X;U_H]

nodes.name: Add the inequalities
nodes.statement: Adding these inequalities gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: Add the inequalities

nodes.name: Submodularity for X, Z, X+Y+Z
nodes.statement: From \Cref{submodularity} we have $$ \bbH[X, X + Y+ Z] + \bbH[Z, X + Y+ Z] \geq \bbH[X, Z, X + Y+ Z] + \bbH[X + Y+ Z].$$
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity for X, Z, X+Y+Z

nodes.name: Evaluate the joint entropies by independence and relabeling
nodes.statement: However, using Lemmas \ref{add-entropy}, \ref{relabeled-entropy} repeatedly we have $\bbH[X, X + Y+ Z] = \bbH[X, Y+ Z] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y+ Z]$, $\bbH[Z, X + Y + Z] = \bbH[Z, X + Y] = \bbH[Z] + \bbH[X + Y]$ and $\bbH[X, Z, X + Y+ Z] = \bbH[X, Y, Z] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y] + \bbH[Z]$.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the joint entropies by independence and relabeling

nodes.name: Calculation
nodes.statement: The claim then follows from a calculation.
nodes.statement_short: Calculation

nodes.name: Conditionally independent trials of (A,B) over Z
nodes.statement: Let $(A_1, B_1)$ and $(A_2, B_2)$ (and $Z'$, which by abuse of notation we call $Z$) be conditionally independent trials of $(A,B)$ relative to $Z$ as produced by \Cref{cond-indep-exist}, thus $(A_1,B_1)$ and $(A_2,B_2)$ are coupled through the random variable $A_1 + B_1 = A_2 + B_2$, which by abuse of notation we shall also call $Z$.
nodes.statement_short: Conditionally independent trials of (A,B) over Z

nodes.name: Rewrite the left-hand side as a conditional entropy expressi
nodes.statement: Observe from \Cref{ruz-indep} that the left-hand side of~\eqref{2-bsg-takeaway} is \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2| Z] - \bbH[A_1 | Z]/2 - \bbH[B_2 | Z]/2. \end{equation} since, crucially, $(A_1 | Z=z)$ and $(B_2 | Z=z)$ are independent for all $z$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the left-hand side as a conditional entropy expression

nodes.name: Submodularity inequality (3.4)
nodes.statement: Applying submodularity (\Cref{alt-submodularity}) gives \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\bbH[A_1 - B_2] + \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1] \\ &\qquad \leq \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1] + \bbH[A_1 - B_2,B_1]. \end{split}\end{equation} We estimate the second, third and fourth terms appearing here.
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity inequality (3.4)

nodes.name: Evaluate the joint entropy term (3.5)
nodes.statement: First note that, by \Cref{cond-trial-ent} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy} (noting that the tuple $(A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1)$ determines the tuple $(A_1, A_2, B_1, B_2)$ since $A_1+B_1=A_2+B_2$) \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1] = \bbH[A_1, B_1, A_2, B_2,Z] = 2\bbH[A,B] - \bbH[Z].\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the joint entropy term (3.5)

nodes.name: Bound (3.6)
nodes.statement: Next observe that \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2, A_1] = \bbH[A_1, B_2] \leq \bbH[A] + \bbH[B]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound (3.6)

nodes.name: Bound (3.7)
nodes.statement: Finally, we have \begin{equation} \bbH[A_1 - B_2, B_1] = \bbH[A_2 - B_1, B_1] = \bbH[A_2, B_1] \leq \bbH[A] + \bbH[B].\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound (3.7)

nodes.name: Substitute to bound H[A_1-B_2|Z]
nodes.statement: Substituting~\eqref{bsg-24},~\eqref{bsg-23} and~\eqref{bsg-25} into~\eqref{bsg-31} yields \[\bbH[A_1 - B_2] \leq 2 \bbI[A:B] + \bbH[Z]\] and so by \Cref{cond-reduce} \[\bbH[A_1 - B_2 | Z] \leq 2 \bbI[A:B] + \bbH[Z].\]
nodes.statement_short: Substitute to bound H[A_1-B_2|Z]

nodes.name: Compute H[A_1|Z], H[B_2|Z] and conclude
nodes.statement: Since \begin{align*} \bbH[A_1 | Z] & = \bbH[A_1, A_1 + B_1] - \bbH[Z] \\ & = \bbH[A,B] - \bbH[Z] \\ & = \bbH[Z] - \bbI[A:B] - 2 \bbH[Z]- \bbH[A]-\bbH[B]\end{align*} and similarly for $\bbH[B_2 | Z]$, we see that~\eqref{lhs-to-bound} is bounded by $3 \bbI[A:B] + 2\bbH[Z]-\bbH[A]-\bbH[B]$ as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Compute H[A_1|Z], H[B_2|Z] and conclude

nodes.name: Prove (3.8) first; reduce to X independent of Y,Z
nodes.statement: We first prove~\eqref{lem51-a}. We may assume (taking an independent copy, using \Cref{independent-exist} and \Cref{ruz-copy}, \ref{ruz-indep}) that $X$ is independent of $Y, Z$.
nodes.statement_short: Prove (3.8) first; reduce to X independent of Y,Z

nodes.name: Expand and apply Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman
nodes.statement: Then we have \begin{align*} d[X ;Y+ Z] & - d[X ;Y] \\ & = \bbH[X + Y + Z] - \bbH[X + Y] - \tfrac{1}{2}\bbH[Y + Z] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Y].\end{align*} Combining this with \Cref{kv} gives the required bound. The second form of the result is immediate \Cref{ruz-indep}.
nodes.statement_short: Expand and apply Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman

nodes.name: Compute I[Y:Y+Z] and apply the conditional distance bound fo
nodes.statement: Turning to~\eqref{ruzsa-3}, we have from \Cref{information-def} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy} \begin{align*} \bbI[Y : Y+ Z] & = \bbH[Y] + \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Y, Y + Z] \\ & = \bbH[Y] + \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Y, Z] = \bbH[Y + Z] - \bbH[Z],\end{align*} and so~\eqref{ruzsa-3} is a consequence of \Cref{cond-dist-fact}. Once again the second form of the result is immediate from \Cref{ruz-indep}.
nodes.statement_short: Compute I[Y:Y+Z] and apply the conditional distance bound for (3.9)

nodes.name: Chain rule for conditioned variables
nodes.statement: For each $z \in U$, we can apply \Cref{chain-rule} to the random variables $(X|Z=z)$ and $(Y|Z=z)$ to obtain $$ \bbH[(X|Z=z),(Y|Z=z)] = \bbH[Y|Z=z] + \bbH[(X|Z=z)|(Y|Z=z)].$$
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule for conditioned variables

nodes.name: Multiply by P[Z=z] and sum
nodes.statement: Now multiply by $\bbP[Z=z]$ and sum. Some helper lemmas may be needed to get to the form above. This sort of ``average over conditioning'' argument to get conditional entropy inequalities from unconditional ones is commonly used in this paper.
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by P[Z=z] and sum

nodes.name: tau depends only on the distributions
nodes.statement: By \Cref{tau-copy}, $\tau$ only depends on the probability distributions of $X_1, X_2$.
nodes.statement_short: tau depends only on the distributions

nodes.name: Compactness and continuity give a minimum
nodes.statement: This ranges over a compact space, and $\tau$ is continuous. So $\tau$ has a minimum.
nodes.statement_short: Compactness and continuity give a minimum

nodes.name: Specific fibring identity with permuted variables
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{cor-fibre}, but now with the choice \[ (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4) := (X_2, X_1, \tilde X_2, \tilde X_1). \] Now \Cref{cor-fibre} can be rewritten as \begin{align*} &d[X_1+\tilde X_1;X_2+\tilde X_2] + d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] \\ &\quad + \bbI[X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 \,|\, X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] = 2k, \end{align*} recalling once again that $k := d[X_1;X_2]$.
nodes.statement_short: Specific fibring identity with permuted variables

nodes.name: Minimality lower bound and comparison upper bounds
nodes.statement: From \Cref{cond-distance-lower} one has \begin{align*} d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1; X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] \geq k &- \eta (d[X^0_1;X_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1]) \\& - \eta (d[X^0_2;X_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2]) . \end{align*} while from \Cref{first-useful} we have \[ d[X^0_1;X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_1;X_1], \] and \[ d[X^0_2;X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_1;X_2]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Minimality lower bound and comparison upper bounds

nodes.name: Combine to bound I_2 by eta(d[X_1;X_1]+d[X_2;X_2])
nodes.statement: Combining all these inequalities with \Cref{dist-sums}, we have \begin{equation} \bbI[X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] \leq \eta ( d[X_1; X_1] + d[X_2; X_2] ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound I_2 by eta(d[X_1;X_1]+d[X_2;X_2])

nodes.name: Apply the auxiliary self-distance bound
nodes.statement: Together with \Cref{second-estimate-aux}, this gives the conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the auxiliary self-distance bound

nodes.name: Identify I(U:V|S), I(W:U|S), I(V:W|S) with I_1, I_2
nodes.statement: From the definitions of $I_1,I_2$ and \Cref{symm-lemma}, we see that \[ I_1 = I(U : V \, | \, S), \qquad I_2 = I(W : U \, | \, S), \qquad I_2 = I(V : W \, | \,S). \]
nodes.statement_short: Identify I(U:V|S), I(W:U|S), I(V:W|S) with I_1, I_2

nodes.name: First and second estimates
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{first-estimate} and \Cref{second-estimate} we have the inequalities \[ I_2 \leq 2 \eta k + \frac{2\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta} . \]
nodes.statement_short: First and second estimates

nodes.name: Sum and calculate
nodes.statement: We conclude that $$ I_1 + I_2 + I_2 \leq I_1+4\eta k+ \frac{4\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta} $$ and the claim follows from some calculation.
nodes.statement_short: Sum and calculate

nodes.name: Second comparison lemma for U
nodes.statement: By \Cref{second-useful} (taking $X = X_1^0$, $Y = X_1$, $Z = X_2$ and $Z' = \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2$, so that $Y + Z = U$ and $Y + Z + Z' = S$) we have, noting that $\bbH[Y+ Z] = \bbH[Z']$, \[ d[X^0_1;U|S] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_1]). \]
nodes.statement_short: Second comparison lemma for U

nodes.name: Further applications for the other terms
nodes.statement: Further applications of \Cref{second-useful} give \begin{align*} d[X^0_2;U|S] - d[X^0_2; X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_2]) \\ d[X^0_1;V|S] - d[X^0_1;X_1] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_1])\\ d[X^0_2;V|S] - d[X^0_2;X_2] &\leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] - \bbH[X_2]) \end{align*} and \[d[X^0_1;W|S] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] + \bbH[W] - \bbH[X_1] - \bbH[W']),\] where $W' := X_2 + \tilde X_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Further applications for the other terms

nodes.name: Treat W via W' and apply the comparison lemma
nodes.statement: To treat $d[X^0_2;W|S]$, first note that this equals $d[X^0_2;W'|S]$, since for a fixed choice $s$ of $S$ we have $W' = W + s$ (here we need some helper lemma about Ruzsa distance). Now we may apply \Cref{second-useful} to obtain \[d[X^0_2;W'|S] - d[X^0_2;X_2] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} (\bbH[S] + \bbH[W'] - \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[W]).\]
nodes.statement_short: Treat W via W' and apply the comparison lemma

nodes.name: Sum six estimates and use the four-sum bound
nodes.statement: Summing these six estimates and using \Cref{foursum-bound}, we conclude that \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \big(d[X^0_i;A|S] & - d[X^0_i;X_i]\big) \\ &\leq 3 \bbH[S] - \tfrac{3}{2} \bbH[X_1] - \tfrac{3}{2} \bbH[X_2]\\ &\leq (6 - 3\eta) k + 3(2 \eta k - I_1) \end{align*} as required.
nodes.statement_short: Sum six estimates and use the four-sum bound

nodes.name: Entropic BSG with (A,B)=(T_1,T_2)
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{entropic-bsg} with $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there. Since $T_1 + T_2 = T_3$, the conclusion is that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] & d[(T_1 | T_3 = t_3); (T_2 | T_3 = t_3)] \\ & \leq 3 \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + 2 \bbH[T_3] - \bbH[T_1] - \bbH[T_2]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG with (A,B)=(T_1,T_2)

nodes.name: Rearrange the right side to delta
nodes.statement: The right-hand side in~\eqref{bsg-t1t2} can be rearranged as \begin{align*} & 2( \bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - 3 \bbH[T_1,T_2] \\ & = 2(\bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - \bbH[T_1,T_2] - \bbH[T_2,T_3] - \bbH[T_1, T_3] = \delta,\end{align*} using the fact (from \Cref{relabeled-entropy}) that all three terms $\bbH[T_i,T_j]$ are equal to $\bbH[T_1,T_2,T_3]$ and hence to each other.
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange the right side to delta

nodes.name: Bound the reference-distance terms by the conditional distan
nodes.statement: We also have \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} P[T_3 = t_3] \bigl(d[X^0_1; (T_1 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_1;X_1]\bigr) \\ &\quad = d[X^0_1; T_1 | T_3] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \leq d[X^0_1;T_1] - d[X^0_1;X_1] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[T_1 : T_3] \end{align*} by \Cref{cond-dist-fact}, and similarly \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] (d[X^0_2;(T_2 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_2; X_2]) \\ &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \leq d[X^0_2;T_2] - d[X^0_2;X_2] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[T_2 : T_3]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the reference-distance terms by the conditional distance bound

nodes.name: Combine and introduce psi
nodes.statement: Putting the above observations together, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3=t_3] \psi[(T_1 | T_3=t_3); (T_2 | T_3=t_3)] \leq \delta + \eta (d[X^0_1;T_1]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) \\ + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2]-d[X^0_2;X_2]) + \tfrac12 \eta \bbI[T_1:T_3] + \tfrac12 \eta \bbI[T_2:T_3] \end{align*} where we introduce the notation \[\psi[Y_1; Y_2] := d[Y_1;Y_2] + \eta (d[X_1^0;Y_1] - d[X_1^0;X_1]) + \eta(d[X_2^0;Y_2] - d[X_2^0;X_2]).\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine and introduce psi

nodes.name: Minimality gives k <= psi
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from \Cref{distance-lower} we have $k \leq \psi[Y_1;Y_2]$, and the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Minimality gives k <= psi

nodes.name: Apply the good-variable lemma to any zero-sum triple
nodes.statement: Set $k := d[X_1;X_2]$. Applying \Cref{construct-good} with any random variables $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically, we deduce that \[ k \leq \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (d[X^0_1;T_j] - d[X^0_i;X_i]) \biggr). \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the good-variable lemma to any zero-sum triple

nodes.name: Specialize to (U,V,W) conditioned on S and average
nodes.statement: Note that $\delta$ is still defined by~\eqref{delta-t1t2t3-def} and thus depends on $T_1,T_2,T_3$. In particular we may apply this for \[ T_1 = (U | S = s),\qquad T_2 = (V | S = s), \qquad T_3 = (W | S = s) \] for $s$ in the range of $S$ (which is a valid choice by \Cref{key-ident}) and then average over $s$ with weights $p_S(s)$, to obtain \[k \leq \tilde \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \tilde \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \bigl( d[X^0_i;A|S] - d[X^0_i;X_i]\bigr) \biggr),\] where \[ \tilde \delta := \bbI[U : V | S] + \bbI[V : W | S] + \bbI[W : U | S]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Specialize to (U,V,W) conditioned on S and average

nodes.name: Combine with the mutual information and distance bounds
nodes.statement: Putting this together with \Cref{uvw-s} and \Cref{total-dist}, we conclude that \begin{align*} k &\leq \Bigl(1+\frac{\eta}{3}\Bigr)\Bigl(6\eta k-\frac{1-5\eta}{1-\eta}(2\eta k-I_1)\Bigr)+\frac{\eta}{3}\Bigl((6-3\eta)k+3(2\eta k-I_1)\Bigr)\\ &= (8\eta + \eta^2) k - \biggl( \frac{1 - 5 \eta}{1-\eta}\Bigl(1 + \frac{\eta}{3}\Bigr) - \eta \biggr)(2 \eta k - I_1)\\ &\leq (8 \eta + \eta^2) k \end{align*} since the quantity $2 \eta k - I_1$ is non-negative (by \Cref{first-estimate}), and its coefficient in the above expression is non-positive provided that $\eta(2\eta + 17) \le 3$, which is certainly the case with \Cref{eta-def}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the mutual information and distance bounds

nodes.name: 8 eta + eta^2 < 1 forces k=0
nodes.statement: Moreover, from \Cref{eta-def} we have $8 \eta + \eta^2 < 1$. It follows that $k=0$, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: 8 eta + eta^2 < 1 forces k=0

nodes.name: Take a tau-minimizer; it has zero distance
nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2$ be the $\tau$-minimizer from \Cref{tau-min}. From \Cref{de-prop}, $d[X_1;X_2]=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a tau-minimizer; it has zero distance

nodes.name: 100% inverse theorem gives H
nodes.statement: From \Cref{lem:100pc}, $d[X_1;U_H] = d[X_2; U_H] = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: 100% inverse theorem gives H

nodes.name: Minimality and the triangle inequality
nodes.statement: Also from $\tau$-minimization we have $\tau[X_1;X_2] \leq \tau[X^0_2;X^0_1]$. Using this and the Ruzsa triangle inequality we can conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Minimality and the triangle inequality

nodes.name: Take Z_1,Z_2 independent
nodes.statement: Let $Z_1,Z_2$ be independent throughout (this is possible by \Cref{ruz-copy} and \Cref{independent-exist}).
nodes.statement_short: Take Z_1,Z_2 independent

nodes.name: Expand the conditional distance and apply submodularity
nodes.statement: By \Cref{cond-dist-alt}, We have \begin{align*} & d[Z_1 |\pi(Z_1); Z_2 |\pi(Z_2)] \\ & = \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)] \\ & \leq \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1+Z_2)] - \tfrac{1}{2} \bbH[Z_1 | \pi(Z_1)] - \tfrac{1}{2}H[Z_2 | \pi(Z_2)] \\ & = d[Z_1;Z_2] - d[\pi(Z_1);\pi(Z_2)]. \end{align*} In the middle step, we used \Cref{submodularity}, and in the last step we used the fact that \[\bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1-Z_2)] = \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2] - \bbH[\pi(Z_1-Z_2)]\] (thanks to \Cref{chain-rule} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy}) and that \[\bbH[Z_i| \pi(Z_i)] = \bbH[Z_i] - \bbH[\pi(Z_i)]\] (since $Z_i$ determines $\pi(Z_i)$). This gives the claimed inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the conditional distance and apply submodularity

nodes.name: Identify the difference of the two sides
nodes.statement: The difference between the two sides is precisely \[\bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)] - \bbH[Z_1 - Z_2 | \pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)].\]
nodes.statement_short: Identify the difference of the two sides

nodes.name: Rewrite the difference as conditional mutual information
