nodes.statement: To rewrite this in terms of (conditional) mutual information, we use the identity \[\bbH[A|B] - \bbH[A | B,C] = \bbI[A : C | B],\] (which follows \Cref{conditional-mutual-alt}) taking $A := Z_1 - Z_2$, $B := \pi(Z_1 - Z_2)$ and $C := (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_{2}))$, and noting that in this case $\bbH[A | B,C] = \bbH[A | C]$ since $C$ uniquely determines $B$ (this may require another helper lemma about entropy). This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the difference as conditional mutual information

nodes.name: Apply general fibring to the addition map
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{fibring-ident} with $H := G \times G$, $H' := G$, $\pi$ the addition homomorphism $\pi(x,y) := x+y$, and with the random variables $Z_1 := (Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Z_2 := (Y_2,Y_4)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply general fibring to the addition map

nodes.name: Compute the distance terms
nodes.statement: Then by independence (\Cref{add-entropy}) \[ d[Z_1; Z_2] = d[Y_1; Y_2] + d[Y_3; Y_4] \] while by definition \[ d[\pi(Z_1); \pi(Z_2)] = d[Y_1+Y_3; Y_2+Y_4]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute the distance terms

nodes.name: Identify the conditional distance
nodes.statement: Furthermore, \[ d[Z_1|\pi(Z_1); Z_2|\pi(Z_2)] = d[Y_1|Y_1+Y_3;Y_2|Y_2+Y_4], \] since $Z_1=(Y_1,Y_3)$ and $Y_1$ are linked by an invertible affine transformation once $\pi(Z_1)=Y_1+Y_3$ is fixed, and similarly for $Z_2$ and $Y_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the conditional distance

nodes.name: Identify the mutual information term
nodes.statement: (This has to do with \Cref{relabeled-entropy-cond}) Finally, we have \begin{align*} &\bbI[Z_1 + Z_2 : (\pi(Z_1),\pi(Z_2)) \,|\, \pi(Z_1) + \pi(Z_2)] \\ &\ = \bbI[(Y_1+Y_2, Y_3+Y_4) : (Y_1+Y_3, Y_2+Y_4) \,|\, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4] \\ &\ = \bbI[Y_1+Y_2 : Y_2+Y_4 \,|\, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4] \end{align*} where in the last line we used the fact that $(Y_1+Y_2, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_3+Y_4$ and similarly $(Y_2+Y_4, Y_1+Y_2+Y_3+Y_4)$ uniquely determine $Y_1+Y_3$. (This requires another helper lemma about entropy.)
nodes.statement_short: Identify the mutual information term

nodes.name: Log sum lower bound for every T
nodes.statement: For every $G$-valued random variable $T$ that is independent of $Y$, $$D_{KL}(U_H \Vert U_A+T) = \sum_{h\in H} \frac{1}{|H|}\log\frac{1/|H|}{\mathbf{P}[U_A+T=h]}\ge -\log(\mathbf{P}[U_A+T\in H]),$$ by \Cref{log-sum}.
nodes.statement_short: Log sum lower bound for every T

nodes.name: Maximize over translates to prove the lower bound
nodes.statement: Then observe that $$-\log(\mathbf{P}[U_A+T\in H])=-\log(\mathbf{P}[U_A\in H-T])\ge -\log(\max_{t\in G} \mathbf{P}[U_A\in H+t]).$$ This proves $\ge$.
nodes.statement_short: Maximize over translates to prove the lower bound

nodes.name: Choice T = U_H - t* gives equality
nodes.statement: To get the equality, let $t^*:=\arg\max_t |A \cap (H+t)|$ and observe that $$\rho^-(U_H)\le D_{KL}(U_H \Vert U_A+(U_H-t^*))= \log |A| - \log \max_t|A \cap (H+t)|.$$
nodes.statement_short: Choice T = U_H - t* gives equality

nodes.name: First claim from the subgroup formulas
nodes.statement: The first claim is a direct corollary of \Cref{rhominus-subgroup} and \Cref{rhoplus-subgroup}.
nodes.statement_short: First claim from the subgroup formulas

nodes.name: Nonnegativity of rho^- and rho^+ of U_H
nodes.statement: To see the second claim, observe that \Cref{rhominus-nonneg} and \Cref{rhoplus-subgroup} imply $\rho^-(U_H),\rho^+(U_H)\ge 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegativity of rho^- and rho^+ of U_H

nodes.name: Bound the entropy difference by 2 rho
nodes.statement: Therefore $$|H(U_A)-H(U_H)|=|\rho^+(U_H)-\rho^-(U_H)|\le \rho^-(U_H)+\rho^+(U_H)= 2\rho(U_H)\le 2r,$$ which implies the second claim.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the entropy difference by 2 rho

nodes.name: First chain of bounds on rho(T_1|T_2,S)
nodes.statement: Let $T_1':=Y_3+Y_4$, $T_2':=Y_2+Y_4$. First note that \begin{align*} \rho(T_1|T_2,S) &\le \rho(T_1|S) + \frac{1}{2}\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S) \\ &\le \frac{1}{2}(\rho(T_1)+\rho(T_1'))+\frac{1}{2}(d[T_1;T_1']+\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S)) \\ &\le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_2]+d[Y_3;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[T_1;T_1']+\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S)). \end{align*} by \Cref{rho-cond}, \Cref{rho-cond-sym}, \Cref{rho-sums-sym} respectively.
nodes.statement_short: First chain of bounds on rho(T_1|T_2,S)

nodes.name: Second chain of bounds on rho(T_1|T_2,S)
nodes.statement: On the other hand, observe that \begin{align*} \rho(T_1|T_2,S) &=\rho(Y_1+Y_2|T_2,T_2') \\ &\le \frac{1}{2}(\rho(Y_1|T_2)+\rho(Y_2|T_2'))+\frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1|T_2;Y_2|T_2']) \\ &\le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_3]+d[Y_2;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1|T_2;Y_2|T_2']). \end{align*} by \Cref{rho-cond-relabeled}, \Cref{rho-sums-sym}, \Cref{rho-cond-sym} respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Second chain of bounds on rho(T_1|T_2,S)

nodes.name: Symmetric bounds for rho(T_2|T_1,S)
nodes.statement: By replacing $(Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4)$ with $(Y_1,Y_3,Y_2,Y_4)$ in the above inequalities, one has $$\rho(T_2|T_1,S) \le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_3]+d[Y_2;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[T_2;T_2']+\bbI(T_1:T_2\mid S))$$ and $$\rho(T_2|T_1,S) \le \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i} \rho(Y_i) +\frac{1}{4}(d[Y_1;Y_2]+d[Y_3;Y_4]) + \frac{1}{2}(d[Y_1|T_1;Y_3|T_1']).$$
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric bounds for rho(T_2|T_1,S)

nodes.name: Sum and apply the fibring identity
nodes.statement: Finally, take the sum of all four inequalities, apply \Cref{cor-fibre} on $(Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4)$ and $(Y_1,Y_3,Y_2,Y_4)$ to rewrite the sum of last terms in the four inequalities, and divide the result by $2$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum and apply the fibring identity

nodes.name: Define the zero-sum triple and S
nodes.statement: Consider $T_1:=X_1+X_2,T_2:=X_1+\tilde X_1, T_3:=\tilde X_1 + X_2$, and $S=X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2$. Note that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the zero-sum triple and S

nodes.name: Symmetrized rho-BSG bound conditioned on S
nodes.statement: First apply \Cref{rho-BSG-triplet-symmetrized} on $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ when conditioned on $S$ to get \begin{align} d[X_1;X_2] &\leq \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} \bbI[T_i:T_j\mid S] + \frac{\eta}{3} \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) -\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2))\nonumber\\ &= (I_1+2I_2) + \frac{\eta}{3} \sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) -\rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2)). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrized rho-BSG bound conditioned on S

nodes.name: Rho increment bound and the I_1-I_2 identity
nodes.statement: Then apply \Cref{rho-increase-symmetrized} on $(X_1,X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2)$ and get $$\sum_{1 \leq i<j \leq 3} (\rho(T_i|T_j,S) + \rho(T_j|T_i,S) - \rho(X_1)-\rho(X_2))\le (4d[X_1;X_2]+d[X_1;X_2]+d[X_2;X_2])= 6 d[X_1;X_2]+(I_2-I_1)$$ by \Cref{I1-I2-diff}.
nodes.statement_short: Rho increment bound and the I_1-I_2 identity

nodes.name: Plug into (7.1)
nodes.statement: Plug in the inequality above to (\ref{eq:further-bsg}), we get $$d[X_1;X_2] \le (I_1+2I_2)+2\eta d[X_1;X_2]+\frac{\eta}{3}(I_2-I_1).$$
nodes.statement_short: Plug into (7.1)

nodes.name: Second phi-estimate
nodes.statement: By \Cref{phi-second-estimate} we can conclude that $$d[X_1;X_2] \le 8\eta d[X_1;X_2]-\frac{3-10\eta}{3-3\eta} (2\eta d[X_1;X_2]-I_1).$$
nodes.statement_short: Second phi-estimate

nodes.name: First phi-estimate and eta < 1/8 give d=0
nodes.statement: Finally by \Cref{phi-first-estimate} and $\eta<1$ we get that the second term is $\le 0$, and thus $d[X_1;X_2] \le 8\eta d[X_1;X_2]$. By the choice $\eta<1/8$ and the non-negativity of $d$ we have $d[X_1;X_2]=0$.
nodes.statement_short: First phi-estimate and eta < 1/8 give d=0

nodes.name: phi-minimizer has zero distance; let eta tend to 1/8
nodes.statement: Let $X_1,X_2$ be a $\phi$-minimizer. By \Cref{phi-minimizer-zero-distance} $d[X_1;X_2]=0$, which by \Cref{phi-min-def} implies $\rho(X_1)+\rho(X_2)\le \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + \frac{1}{\eta} d[Y_1;Y_2]$ for every $\eta<1/8$. Take the limit at $\eta=1/8$ to get $\rho(X_1)+\rho(X_2)\le \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + 8 d[Y_1;Y_2]$.
nodes.statement_short: phi-minimizer has zero distance; let eta tend to 1/8

nodes.name: Minimizers are translates of uniform subgroup variables
nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} and \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg} we have $d[X_1;X_1]=d[X_2;X_2]=0$, and by \Cref{sym-zero} there are $H_1:=\mathrm{Sym}[X_1],H_2:=\mathrm{Sym}[X_2]$ such that $X_1=U_{H_1}+x_1$ and $X_2=U_{H_2}+x_2$ for some $x_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Minimizers are translates of uniform subgroup variables

nodes.name: Translation invariance of rho
nodes.statement: By \Cref{rho-invariant} we get $\rho(U_{H_1})+\rho(U_{H_2})\le \rho(Y_1) + \rho(Y_2) + 8 d[Y_1;Y_2]$, and thus the claim holds for $H=H_1$ or $H=H_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Translation invariance of rho

nodes.name: Apply rho form of PFR to U_A
nodes.statement: Apply \Cref{pfr-rho} on $U_A,U_A$ to get a subspace such that $2\rho(U_H)\le 2\rho(U_A)+8d[U_A;U_A]$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply rho form of PFR to U_A

nodes.name: Recall d[U_A;U_A] <= log K and rho(U_A)=0
nodes.statement: Recall that $d[U_A;U_A]\le \log K$ as proved in \Cref{pfr_aux}, and $\rho(U_A)=0$ by \Cref{rho-init}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall d[U_A;U_A] <= log K and rho(U_A)=0

nodes.name: Hence rho(U_H) <= 4 log K
nodes.statement: Therefore $\rho(U_H)\le 4\log(K)$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence rho(U_H) <= 4 log K

nodes.name: Rho of subgroup lemma
nodes.statement: The claim then follows from \Cref{rho-subgroup}.
nodes.statement_short: Rho of subgroup lemma

nodes.name: Define H_0 and H_1
nodes.statement: We can take $H_0$ to be the projection of $H$ to $G$, and $H_1$ to be the slice $H_1 := \{ y: (0,y) \in H \}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define H_0 and H_1

nodes.name: Construct phi greedily and extend; count
nodes.statement: One can construct $\phi$ on $H_0$ one generator at a time by the greedy algorithm, and then extend to $G$ by \Cref{hb-thm}. The cardinality bound is clear from direct counting.
nodes.statement_short: Construct phi greedily and extend; count

nodes.name: Introduce the graph A of f
nodes.statement: Consider the graph $A \subset G \times G'$ defined by $$ A := \{ (x,f(x)): x \in G \}.$$ Clearly, $|A| = |G|$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the graph A of f

nodes.name: |A+A| <= |S||A|
nodes.statement: By hypothesis, we have $$ A+A \subset \{ (x,f(x)+s): x \in G, s \in S\}$$ and hence $|A+A| \leq |S| |A|$.

nodes.name: PFR covering by translates of H
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{pfr-9-aux'}, we may find a subspace $H \subset G \times G'$ such that $|H|/ |A| \in [|S|^{-8}, |S|^{8}]$ and $A$ is covered by $c + H$ with $|c| \le |S|^5|A|^{1/2} / |H|^{1/2}$.
nodes.statement_short: PFR covering by translates of H

nodes.name: Goursat bounds |H_1|
nodes.statement: If we let $H_0, H_1$ be as in \Cref{goursat}, this implies on taking projections that $G$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H_0$. This implies that $$ |c| |H_0| \geq |G|;$$ since $|H_0| |H_1| = |H|$, we conclude that $$ |H_1| \leq |c| |H|/|G| = |c| |H|/|A|.$$
nodes.statement_short: Goursat bounds |H_1|

nodes.name: Cover A by translates of the graph of phi
nodes.statement: By hypothesis, $A$ is covered by at most $|c|$ translates of $H$, and hence by at most $|c| |H_1|$ translates of $\{ (x,\phi(x)): x \in G \}$. As $\phi$ is a homomorphism, each such translate can be written in the form $\{ (x,\phi(x)+d): x \in G \}$ for some $d \in G'$.
nodes.statement_short: Cover A by translates of the graph of phi

nodes.name: Count translates
nodes.statement: Since $$ |c| |H_1| \le |c|^2 \frac{|H|}{|A|} \le \left(|S|^5 \frac{|A|^{1/2}}{|H|^{1/2}}\right)^2 \frac{|H|}{|A|} = |S|^{10}, $$ the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Count translates

nodes.name: Entropic BSG with (A,B)=(T_1,T_2)
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{entropic-bsg} with $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there. Since $T_1 + T_2 = T_3$, the conclusion is that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] & d[(T_1 | T_3 = t_3); (T_2 | T_3 = t_3)] \\ & \leq 3 \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + 2 \bbH[T_3] - \bbH[T_1] - \bbH[T_2]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG with (A,B)=(T_1,T_2)

nodes.name: Rearrange the right side to delta
nodes.statement: The right-hand side in~\eqref{bsg-t1t2'} can be rearranged as \begin{align*} & 2( \bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - 3 \bbH[T_1,T_2] \\ & = 2(\bbH[T_1] + \bbH[T_2] + \bbH[T_3]) - \bbH[T_1,T_2] - \bbH[T_2,T_3] - \bbH[T_1, T_3] = \delta,\end{align*} using the fact (from \Cref{relabeled-entropy}) that all three terms $\bbH[T_i,T_j]$ are equal to $\bbH[T_1,T_2,T_3]$ and hence to each other.
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange the right side to delta

nodes.name: Express the reference-distance terms as conditional distance
nodes.statement: We also have \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} P[T_3 = t_3] \bigl(d[X^0_1; (T_1 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_1;X_1]\bigr) \\ &\quad = d[X^0_1; T_1 | T_3] - d[X^0_1;X_1] \end{align*} and similarly \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3 = t_3] (d[X^0_2;(T_2 | T_3=t_3)] - d[X^0_2; X_2]) \\ &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \leq d[X^0_2;T_2|T_3] - d[X^0_2;X_2]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Express the reference-distance terms as conditional distances

nodes.name: Combine and introduce psi
nodes.statement: Putting the above observations together, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t_3} \bbP[T_3=t_3] \psi[(T_1 | T_3=t_3); (T_2 | T_3=t_3)] \leq \delta + \eta (d[X^0_1;T_1|T_3]-d[X^0_1;X_1]) \\ + \eta (d[X^0_2;T_2|T_3]-d[X^0_2;X_2]) \end{align*} where we introduce the notation \[\psi[Y_1; Y_2] := d[Y_1;Y_2] + \eta (d[X_1^0;Y_1] - d[X_1^0;X_1]) + \eta(d[X_2^0;Y_2] - d[X_2^0;X_2]).\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine and introduce psi

nodes.name: Minimality gives k <= psi
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from \Cref{distance-lower} we have $k \leq \psi[Y_1;Y_2]$, and the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Minimality gives k <= psi

nodes.name: First bound via conditional distance and comparison lemmas
nodes.statement: On the one hand, by \Cref{cond-dist-fact} and two applications of \Cref{first-useful} we have \begin{align*} &d[Y;X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1+X_2|S] + \tfrac{1}{2} \bbI[X_1 + X_2 : X_1 + X_3|S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1+X_2]\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1+X_2;X_3+X_4] + \bbI[X_1 + X_2 : X_1 + X_3|S])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4])\\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1;X_2] + d[X_1+X_2;X_3+X_4] + \bbI[X_1 + X_2 : X_1 + X_3|S])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4] + \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[X_1]). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: First bound via conditional distance and comparison lemmas

nodes.name: Fibring identity for (X_3,X_1,X_4,X_2)
nodes.statement: From \Cref{cor-fibre} (with $Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4$ set equal to $X_3, X_1, X_4, X_2$ respectively) one has $$ d[X_3+X_4; X_1+X_2] + d[X_3|X_3+X_4; X_1|X_1+X_2] $$ $$ + \bbI[X_3 + X_1 : X_1 + X_2|S] = d[X_3;X_1] + d[X_4;X_2].$$
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity for (X_3,X_1,X_4,X_2)

nodes.name: Rearrange into the first bound
nodes.statement: Rearranging the mutual information and Ruzsa distances slightly, we conclude that \begin{align*} &d[Y;X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1;X_2] + d[X_1;X_3] + d[X_2;X_4] - d[X_3|X_3+X_4; X_1|X_1+X_2])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_3+X_4] + \bbH[X_2] - \bbH[X_1]). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange into the first bound

nodes.name: Second bound via conditioned independent sums
nodes.statement: On the other hand, $(X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S)$ has an identical distribution to the independent sum of $(X_1|X_1+X_3)$ and $(X_2|X_2+X_4)$. We may therefore apply \Cref{first-useful} to conditioned variables $(X_1|X_1+X_3=s)$ and $(X_2|X_2+X_4=t)$ and average in $s,t$ to obtain the alternative bound \begin{align*} & d[Y;X_1+X_2|X_1 + X_3, S] \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1|X_1+X_3] + \tfrac{1}{2} d[X_1|X_1+X_3; X_2|X_2+X_4] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_2|X_2+X_4] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_3]) \\ &\quad \leq d[Y;X_1] \\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2} (d[X_1;X_3] + d[X_1|X_1+X_3;X_2|X_2+X_4])\\ &\qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_2|X_2+X_4] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_3] + \bbH[X_1] - \bbH[X_3]). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Second bound via conditioned independent sums

nodes.name: Average the two bounds
nodes.statement: If one takes the arithmetic mean of these two bounds and simplifies using \Cref{cor-fibre}, one obtains the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Average the two bounds

nodes.name: General inequality over permutations for X_1^0
nodes.statement: If we apply \Cref{gen-ineq} with $X_1:=X_1$, $Y:=X_1^0$ and $(X_2,X_3,X_4)$ equal to the $3!$ permutations of $(X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2)$, and sums (using the symmetry $\bbH[X|X+Y] = \bbH[Y|X+Y]$, which follows from \Cref{relabeled-entropy-cond}), we can bound $$ \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} d[X_1^0;A|B, S] - d[X_1^0;X_1]$$ by \begin{align*} &\quad \tfrac{1}{4} (6d[X_1;X_2] + 6d[X_1;\tilde X_2]\\ &\qquad + 6d[X_1;\tilde X_1] + 2d[\tilde X_1;\tilde X_2] + 2 d[\tilde X_1;X_2] + 2d[X_2;\tilde X_2])\\ &\quad + \tfrac{1}{8} (2\bbH[X_1+X_2] + 2\bbH[X_1+\tilde X_1] + 2 \bbH[X_1+\tilde X_2] \\ &\qquad - 2\bbH[\tilde X_1+X_2] - 2\bbH[X_2+\tilde X_2] - 2\bbH[\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (\bbH[X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] + \bbH[\tilde X_1|\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2] + \bbH[\tilde X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2] \\ &\qquad \qquad \qquad - \bbH[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+X_2] - \bbH[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2]), \end{align*} which simplifies to \begin{align*} &\quad \tfrac{1}{4} (16k + 6d[X_1;X_1] + 2d[X_2;X_2])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (H[X_1+\tilde X_1] - H[X_2+\tilde X_2] + d[X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2] - d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1]). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: General inequality over permutations for X_1^0

nodes.name: Symmetric bound for X_2^0
nodes.statement: A symmetric argument also bounds $$ \sum_{A,B \in \{U,V,W\}: A \neq B} d[X_2^0;A|B, S] - d[X_2^0;X_2]$$ by \begin{align*} &\quad \tfrac{1}{4} (16k + 6d[X_2;X_2] + 2d[X_1;X_1])\\ &\qquad \qquad + \tfrac{1}{4} (H[X_2+\tilde X_2] - H[X_1+\tilde X_1] + d[X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1] - d[X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2]). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric bound for X_2^0

nodes.name: Self-distance bound
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from \Cref{second-estimate-aux} one has $$ d[X_1;X_1] + d[X_2;X_2] \leq 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Self-distance bound

nodes.name: Sum the three estimates
nodes.statement: Summing the previous three estimates, we obtain the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the three estimates

nodes.name: Minimizers for eta < 1/8 have zero distance
nodes.statement: For each $\eta<1/8$, consider minimizers $X_1^\eta$ and $X_2^\eta$ from \Cref{tau-min}. By \Cref{de-prop-improv}, they satisfy $d[X_1^\eta; X_2^\eta]=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Minimizers for eta < 1/8 have zero distance

nodes.name: Extract a convergent subsequence
nodes.statement: By compactness of the space of probability measures on $G$, one may extract a converging subsequence of the distributions of $X_1^\eta$ and $X_2^\eta$ as $\eta \to 1/8$.
nodes.statement_short: Extract a convergent subsequence

nodes.name: Continuity gives the limit minimizers
nodes.statement: By continuity of all the involved quantities, the limit is a pair of tau-minimizers for $1/8$ satisfying additionally $d[X_1;X_2] = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity gives the limit minimizers

nodes.name: Take the good tau-minimizer with zero distance
nodes.statement: Let $X_1, X_2$ be the good $\tau$-minimizer from \Cref{de-prop-lim-improv}. By construction, $d[X_1;X_2]=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Take the good tau-minimizer with zero distance

nodes.name: 100% inverse theorem
nodes.statement: From \Cref{lem:100pc}, $d[X_1;U_H] = d[X_2; U_H] = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: 100% inverse theorem

nodes.name: Minimality and triangle inequality
nodes.statement: Also from $\tau$-minimization we have $\tau[X_1;X_2] \leq \tau[X^0_2;X^0_1]$. Using this and the Ruzsa triangle inequality we can conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Minimality and triangle inequality

nodes.name: Uniform variable U_A with entropy log|A|
nodes.statement: Let $U_A$ be the uniform distribution on $A$ (which exists by \Cref{unif-exist}), thus $\bbH[U_A] = \log |A|$ by \Cref{uniform-entropy-II}.
nodes.statement_short: Uniform variable U_A with entropy log|A|

nodes.name: Jensen bound on H[U_A+U_A]
nodes.statement: By \Cref{jensen-bound} and the fact that $U_A + U_A$ is supported on $A + A$, $\bbH[U_A + U_A] \leq \log|A+A|$.
nodes.statement_short: Jensen bound on H[U_A+U_A]

nodes.name: d[U_A;U_A] <= log K
nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruz-dist-def}, the doubling condition $|A+A| \leq K|A|$ therefore gives \[d[U_A;U_A] \leq \log K.\]
nodes.statement_short: d[U_A;U_A] <= log K

nodes.name: Entropic PFR gives H
nodes.statement: By \Cref{entropy-pfr}, we may thus find a subspace $H$ of $\F_2^n$ such that \begin{equation} d[U_A;U_H] \leq \tfrac{1}{2} C' \log K\end{equation} with $C' = 11$.
nodes.statement_short: Entropic PFR gives H

nodes.name: Entropy difference bound proves (11.1)
nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruzsa-diff} we conclude that \begin{equation*} |\log |H| - \log |A|| \leq C' \log K, \end{equation*} proving~\eqref{ah}.
nodes.statement_short: Entropy difference bound proves (11.1)

nodes.name: Rewrite (11.2) as an entropy bound
nodes.statement: From \Cref{ruz-dist-def},~\eqref{uauh} is equivalent to \[\bbH[U_A - U_H] \leq \log( |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}) + \tfrac{1}{2} C' \log K.\]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite (11.2) as an entropy bound

nodes.name: Concentration gives a heavy coset
nodes.statement: By \Cref{bound-conc} we conclude the existence of a point $x_0 \in \F_p^n$ such that \[p_{U_A-U_H}(x_0) \geq |A|^{-1/2} |H|^{-1/2} K^{-C'/2},\] or equivalently \[|A \cap (H + x_0)| \geq K^{-C'/2} |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Concentration gives a heavy coset

nodes.name: Ruzsa covering
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{ruz-cov}, we may thus cover $A$ by at most \[\frac{|A + (A \cap (H+x_0))|}{|A \cap (H + x_0)|} \leq \frac{K|A|}{K^{-C'/2} |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}} = K^{C'/2+1} \frac{|A|^{1/2}}{|H|^{1/2}}\] translates of \[\bigl(A \cap (H + x_0)\bigr) - \bigl(A \cap (H + x_0)\bigr) \subseteq H.\] This proves the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Ruzsa covering

nodes.name: Case |H| <= |A|
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be given by \Cref{pfr_aux}. If $|H| \leq |A|$ then we are already done thanks to~\eqref{ah}.
nodes.statement_short: Case |H| <= |A|

nodes.name: Case |H| > |A|: split H into smaller subspaces
nodes.statement: If $|H| > |A|$ then we can cover $H$ by at most $2 |H|/|A|$ translates of a subspace $H'$ of $H$ with $|H'| \leq |A|$. We can thus cover $A$ by at most \[2K^{13/2} \frac{|H|^{1/2}}{|A|^{1/2}}\] translates of $H'$, and the claim again follows from~\eqref{ah}.
nodes.statement_short: Case |H| > |A|: split H into smaller subspaces

nodes.name: WLOG X,Y independent
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality (using \Cref{ruz-copy} and \Cref{independent-exist}) we may take $X,Y$ to be independent.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG X,Y independent

nodes.name: Conditionally independent trials and a third copy
nodes.statement: By $(X_1,Y_1)$, $(X_2,Y_2)$ be copies of $(X,Y)$ that are conditionally independent over $X_1-Y_1=X_2-Y_2$ (this exists thanks to \Cref{cond-indep-exist}). By \Cref{independent-exist}, we can also find another copy $(X_3,Y_3)$ of $(X,Y)$ that is independent of $X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Conditionally independent trials and a third copy

nodes.name: Submodularity inequality
nodes.statement: From \Cref{alt-submodularity}, one has $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3, Y_3, X_3+Y_3] + \bbH[X_3+Y_3] \leq \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] + \bbH[X_3, Y_3, X_3+Y_3].$$
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity inequality

nodes.name: Entropy of X_3+Y_3
nodes.statement: From \Cref{ruz-indep}, \Cref{neg-ent}, \Cref{ruz-copy} we have $$ \bbH[X_3+Y_3] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X_3] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[-Y_3] + d[X_3;-Y_3] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[Y] + d[X;-Y].$$
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of X_3+Y_3

nodes.name: Entropy of (X_3,Y_3,X_3+Y_3)
nodes.statement: Since $X_3+Y_3$ is a function of $X_3,Y_3$, we see from \Cref{relabeled-entropy} and \Cref{add-entropy} that $$ \bbH[X_3,Y_3,X_3+Y_3] = \bbH[X_3,Y_3] = \bbH[X,Y] = \bbH[X]+\bbH[Y].$$
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of (X_3,Y_3,X_3+Y_3)

nodes.name: Relabeling and subadditivity bound
nodes.statement: Because $X_1-Y_1=X_2-Y_2$, we have $$ X_3+Y_3 = (X_3-Y_2) - (X_1-Y_3) + (X_2+Y_1)$$ and thus by \Cref{relabeled-entropy} $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] = \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1]$$ and hence by \Cref{subadditive} $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] \leq \bbH[X_3-Y_2] + \bbH[X_1-Y_3] + \bbH[X_2] + \bbH[Y_1].$$
nodes.statement_short: Relabeling and subadditivity bound

nodes.name: Entropies of X_3-Y_2 and X_1-Y_3
nodes.statement: Since $X_3,Y_2$ are independent, we see from \Cref{ruz-indep}, \Cref{ruz-copy} that $$\bbH[X_3-Y_2] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[Y] + d[X; Y].$$ Similarly $$ \bbH[X_1-Y_3] = \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2} \bbH[Y] + d[X; Y].$$
nodes.statement_short: Entropies of X_3-Y_2 and X_1-Y_3

nodes.name: Combine into a bound
nodes.statement: We conclude that $$ \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3+Y_3] \leq 2\bbH[X] + 2\bbH[Y] + 2d[X; Y].$$
nodes.statement_short: Combine into a bound

nodes.name: Data processing
nodes.statement: Finally, from \Cref{data-process-single} we have $$ \bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,X_3,Y_3] \leq \bbH[X_3-Y_2, X_1-Y_3, X_2, Y_1, X_3, Y_3, X_3+Y_3].$$
nodes.statement_short: Data processing

nodes.name: Evaluate the joint entropy of the six variables
nodes.statement: From \Cref{add-entropy} followed by \Cref{cond-trial-ent}, we have $$\bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,X_3,Y_3] = \bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_1-Y_1] + \bbH[X_2,Y_2,X_2-Y_2] - \bbH[X_1-Y_1] + \bbH[X_3,Y_3]$$ and thus by \Cref{ruz-indep}, \Cref{ruz-copy}, \Cref{relabeled-entropy}, \Cref{add-entropy} $$\bbH[X_1,Y_1,X_2,Y_2,X_3,Y_3] = \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y] + \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y] -\left(\frac{1}{2}\bbH[X] + \frac{1}{2}\bbH[Y] + d[X; Y]\right) + \bbH[X] + \bbH[Y].$$
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the joint entropy of the six variables

nodes.name: Linear arithmetic
nodes.statement: Applying all of these estimates, the claim now follows from linear arithmetic.
nodes.statement_short: Linear arithmetic

nodes.name: Base cases n=0,1,2
nodes.statement: This is trivial for $n=0,1$, while the $n=2$ case is \Cref{kv}.
nodes.statement_short: Base cases n=0,1,2

nodes.name: Inductive step via KVM and induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Now suppose inductively that $n > 2$, and the claim was already proven for $n-1$. By a further application of \Cref{kv} one has $$ \bbH\left[X + \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i\right] - \bbH\left[X + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} Y_i\right] \leq \bbH[X+Y_n] - \bbH[X].$$ By induction hypothesis one has $$ \bbH\left[X + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} Y_i\right] - \bbH[X] \leq \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} \bbH[X+Y_i] - \bbH[X].$$
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step via KVM and induction hypothesis

nodes.name: Sum the inequalities
nodes.statement: Summing the two inequalities, we obtain the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the inequalities

nodes.name: KVM with negated Y_i
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{klm-1} with all the $Y_i$ replaced by $-Y_i$, and using \Cref{neg-ent} and \Cref{ruz-indep}, we obtain after some rearranging $$ d[X; \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] + \frac{1}{2} (\bbH[\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] - \bbH[X]) \leq \sum_{i=1}^n \left(d[X;Y_i] + \frac{1}{2} (\bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X])\right).$$
nodes.statement_short: KVM with negated Y_i

nodes.name: Sumset lower bound and averaging
nodes.statement: From \Cref{sumset-lower} we have $$ \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] \geq \bbH[Y_i]$$ for all $i$; subtracting $\bbH[X]$ and averaging, we conclude that $$ \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] - \bbH[X] \geq \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X]$$ and thus $$ d[X; \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i] \leq \sum_{i=1}^n d[X;Y_i] + \frac{n-1}{2n} (\bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X]).$$
nodes.statement_short: Sumset lower bound and averaging

nodes.name: Entropy difference bound
nodes.statement: From \Cref{ruzsa-diff} we have $$ \bbH[Y_i] - \bbH[X] \leq 2 d[X;Y_i].$$
nodes.statement_short: Entropy difference bound

nodes.name: Coefficient bound
nodes.statement: Since $0 \leq \frac{n-1}{2n} \leq \frac{1}{2}$, the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Coefficient bound

nodes.name: Sumset lower bound and iterated KVM with W
nodes.statement: Write $W := \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$. From \Cref{sumset-lower} we have $$ \bbH[\sum_{j=1}^l Y_j] \leq \bbH[-W + \sum_{j=1}^l Y_j]$$ while from \Cref{klm-1} one has $$ \bbH[-W + \sum_{j=1}^l Y_j] \leq \bbH[-W] + \sum_{j=1}^l \bbH[-W + Y_j] - \bbH[-W].$$
nodes.statement_short: Sumset lower bound and iterated KVM with W

nodes.name: KVM for each term
nodes.statement: From \Cref{kv} one has $$ \bbH[-W + Y_j] - \bbH[-W] \leq \bbH[-X_{f(j)} + Y_j] - \bbH[-X_{f(j)}].$$
nodes.statement_short: KVM for each term

nodes.name: Algebra
nodes.statement: The claim now follows from \Cref{neg-ent} and some elementary algebra.
nodes.statement_short: Algebra

nodes.name: Take the X_i independent
nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruz-copy}, \Cref{multidist-copy} we may take the $X_i$ to be jointly independent.
nodes.statement_short: Take the X_i independent

nodes.name: Bound each d[X_j;-X_k]
nodes.statement: From \Cref{sumset-lower}, we see that for any distinct $1 \leq j,k \leq m$, we have \[ \bbH[X_j+X_k] \leq \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i], \] and hence by \Cref{ruz-indep} \[ d[X_j;-X_k] \leq \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i] - \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X_j] - \frac{1}{2} \bbH[X_k]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound each d[X_j;-X_k]

nodes.name: Sum over pairs
nodes.statement: Summing this over all pairs $(j,k)$, $j \neq k$ and using Lemma \ref{multidist-indep}, we obtain the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over pairs

nodes.name: Take the X_i independent
nodes.statement: By \Cref{ruz-copy}, \Cref{multidist-copy} we may take the $X_i$ to be jointly independent.
nodes.statement_short: Take the X_i independent

nodes.name: Extra copy X_0 and KVM
nodes.statement: Let $X_0$ be a further independent copy of the $X_i$. From \Cref{klm-1}, we have $$ \bbH[-X_0 + \sum_{i=1}^m X_i] - \bbH[-X_0] \leq \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_0 - X_i] - \bbH[-X_0]$$ and hence by \Cref{neg-ent} and \Cref{ruz-indep} $$ \bbH[-X_0 + \sum_{i=1}^m X_i] - \bbH[X_0] \leq m d[X_i,X_i].$$
nodes.statement_short: Extra copy X_0 and KVM

nodes.name: Sumset lower bound
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by \Cref{sumset-lower} we have $$ \bbH[\sum_{i=1}^m X_i] \leq \bbH[-X_0 + \sum_{i=1}^m X_i]$$ and the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Sumset lower bound

nodes.name: Independent copies X'_i and distinct a,b
nodes.statement: Take $(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ to be further independent copies of $(X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$ (which exist by \Cref{independent-exist}), and write $W' := \sum_{i=1}^m X'_i$. Fix any distinct $a,b \in I$.
nodes.statement_short: Independent copies X'_i and distinct a,b

nodes.name: KVM twice
nodes.statement: From \Cref{kv} one has \begin{equation} \bbH[W + W'] \leq \bbH[W] + \bbH[X_{a} + W'] - \bbH[X_{a}] \end{equation} and also \[ \bbH[X_a + W'] \leq \bbH[X_a + X_b] + \bbH[W'] - \bbH[X'_b].\]
nodes.statement_short: KVM twice

nodes.name: Combine with sumset lower bound
nodes.statement: Combining this with~\eqref{7922} and then applying \Cref{sumset-lower} we have \begin{align*} \bbH[W + W'] & \leq 2\bbH[W] + \bbH[X_a + X_b] - \bbH[X_a] - \bbH[X_b] \\ & \leq 3 \bbH[W] - \bbH[X_a] - \bbH[X_b]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Combine with sumset lower bound

nodes.name: Average over (a,b)
nodes.statement: Averaging this over all choices of $(a,b)$ gives $\bbH[W] + 2 D[X_{[m]}]$, and the claim follows from \Cref{ruz-indep}.
nodes.statement_short: Average over (a,b)

nodes.name: Minimality of tau
nodes.statement: By \Cref{tau-min-multi} we have $$ \tau[ (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \leq \tau[ (X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}]$$ and hence by \Cref{tau-def-multi} $$ k + \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X^0] \leq D[(X'_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] + \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X'_i; X^0].$$
nodes.statement_short: Minimality of tau

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} we have $$ d[X'_i; X^0] \leq d[X_i; X^0] + d[X_i; X'_i].$$ The claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality

nodes.name: Express the conditional mutual information in entropies
nodes.statement: For notational brevity during this proof, write $S := \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$. From \Cref{conditional-mutual-alt} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy}, noting that $\pi(S)$ is determined both by $S$ and by $\pi(X_{[m]})$, we have \begin{equation*} \bbI[S:\pi(X_{[m]})|\pi(S)] = \bbH[S]+\bbH[\pi(X_{[m]})]-\bbH[S,\pi(X_{[m]})]-\bbH[\pi(S)], \end{equation*} and by \Cref{chain-rule} the right-hand side is equal to \begin{equation*} \bbH[S]-\bbH[S|\pi(X_{[m]})]-\bbH[\pi(S)]. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Express the conditional mutual information in entropies

nodes.name: Rearrange to (12.6)
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{equation} \bbH[S]=\bbH[S|\pi(X_{[m]})]+\bbH[\pi(S)]+\bbI[S:\pi(X_{[m]})|\pi(S)]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange to (12.6)

nodes.name: Chain rule for each X_i (12.7)
nodes.statement: From a further application of \Cref{chain-rule} and \Cref{relabeled-entropy} we have \begin{equation} \bbH[X_i] = \bbH[X_i \, | \, \pi(X_i)] + \bbH[\pi(X_i)] \end{equation} for all $1 \leq i \leq m$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule for each X_i (12.7)

nodes.name: Average and subtract
nodes.statement: Averaging~\eqref{chain-2} in $i$ and subtracting this from~\eqref{chain-1}, we obtain the claim from \Cref{multidist-def}.
nodes.statement_short: Average and subtract

nodes.name: Define the partial-sum maps pi_d
nodes.statement: In \Cref{multidist-chain-rule-iter} we take $G_d := G^d$ with the maps $\pi_d \colon G^m \to G^d$ for $d=1,\dots,m$ defined by \[ \pi_d(x_1,\dots,x_m) := (x_1,\dots,x_{d-1}, x_d + \cdots + x_m) \] with $\pi_0=0$. Since $\pi_{d-1}(x)$ can be obtained from $\pi_{d}(x)$ by applying a homomorphism, we obtain a sequence of the form~\eqref{g-seq}.
nodes.statement_short: Define the partial-sum maps pi_d

nodes.name: Apply the iterated chain rule; independence splits D
nodes.statement: Now we apply \Cref{multidist-chain-rule-iter} with $I = \{1,\dots, m\}$ and $X_i := (X_{i,j})_{j = 1}^m$. Using joint independence and \Cref{add-entropy}, we find that \[ D[ X_{[m]} ] = \sum_{j=1}^m D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the iterated chain rule; independence splits D

nodes.name: Identify conditional terms
nodes.statement: On the other hand, for $1 \leq j \leq m-1$, we see that once $\pi_{j}(X_i)$ is fixed, $\pi_{j+1}(X_i)$ is determined by $X_{i, j}$ and vice versa, so \[ D[ \pi_{j+1}(X_{[m]}) \; | \; \pi_{j}(X_{[m]}) ] = D[ (X_{i, j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; \pi_{j}(X_{[m]} )]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Identify conditional terms

nodes.name: Simplify by independence
nodes.statement: Since the $X_{i,j}$ are jointly independent, we may further simplify: \[ D[ (X_{i, j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; \pi_{j}(X_{[m]})] = D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; ( X_{i, j} + \cdots + X_{i, m})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Simplify by independence

nodes.name: Rearrange
nodes.statement: Putting all this into the conclusion of \Cref{multidist-chain-rule-iter}, we obtain \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m} D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ] \geq \begin{aligned}[t] &\sum_{j=1}^{m-1} D[ (X_{i,j})_{1 \leq i \leq m} \; | \; (X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m})_{1 \leq i \leq m} ] \\ &\!\!\!+ D[ \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{1 \leq i \leq m}] \\ &\!\!\!+\bbI[ \bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{j =1}^{m} : \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; \sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{j = 1}^m X_{i,j} ] \end{aligned} \] and the claim follows by rearranging.
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange

nodes.name: Rows and columns
nodes.statement: For each $j \in \{1,\dots,m\}$ we call the tuple $(X_{i,j})_{i = 1}^m$ a \emph{column} and for each $i \in \{1,\dots, m\}$ we call the tuple $(X_{i,j})_{j = 1}^m$ a \emph{row}. Hence, by hypothesis, each column is a permutation of $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{i=1}^m$.
nodes.statement_short: Rows and columns

nodes.name: Chain-rule corollary splits I into A_j and B
nodes.statement: From \Cref{cor-multid} we have \begin{equation} {\mathcal I} \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} A_j + B,\end{equation} where \[ A_j := D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m] - D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m \; \big| \; (X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m})_{i =1}^m ] \] and \[ B := D[ (X_{i,m})_{i=1}^m ] - D[ \bigl(\sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}\bigr)_{i=1}^m ]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Chain-rule corollary splits I into A_j and B

nodes.name: D of each column equals k
nodes.statement: We first consider the $A_j$, for fixed $j \in \{1,\dots, m-1\}$. By \Cref{multidist-perm} and our hypothesis on columns, we have \[ D[ (X_{i, j})_{i = 1}^m ]= D[ (X_i)_{i=1}^m ] = k. \]
nodes.statement_short: D of each column equals k

nodes.name: Conditional lower bound gives (12.14)
nodes.statement: Let $\sigma = \sigma_j \colon I \to I$ be a permutation such that $X_{i,j} \equiv X_{\sigma(i)}$, and write $X'_i := X_{i,j}$ and $Y_i := X_{i,j} + \cdots + X_{i,m}$. By \Cref{cond-multidist-lower-II}, we have \begin{align} A_j & \leq \eta (\sum_{i = 1}^{m} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i, j}|X_{i, j} + \cdots + X_{i,m}]). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Conditional lower bound gives (12.14)

nodes.name: Column m has multidistance k
nodes.statement: We similarly consider $B$. By \Cref{multidist-perm} applied to the $m$-th column, \[ D[ (X_{i, m})_{i = 1}^m ] = D[X_{[m]}] = k. \]
nodes.statement_short: Column m has multidistance k

nodes.name: Row sums V_i and bound (12.15)
nodes.statement: For $1 \leq i \leq m$, denote the sum of row $i$ by \[ V_i := \sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j}; \] if we apply \Cref{cond-multidist-lower-II} again, now with $X_{\sigma(i)} = X_{i,m}$, $X'_i := V_i$, and with the variable $Y_i$ being trivial, we obtain \begin{equation} B \leq \eta \sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_{i,m}; V_i]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Row sums V_i and bound (12.15)

nodes.name: It remains to bound the distances
nodes.statement: It remains to bound the distances appearing in~\eqref{54a} and~\eqref{55a} further using Ruzsa calculus.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to bound the distances

nodes.name: First comparison lemma, summed over j
nodes.statement: For $1 \leq j \leq m-1$ and $1 \leq i \leq m$, by \Cref{first-useful} we have \begin{align*} &d[ X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}| X_{i,j}+\cdots+X_{i,m}] \leq d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}] \\ &\quad + \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\bbH[X_{i,j}+\cdots+X_{i,m}] - \bbH[X_{i,{j+1}}+\cdots+X_{i,m}]\bigr). \end{align*} For each $i$, summing over $j = 1,\dots, m-1$ gives \begin{align} \nonumber &\sum_{j=1}^{m-1} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}| X_{i,j}+\cdots+X_{i,m}] \\ &\qquad \leq \sum_{j=1}^{m-1} d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}] + \frac12 \bigl( \bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}] \bigr). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: First comparison lemma, summed over j

nodes.name: KVM III bound (12.17)
nodes.statement: On the other hand, by \Cref{klm-3} (since $X_{i,m}$ appears in the sum $V_i$) we have \begin{align} d[X_{i,m}; V_i] &\leq d[X_{i,m}; X_{i,m}] + \frac12 \bigl( \bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}] \bigr). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: KVM III bound (12.17)

nodes.name: Combine into (12.18)
nodes.statement: Combining~\eqref{441},~\eqref{54a} and~\eqref{55a} with~\eqref{eq:distbnd1} and~\eqref{eq:distbnd2} (the latter two summed over $i$), we get \begin{align} \nonumber \frac1{\eta} {\mathcal I} &\leq \sum_{i,j=1}^m d[X_{i,j};X_{i,j}] + \sum_{i=1}^m (\bbH[V_i] - \bbH[X_{i,m}]) \\ &= m \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; X_i] + \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[V_i] - \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine into (12.18)

nodes.name: Compare-sums bound on H[V_i]
nodes.statement: By \Cref{compare-sums} (with $f$ taking each $j$ to the index $j'$ such that $X_{i,j}$ is a copy of $X_{j'}$) we obtain the bound \[ \bbH[V_i] \leq \bbH[\sum_{j=1}^m X_j] + \sum_{j=1}^m d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Compare-sums bound on H[V_i]

nodes.name: Sum over i and combine
nodes.statement: Finally, summing over $i$ and using $D[X_{[m]}] = k$ gives \begin{align*} \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[V_i] - \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i] & \leq \sum_{i,j=1}^m d[X_{i,j}; X_{i,j}] + m k \\ & = m\sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_i; X_i] + mk, \end{align*} where in the second step we used the permutation hypothesis. Combining this with~\eqref{eq:distbnd3} gives the $$ {\mathcal I} \leq 2\eta m \biggl( \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i;X_i] \biggr) + mk.$$
nodes.statement_short: Sum over i and combine

nodes.name: Multidistance-Ruzsa II
nodes.statement: The claim \eqref{I-ineq} is now immediate from \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-II}.
nodes.statement_short: Multidistance-Ruzsa II

nodes.name: Three applications of the key proposition
nodes.statement: We analyze these variables by \Cref{key} in several different ways.
nodes.statement_short: Three applications of the key proposition

nodes.name: First application: X_{i,j}=Y_{i,j}
nodes.statement: In the first application, take $X_{i,j}=Y_{i,j}$. Note that each column $(X_{i,j})_{i=1}^m$ is indeed a permutation of $X_1,\dots,X_m$; in fact, the trivial permutation.
nodes.statement_short: First application: X_{i,j}=Y_{i,j}

nodes.name: Row and column sums are P_i, Q_j
nodes.statement: Note also that for each $i \in \Z/m\Z$, the row sum is \[ \sum_{j=1}^m X_{i,j} = \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} = P_i \] and for each $j \in \Z/m\Z$, the column sum is \[ \sum_{i=1}^m X_{i,j} = \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j} = Q_j. \] Finally note that $\sum_{i,j=1}^m X_{i,j} = W$.
nodes.statement_short: Row and column sums are P_i, Q_j

nodes.name: Key proposition and data processing bound I[Z_1:Z_2|W]
nodes.statement: From \Cref{key} we then have \[ \bbI[ (P_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z} : (Q_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z } \,\big|\, W ] \leq t, \] with $t$ as in~\eqref{t-def}. Since $Z_1$ is a function of $(P_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z}$ by~\eqref{pqr-defs}, and similarly $Z_2$ is a function of $(Q_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z}$, it follows immediately from \Cref{data-process} that \[ \bbI[ Z_1 : Z_2 \,|\, W ] \leq t. \]
nodes.statement_short: Key proposition and data processing bound I[Z_1:Z_2|W]

nodes.name: Second application: X'_{i,j}=Y_{i-j,j}
nodes.statement: In the second application of \Cref{key}, we instead consider $X'_{i,j} = Y_{i-j,j}$. Again, for each fixed $j$, the tuple $(X'_{i,j})_{i=1}^m$ is a permutation of $X_1,\dots,X_m$.
nodes.statement_short: Second application: X'_{i,j}=Y_{i-j,j}

nodes.name: Row sums R_{-i}, column sums Q_j
nodes.statement: This time the row sums for $i \in \{1,\dots, m\}$ are \[ \sum_{j=1}^m X'_{i,j} = \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i-j,j} = R_{-i}. \] Similarly, the column sums for $j \in \{1,\dots, m\}$ are \[ \sum_{i=1}^m X'_{i,j} = \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i-j,j} = Q_j. \] As before, $\sum_{i,j=1}^m X'_{i,j} = W$.
nodes.statement_short: Row sums R_{-i}, column sums Q_j

nodes.name: Bound I[Z_3:Z_2|W]
nodes.statement: Hence, using~\eqref{pqr-defs} and \Cref{data-process} again, \Cref{key} tells us \[ \bbI[ Z_3 : Z_2 \,|\, W] \leq \bbI[ (R_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z} : (Q_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z } \,\big|\, W ] \leq t. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound I[Z_3:Z_2|W]

nodes.name: Third application: X''_{i,j}=Y_{i,j-i}
nodes.statement: In the third application\footnote{In fact, by permuting the variables $(Y_{i,j})_{i,j \in \Z/m\Z}$, one can see that the random variables $(W, Z_1, Z_2)$ and $(W, Z_1, Z_3)$ have the same distribution, so this is in some sense identical to -- and can be deduced from -- the first application.} of \Cref{key}, take $X''_{i,j} = Y_{i,j-i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Third application: X''_{i,j}=Y_{i,j-i}

nodes.name: Bound I[Z_1:Z_3|W]
nodes.statement: The column and row sums are respectively \[ \sum_{j=1}^m X''_{i,j} = \sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j-i} = P_i \] and \[ \sum_{i=1}^m X''_{i,j} = \sum_{i \in \Z/m\Z} Y_{i,j-i} = R_{-j}. \] Hence, \Cref{key} and \Cref{data-process} give \[ \bbI[ Z_1 : Z_3 \,|\, W] \leq \bbI[ (P_i)_{i \in \Z/m\Z} : (R_j)_{j \in \Z/m\Z } \,\big|\, W ] \leq t, \] which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Bound I[Z_1:Z_3|W]

nodes.name: WLOG independent
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we may take $X_1,\dots,X_m$ to be independent.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG independent

nodes.name: S and the column sums Q_j distributed as S
nodes.statement: Write $S = \sum_{i=1}^m X_i$. Note that for each $j \in \Z/m\Z$, the sum $Q_j$ from~\eqref{pqr-defs} above has the same distribution as $S$.
nodes.statement_short: S and the column sums Q_j distributed as S

nodes.name: KVM on W
nodes.statement: By \Cref{klm-1} we have \begin{align*} \bbH[W] = \bbH[\sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} Q_j] & \leq \bbH[S] + \sum_{j=2}^m (\bbH[Q_1+Q_j] - \bbH[S]) \\ & = \bbH[S] + (m-1) d[S;-S]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: KVM on W

nodes.name: Multidistance-Ruzsa IV gives d[S;-S] <= 2k
nodes.statement: By \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-IV}, we have \begin{equation} d[S; -S] \leq 2 k \end{equation} and hence \[ \bbH[W] \leq 2 k (m-1) + \bbH[S]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Multidistance-Ruzsa IV gives d[S;-S] <= 2k

nodes.name: Entropy of S
nodes.statement: From \Cref{multidist-def} we have \begin{equation} \bbH[S] = k + \frac1m \sum_{i=1}^m \bbH[X_i], \end{equation} and the claim follows.
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of S

nodes.name: Write Z_2 via the Q_j
nodes.statement: We observe \[ \bbH[Z_2] = \bbH[\sum_{j \in \Z/m\Z} j Q_j]. \]
nodes.statement_short: Write Z_2 via the Q_j

nodes.name: KVM
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{klm-1} one has \begin{align*} \bbH[Z_2] &\leq \sum_{i=2}^{m-1} \bbH[Q_1 + i Q_i] - (m-2) \bbH[S]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: KVM

nodes.name: Sums of dilates and (12.22)
nodes.statement: Using \Cref{sum-dilate-II} and~\eqref{eq:s-bound} we get \begin{align*} \bbH[Z_2] &\leq \bbH[S] + 4m (m-2) d[S;-S] \\ &\leq \bbH[S] + 8m (m-2) k. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Sums of dilates and (12.22)

nodes.name: Apply (12.23)
nodes.statement: Applying~\eqref{eq:ent-s} gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Apply (12.23)

nodes.name: KVM III and the conditional distance bound
nodes.statement: For each $i \in \{1,\dots, m\}$, using \Cref{klm-3} (noting the sum $Z_2$ contains $X_i$ as a summand) we have \begin{equation} d[X_i;Z_2] \leq d[X_i;X_i] + \tfrac12 (\bbH[Z_2] - \bbH[X_i]) \end{equation} and using \Cref{cond-dist-fact} we have \[ d[X_i;Z_2 | W] \leq d[X_i;Z_2] + \tfrac12 \bbI[W : Z_2]. \]
nodes.statement_short: KVM III and the conditional distance bound

nodes.name: Combine with the mutual information bound
nodes.statement: Combining with~\eqref{in-a-bit-6} and \Cref{mutual-w-z2} gives \[ d[X_i;Z_2 | W] \leq d[X_i;X_i] + \tfrac12 (\bbH[Z_2] - \bbH[X_i]) + (m-1)k.\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the mutual information bound

nodes.name: Sum over i with the entropy bound on Z_2
nodes.statement: Summing over $i$ and applying \Cref{ent-z2} gives \[ \sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_i;Z_2 | W] \leq \sum_{i = 1}^m d[X_i;X_i] + m(8m^2-16m+1) k/2 + m(m-1) k.\]
nodes.statement_short: Sum over i with the entropy bound on Z_2

nodes.name: Multidistance-Ruzsa II
nodes.statement: Finally, applying \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-II} (and dropping some lower order terms) gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Multidistance-Ruzsa II

nodes.name: Entropic BSG for (T_1,T_2) gives (12.26)
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{entropic-bsg} with $X=T_1$ and $Y=T_2$. Since $T_1+T_2=-T_3$, we find that \begin{equation} \begin{split} \sum_{z} p_{T_3}(z) & d[T_1 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z;T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] \\ &\leq 3 \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + 2 \bbH[T_3] - \bbH[T_1] - \bbH[T_2] \\ &\ = \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + \bbI[T_1 : T_3] + \bbI[T_2 : T_3] = \delta, \end{split} \end{equation} where the last line follows from \Cref{relabeled-entropy} by observing \[ \bbH[T_1,T_2] = \bbH[T_1,T_3] = \bbH[T_2,T_3] = \bbH[T_1,T_2,T_3] \] since any two of $T_1,T_2,T_3$ determine the third.
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG for (T_1,T_2) gives (12.26)

nodes.name: Triangle inequality and comparison bounds
nodes.statement: By~\eqref{514a} and the triangle inequality, \[ \sum_z p_{T_3}(z) d[T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z; T_2 \,|\, T_3\mathop{=}z] \leq 2 \delta \] and by \Cref{first-useful}, for each $Y_i$, \begin{align*} &\sum_z p_{T_3}(z) d[Y_i; T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] \\ &\qquad= d[Y_i; T_2 \,|\, T_3] \leq d[Y_i;T_2] + \frac12 \bbI[T_2 : T_3] \leq d[Y_i;T_2] + \frac{\delta}{2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality and comparison bounds

nodes.name: Average and pick a good fibre
nodes.statement: Hence, \begin{align*} &\sum_z p_{T_3}(z) \bigg( d[T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z; T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i;T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z] \bigg) \\ &\qquad \leq \Bigl(2 + \frac{\alpha n}{2} \Bigr) \delta + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^n d[Y_i; T_2], \end{align*} and the result follows by setting $U=(T_2 \,|\, T_3 \mathop{=} z)$ for some $z$ such that the quantity in parentheses on the left-hand side is at most the weighted average value.
nodes.statement_short: Average and pick a good fibre

nodes.name: Apply the BSG extraction for each W=w
nodes.statement: For each value $W=w$, apply \Cref{lem:get-better} (and \Cref{Zero-sum}) to \[ T_1 = (Z_1 \,|\, W \mathop{=} w),\ T_2 = (Z_2 \,|\, W \mathop{=} w),\ T_3 = (Z_3 \,|\, W \mathop{=} w) \] with $Y_i=X_i$ and $\alpha=\eta/m$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the BSG extraction for each W=w

nodes.name: delta_w and its average bound
nodes.statement: Write \[ \delta_w := \bbI[T_1 : T_2] + \bbI[T_1 : T_3] + \bbI[T_2 : T_3] \] for this choice, and note that \begin{align} \nonumber \delta_\ast := \sum_w p_W(w) \delta_w &= \bbI[Z_1 : Z_2 \,|\, W] + \bbI[Z_1 : Z_3 \,|\, W] + \bbI[Z_2 : Z_3 \,|\, W] \\ & \leq 3 m (4m+1) \eta k \end{align} by \Cref{prop:52}.
nodes.statement_short: delta_w and its average bound

nodes.name: Variable U_w with bound (12.28)
nodes.statement: Write $U_w$ for the random variable guaranteed to exist by \Cref{lem:get-better}, so that~\eqref{eq:get-better} gives \begin{equation} d[U_w; U_w] \leq \Bigl( 2 + \frac{\alpha m}{2} \Bigr) \delta_w + \alpha \sum_{i=1}^m \bigl( d[X_i; T_2] - d[X_i; U_w] \bigr). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Variable U_w with bound (12.28)

nodes.name: Repeated tuple and Multidistance-Ruzsa III
nodes.statement: Let $(U_w)_I$ denote the tuple consisting of the same variable $U_w$ repeated $m$ times. By \Cref{multidist-ruzsa-III} \begin{equation} D[(U_w)_I] \leq m d[U_w; U_w]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Repeated tuple and Multidistance-Ruzsa III

nodes.name: Multidistance lower bound
nodes.statement: On the other hand, from \Cref{multidist-lower} one has \begin{equation} D[(U_w)_I] \geq k - \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i;U_w]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Multidistance lower bound

nodes.name: Combine and average over w
nodes.statement: Combining~\eqref{eq:uw1},~\eqref{eq:uw2} and~\eqref{eq:uw3} and averaging over $w$ (with weight $p_W(w)$), and recalling the value $\alpha=\eta/m$, gives \[ m \Bigl( 2 + \frac{\eta}{2} \Bigr) \delta_\ast + \eta \sum_{i=1}^m d[X_i; Z_2 | W] \geq k \] since the terms $d[X_i; U_w]$ cancel by our choice of $\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine and average over w

nodes.name: Substitute distance and mutual information bounds
nodes.statement: Substituting in \Cref{xi-z2-w-dist} and~\eqref{eq:delta-w}, and using the fact that $2 + \frac{\eta}{2} < 3$, we have \[ 3 m^2 (4m+1) (2+\frac{\eta}{2}) \eta k + \eta 8(m^3-m^2) k \geq k. \]
nodes.statement_short: Substitute distance and mutual information bounds

nodes.name: Choice of eta forces k=0
nodes.statement: From \Cref{eta-def-multi} we have we have $$ 3 m^2 (4m+1) (2+\frac{\eta}{2}) \eta + \eta 8(m^3-m^2) < 1$$ and hence $k \leq 0$. The claim now follows from \Cref{multidist-nonneg}.
nodes.statement_short: Choice of eta forces k=0

nodes.name: Take a tau-minimizer with reference X
nodes.statement: Set $X^0 := X$. By \Cref{tau-min-exist-multi}, there exists a $\tau$-minimizer $X_{[m]} = (X_i)_{1 \leq i \leq m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a tau-minimizer with reference X

nodes.name: Zero multidistance
nodes.statement: By \Cref{k-vanish}, we have $D[X_{[m]}]=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Zero multidistance

nodes.name: Pigeonhole on reference distances
nodes.statement: By \Cref{tau-ref} and the pigeonhole principle, there exists $1 \leq i \leq m$ such that $d[X_i; X] \leq \frac{2}{\eta} d[X;X]$.
nodes.statement_short: Pigeonhole on reference distances

nodes.name: Vanishing proposition and triangle inequality
nodes.statement: By \Cref{multi-zero}, we have $d[X_i;U_H]=0$ for some subgroup $H \leq G$, hence by \Cref{ruzsa-triangle} we have $d[U_H; X] \leq \frac{2}{\eta} d[X;X]$.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing proposition and triangle inequality

nodes.name: Value of eta
nodes.statement: The claim then follows from \Cref{eta-def-multi}.
nodes.statement_short: Value of eta

nodes.name: Independent copies Y_1,Y_2 and a joint entropy identity
nodes.statement: Let $Y_1,Y_2$ be independent copies of $Y$ (also independent of $X$). Since $G$ is torsion-free we know $X,Y_1-Y_2,X-2Y_1$ uniquely determine $X,Y_1,Y_2$ and so \[\mathbb{H}(X,Y_1,Y_2,X-2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(X,Y_1,Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(X)+2\mathbb{H}(Y).\]
nodes.statement_short: Independent copies Y_1,Y_2 and a joint entropy identity

nodes.name: H(X,X-2Y_1)
nodes.statement: Similarly \[\mathbb{H}(X,X-2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y).\]

nodes.name: Subadditivity bound
nodes.statement: Furthermore \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2,X-2Y_1)=\mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2).\]
nodes.statement_short: Subadditivity bound

nodes.name: Submodularity, combined
nodes.statement: By submodularity (\Cref{alt-submodularity}) \[\mathbb{H}(X,Y_1,Y_2,X-2Y_1)+\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)\leq \mathbb{H}(X,X-2Y_1)+\mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2,X-2Y_1).\] Combining these inequalities \[\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2)-\mathbb{H}(Y).\]
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity, combined

nodes.name: Second submodularity
nodes.statement: Similarly we have \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1,Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(X)+2\mathbb{H}(Y),\] \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1,X-Y_1-Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(Y)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_2),\] and \[\mathbb{H}(Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)=\mathbb{H}(Y)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1)\] and by submodularity (\Cref{alt-submodularity}) again \[\mathbb{H}(Y_1,Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2)+ \mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1,X-Y_1-Y_2)+\mathbb{H}(Y_2,X-Y_1-Y_2).\]
nodes.statement_short: Second submodularity

nodes.name: Bound H(X-Y_1-Y_2)
nodes.statement: Combining these inequalities (and recalling the definition of Ruzsa distance) gives \[\mathbb{H}(X-Y_1-Y_2)\leq \mathbb{H}(X-Y_1)+\mathbb{H}(X-Y_2)-\mathbb{H}(X)=2d[X;Y]+\mathbb{H}(Y).\]
nodes.statement_short: Bound H(X-Y_1-Y_2)

nodes.name: Bound d[X;2Y]
nodes.statement: It follows that \[\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+2d[X;Y]\] and so (using $\mathbb{H}(2Y)=\mathbb{H}(Y)$) \begin{align*} d[X;2Y] &=\mathbb{H}(X-2Y_1)-\mathbb{H}(X)/2-\mathbb{H}(2Y)/2\\ &\leq \mathbb{H}(Y_1-Y_2)+2d[X;Y]-\mathbb{H}(X)/2-\mathbb{H}(Y)/2\\ &= d[Y_1;Y_2]+\frac{\mathbb{H}(Y)-\mathbb{H}(X)}{2}+2d[X;Y]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound d[X;2Y]

nodes.name: Triangle inequality for d[Y_1;Y_2]
nodes.statement: Finally note that by the triangle inequality (\Cref{ruzsa-triangle}) we have \[d[Y_1;Y_2]\leq d[Y_1;X]+d[X;Y_2]=2d[X;Y].\]
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality for d[Y_1;Y_2]

nodes.name: Entropy difference bound
nodes.statement: The result follows from $(\mathbb{H}(Y)-\mathbb{H}(X))/2\leq d[X;Y]$ (\Cref{ruzsa-diff}).
nodes.statement_short: Entropy difference bound

nodes.name: Improved entropic PFR gives H
nodes.statement: By \Cref{entropy-pfr-improv} there exists a subgroup $H$ such that $d[X;U_H] + d[Y;U_H] \leq 10 d[X;Y]$.
nodes.statement_short: Improved entropic PFR gives H

nodes.name: Projection entropy bound gives the second claim
nodes.statement: Using \Cref{dist-projection} we deduce that $\mathbb{H}(\psi(X)) + \mathbb{H}(\psi(X)) \leq 20 d[X;Y]$. The second claim follows adding these inequalities and using the assumption on $\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Projection entropy bound gives the second claim

nodes.name: Bound log|H|
nodes.statement: Furthermore we have by \Cref{ruzsa-diff} \[\log \lvert H \rvert-\mathbb{H}(X)\leq 2d[X;U_H]\] and similarly for $Y$ and thus \begin{align*} \log \lvert H\rvert &\leq \frac{\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)}{2}+d[X;U_H] + d[Y;U_H] \leq \frac{\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)}{2}+ 10d[X;Y] \\& < \frac{1+\alpha}{2}(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound log|H|

nodes.name: H nontrivial by nonnegativity
nodes.statement: Finally note that if $H$ were trivial then $\psi(X)=X$ and $\psi(Y)=Y$ and hence $\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)=0$, which contradicts \Cref{ruzsa-nonneg}.
nodes.statement_short: H nontrivial by nonnegativity

nodes.name: Choose a maximal subgroup H
nodes.statement: Let $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ be a maximal subgroup such that \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))> \frac{20}{\alpha} d[\psi(X);\psi(Y)]\] and such that there exists $c \ge 0$ with \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq \frac{1+\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)}(1-c)(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\leq c (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)).\] Note that this exists since $H=\{0\}$ is an example of such a subgroup or we are done with this choice of $H$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a maximal subgroup H

nodes.name: Projection lemma in G/H gives H'
nodes.statement: We know that $G/H$ is a $2$-elementary group and so by Lemma \ref{app-ent-pfr} there exists some non-trivial subgroup $H'\leq G/H$ such that \[\log \lvert H'\rvert < \frac{1+\alpha}{2}(\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi' \circ\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi' \circ \psi(Y))< \alpha(\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y)))\] where $\psi':G/H\to (G/H)/H'$.
nodes.statement_short: Projection lemma in G/H gives H'

nodes.name: Lift H' to H'' properly containing H
nodes.statement: By group isomorphism theorems we know that there exists some $H''$ with $H\leq H''\leq G$ such that $H'\cong H''/H$ and $\psi' \circ \psi(X)=\psi''(X)$ where $\psi'':G\to G/H''$ is the projection homomorphism. Since $H'$ is non-trivial we know that $H$ is a proper subgroup of $H''$.
nodes.statement_short: Lift H' to H'' properly containing H

nodes.name: Bounds for H''
nodes.statement: On the other hand we know that \[\log \lvert H''\rvert=\log \lvert H'\rvert+\log \lvert H\rvert< \frac{1+\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)}(1-\alpha c)(\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y))\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\psi''(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi''(Y))< \alpha (\mathbb{H}(\psi(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi(Y)))\leq \alpha c (\mathbb{H}(X)+\mathbb{H}(Y)).\]
nodes.statement_short: Bounds for H''

nodes.name: Maximality forces the conclusion
nodes.statement: Therefore (using the maximality of $H$) it must be the first condition that fails, whence \[\mathbb{H}(\psi''(X))+\mathbb{H}(\psi''(Y))\leq \frac{20}{\alpha}d[\psi''(X);\psi''(Y)].\]
nodes.statement_short: Maximality forces the conclusion

nodes.name: Conditioned uniform variables are uniform on fibres
nodes.statement: The random variables $(U_A\mid \phi(U_A)=x)$ and $(U_B\mid \phi(U_B)=y)$ are equal in distribution to $U_{A_x}$ and $U_{B_y}$ respectively (both are uniformly distributed over their respective fibres).
nodes.statement_short: Conditioned uniform variables are uniform on fibres

nodes.name: Fibring identity
nodes.statement: It follows from \Cref{fibring-ident} that \begin{align*} \sum_{x,y\in H}\frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}] &=d[U_A\mid \phi(U_A); U_B\mid \phi(U_B)]\\ &\leq d[U_A;U_B]-d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity

nodes.name: Multiply by M
nodes.statement: Therefore with $M:=\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_A))+\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_B))$ we have \[\left(\sum_{x,y\in H}\frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}Md[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]\right)+Md[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\leq Md[U_A;U_B].\]
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by M

nodes.name: Expand M as an average
nodes.statement: Since \[M=\sum_{x,y\in H}\frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\] we have \[\sum_{x,y\in H} \frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}\left(Md[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]+d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\right)\leq Md[U_A;U_B].\]
nodes.statement_short: Expand M as an average

nodes.name: Pick a good pair of fibres
nodes.statement: It follows that there exists some $x,y\in H$ such that $\lvert A_x\rvert,\lvert B_y\rvert\neq 0$ and \[Md[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]+d[\phi(U_A);\phi(U_B)]\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\leq Md[U_A;U_B].\]
nodes.statement_short: Pick a good pair of fibres

nodes.name: WLOG non-degenerate; induct on |A|+|B|
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality we can assume that $A$ and $B$ are not both inside (possibly distinct) cosets of the same subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, or we just replace $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with that subgroup. We prove the result by induction on $\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG non-degenerate; induct on |A|+|B|

nodes.name: Mod-2 projection has small entropy
nodes.statement: Let $\phi:\mathbb{Z}^d\to \mathbb{F}_2^d$ be the natural mod-2 homomorphism. By \Cref{torsion-dist-shrinking} \[\max(\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_A)),\mathbb{H}(\phi(U_B)))\leq 10d[U_A;U_B].\]
nodes.statement_short: Mod-2 projection has small entropy

nodes.name: Projection lemma gives H
nodes.statement: We now apply \Cref{pfr-projection}, obtaining some subgroup $H\leq \mathbb{F}_2^d$ such that \[\log \lvert H\rvert \leq 40d[U_A;U_B]\] and \[\mathbb{H}(\tilde{\phi}(U_A))+\mathbb{H}(\tilde{\phi}(U_B))\leq 34 d[\tilde{\phi}(U_A);\tilde{\phi}(U_B)]\] where $\tilde{\phi}:\mathbb{Z}^d\to \mathbb{F}_2^d/H$ is $\phi$ composed with the projection onto $\mathbb{F}_2^d/H$.
nodes.statement_short: Projection lemma gives H

nodes.name: Single fibres lemma
nodes.statement: By \Cref{single-fibres} there exist $x,y\in \mathbb{F}_2^d/H$ such that, with $A_x=A\cap \tilde{\phi}^{-1}(x)$ and similarly for $B_y$, \[\log \frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}\leq 34(d[U_A;U_B]-d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]).\]
nodes.statement_short: Single fibres lemma

nodes.name: Case: fibres are everything
nodes.statement: Suppose first that $\lvert A_x\rvert+\lvert B_y\rvert=\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert$. This means that $\tilde{\phi}(A)=\{x\}$ and $\tilde{\phi}(B)=\{y\}$, and hence both $A$ and $B$ are in cosets of $\ker \tilde{\phi}$. Since by assumption $A,B$ are not in cosets of a proper subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ this means $\ker\tilde{\phi}=\mathbb{Z}^d$, and so (examining the definition of $\tilde{\phi}$) we must have $H=\mathbb{F}_2^d$. Then our bound on $\log\lvert H\rvert$ forces $d\leq \frac{40}{\log 2}d[U_A;U_B]$ and we are done with $A'=A$ and $B'=B$.
nodes.statement_short: Case: fibres are everything

nodes.name: Case: smaller fibres, induction
nodes.statement: Otherwise, \[\lvert A_x\rvert+\lvert B_y\rvert <\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert.\] By induction we can find some $A'\subseteq A_x$ and $B'\subseteq B_y$ such that $\dim A',\dim B'\leq \frac{40}{\log 2} d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}]\leq \frac{40}{\log 2}d[U_A;U_B]$ and \[\log \frac{\lvert A_x\rvert\lvert B_y\rvert}{\lvert A'\rvert\lvert B'\rvert}\leq 34d[U_{A_x};U_{B_y}].\] Adding these inequalities implies \[\log\frac{\lvert A\rvert\lvert B\rvert}{\lvert A'\rvert\lvert B'\rvert}\leq 34d[U_A;U_B]\] as required.
nodes.statement_short: Case: smaller fibres, induction
